wat-pho.name: Wat Pho
wat-pho.type: A royal temple known for its Reclining Buddha and traditional medicine
wat-pho.title: Wat Pho in Bangkok: Reclining Buddha, Temple Grounds and Visitor Guide | ThaiLiveNow
wat-pho.description: Wat Pho, just south of Bangkok’s Grand Palace, is home to a 46-metre-long Reclining Buddha with mother-of-pearl inlay on its feet. Visit the Buddha hall, then explore the temple’s chedis, halls and other details across the grounds.
intro: Up close, the Reclining Buddha’s 46-metre golden figure stretches across the hall. Look down to its feet to see 108 patterns inlaid with mother-of-pearl, a fine detail alongside the statue’s immense scale. Wat Pho is a royal temple just south of Bangkok’s Grand Palace.

After seeing the Reclining Buddha, walk among the four royal chedis, each a different colour, and along the galleries lined with Buddha images. You can also look for Chinese-style stone figures and inscriptions preserving knowledge of medicine and language. If you are interested in Thai massage, learn about the traditional knowledge associated with the temple; massage is a separate paid service you can choose after your visit.

experiences.title: The patterns on the Reclining Buddha’s feet
paragraphs: Built during the reign of Rama III, the Reclining Buddha measures 46 metres long and 15 metres high. Take your time following the figure from its face along its outstretched body to its feet. The soles are decorated with 108 patterns in mother-of-pearl made from shaped shell, bringing delicate craftsmanship to this monumental statue.

After taking in the golden figure, look closely at the mother-of-pearl on the soles. Small designs reflecting Buddhist cosmology form a dense pattern. The Reclining Buddha is enshrined inside a hall, so enter the designated viewing area to see the statue and its decorated feet.

experiences.title: Four royal chedis in different colours
paragraphs: The four large chedis inside the white walls are associated with Kings Rama I through Rama IV. Green, white, yellow and deep blue mosaics give each tower its own appearance. Follow the colours to tell apart the chedis that may look similar at first.

The green chedi houses a damaged Phra Si Sanphet Buddha image brought from the royal palace in Ayutthaya. After Ayutthaya fell, the surviving image was moved to Bangkok and enshrined here. A Buddha image once kept at Ayutthaya’s former royal temple remains at Wat Pho today.

experiences.title: Galleries of Buddha images and Chinese-style stone figures
paragraphs: The double galleries around the main hall contain Buddha images brought from northern Thailand. Even among images seated in similar poses, the faces and bodies differ. If you are interested in Buddhist art, compare their features as you walk.

Some Chinese-style stone figures on the grounds came from stone ballast carried on old Chinese trading ships to balance their loads. As you leave the Reclining Buddha hall, look along the paths for armed guardians, figures in long robes and animal sculptures. Their expressions and clothing offer a contrast with the golden Buddha images.

experiences.title: Knowledge inscribed at the temple and traditional massage
paragraphs: King Rama III had knowledge from several fields inscribed around the temple so people could learn from it. This is why Wat Pho is often described as Thailand’s first university. The temple served not only as a place of worship, but also as a place for sharing knowledge, including medicine and language.

Traditional massage is also available, but **massage is not included in the temple admission ticket.** If you would like a massage after your visit, choose a service and pay separately. It can be a way to rest after taking time to explore the halls and galleries.

rules.title: Arrive before last admission
paragraphs: The temple closes at 20:00, but **new visitors are admitted only until 19:30**. If you are visiting in the evening, do not plan your arrival around closing time.

rules.title: Massage is separate from temple admission
paragraphs: The massage pavilion accepts visitors **in person without advance reservations**. If you would like a massage after your visit, plan your route so you arrive **before the 18:00 registration cutoff**. Massage fees are not included in the temple admission ticket.

rules.title: Women cannot enter in shorts above the knee
paragraphs: Wat Pho **restricts women from entering in shorts that end above the knee**. Visitors of all genders are advised to cover their shoulders and knees. Wear a top with sleeves and long trousers or a skirt that covers the knees.

rules.title: Remove your shoes before entering worship halls
paragraphs: Before entering a religious building, **remove your shoes and place them on the designated rack.** Check the signs and shoe racks at the entrances to shrines and halls, and follow posted directions elsewhere on the grounds.

rules.title: Some areas for monks’ ceremonies are restricted
paragraphs: **Women may not enter areas specifically set aside for monks to perform ceremonies.** This does not restrict women from visiting the temple as a whole. Follow area-specific signs and staff directions around the grounds.

accessSections.title: Arrive by MRT or from a pier
paragraphs: From **Sanam Chai Station on the MRT Blue Line**, it is about a five-minute walk to the temple. If you are travelling by boat, you can reach the temple from Tha Tien Pier.

faq: Does the Wat Pho admission ticket include a massage?
No. Temple admission and massage are charged separately. After visiting the Reclining Buddha and the temple grounds, you can choose a massage type and duration on site and pay its fee separately.

wat-arun.name: Wat Arun
wat-arun.thai: วัดอรุณราชวรารามราชวรมหาวิหาร
wat-arun.title: Wat Arun Bangkok: Temple, Riverside Views and Visitor Guide | ThaiLiveNow
wat-arun.description: Wat Arun, also called the Temple of Dawn, stands on the west bank of Bangkok’s Chao Phraya River. Admire its tall prang from the river, then look closely at the ceramic fragments and decorative details across the temple grounds.
intro: When the bright prang comes into view from a boat crossing the Chao Phraya River, you are nearing Wat Arun. Known as the Temple of Dawn, it stands on the west side of Bangkok. From the riverbank you can take in the tower’s outline; once inside the grounds, you can see ceramic fragments and small figures that are hard to make out from a distance.

After looking around the smaller towers surrounding the central prang and the guardians at the entrance, visit the Buddha image and murals inside the main hall. If you are crossing by boat from Wat Pho, you can see the full tower from the river and then examine its ceramic details and sculptures up close.
facts: About **1–2 hours** · An estimate for planning; actual time varies with sightseeing, photography and rest breaks.

experiences.title: The central prang and its ceramic details
paragraphs: At the heart of Wat Arun is a tall tower called a prang. From across the river, its rising outline stands out first; up close, you can see the ceramic pieces covering its surface and decorations arranged like flowers. Look closely to see how the bright exterior is made from many small fragments.

Four smaller prangs stand around the central tower. Rather than photographing only the largest one, take a moment to notice the decoration and rooflines among the smaller towers too. Some stairs on the prang are high and steep, so **use only sections open to visitors on the day**.

experiences.title: The name “Temple of Dawn” and its royal history
paragraphs: The temple’s name comes from Aruna, a Hindu deity associated with dawn. The site dates to the Ayutthaya period, and the halls and towers you see today reflect later additions and repairs by successive dynasties. This is a long-standing place of religious worship, not simply a riverside lookout.

The Emerald Buddha was once enshrined at Wat Arun. After the dynasty changed, it was moved across the river to Wat Phra Kaew in Bangkok. If you visit both Wat Arun and the Grand Palace, you can follow the history of the same image being enshrined at temples on either side of the river.

experiences.title: Guardian figures, the Buddha image and main-hall murals
paragraphs: Two yaksha guardian figures stand at the temple entrance. They are larger sculptures, quite different from the smaller decorations on the prang, and worth a look before you walk straight toward the tower.

The main hall, called the ubosot, contains a Buddha image and murals. After seeing the ceramic decoration outside, step into the hall to look at the paintings. **Remove your shoes before entering the main hall**, and move quietly without blocking people who are praying.

experiences.title: Riverside scenery from the boat
paragraphs: You can cross the river by boat from Tha Tien Pier on the Wat Pho side, or take a boat service that stops at Wat Arun Pier. From the boat, look out at the riverside temples and towers; after you arrive, walk closer to the prang to see its decoration. Boat fares and temple admission are separate.

November through February is a relatively cooler time in Bangkok. If you find the heat tiring, visit the grounds in the morning and plan to rest indoors around midday. Near sunset, you can also admire the tower’s silhouette from across the river. Allow about 1–2 hours for the visit, including photos and rest; this is a planning estimate.

experiences.title: The temple from across the river and its night lighting
paragraphs: **Nagaraphirom Park** is a public riverside park opposite Wat Arun. You can view the whole prang from the park without paying for a seat at a restaurant or rooftop venue. After seeing the ceramic decoration up close inside the temple, you may also want to take in the river and tower from here. Check whether the park is open before you go and follow on-site access instructions.

The Tourism Authority of Thailand’s **2024 night-view guide** lists the main prang’s lighting hours as **18:00 to 06:00 the next day**. The schedule may change with local conditions. In daylight, the bright ceramic decoration catches your eye; after the lights come on, the tower’s outline rises above the dark river. These hours describe exterior lighting and **are different from the hours when visitors may enter the temple grounds.**

rules.title: Watch your step on the prang stairs
paragraphs: Some stairs on the prang are high, steep or narrow. **Use only sections open to visitors on the day**, and do not climb on or damage the decorations.

rules.title: Cover your shoulders and knees; remove shoes in the main hall
paragraphs: **Clothing that covers your shoulders and knees is required.** Remove your shoes before entering the main hall (ubosot). If you are visiting with a wheelchair or stroller, contact the temple office in advance to ask which entrance and areas are accessible in practice.

rules.title: Recommended clothing for visiting the temple
paragraphs: Visitors of all genders are advised to wear **clothing that covers the shoulders and knees**. A sleeved top with long trousers or a skirt that covers the knees is a practical choice. Please dress modestly rather than wearing a sleeveless top or short bottoms.

accessSections.title: Walk from Itsaraphap Station
paragraphs: **Itsaraphap Station on the MRT Blue Line** is on the same side of the river as Wat Arun. If you want to reach the temple without crossing the river, check the actual walking route from the station.

accessSections.title: Use Wat Arun Pier or the Tha Tien cross-river ferry
paragraphs: From Sathorn Pier, choose a route that stops at Wat Arun Pier. The stop lists differ between regular express boats and tourist boats.

At Tha Tien Pier, on the Wat Pho side, you can take a cross-river ferry. This is a different service from boats travelling along the river, so when buying a ticket, ask for **the boat crossing to Wat Arun**.

faq: How much is admission?
Admission is 200 baht for international visitors; Thai visitors are listed as entering free. Check the ticket booth for the fare on the day of your visit.
What are the opening hours?
The temple is open daily from 08:00 to 18:00. If you arrive late in the afternoon, leave enough time to explore before closing.
What should I wear?
Wear clothing that covers your shoulders and knees. Remove your shoes before entering the main hall.
How do I get there?

You can walk from Itsaraphap Station on the MRT Blue Line. If travelling by boat, choose a route that stops at Wat Arun Pier. If you are already near Wat Pho, you can take the cross-river ferry from Tha Tien Pier.
Can I see the temple from outside without entering?
Yes. You can view the tower from the riverbank across the river. You need an admission ticket to explore the grounds; follow on-site directions for access to the tower viewing area.
How long should I plan for a visit?
Allow about 1–2 hours, including time for photos and a rest. This is a planning estimate, not a set visit duration; the time you spend taking photos and resting will affect your visit.
Are Wat Arun and Wat Pho the same place?

No. They are separate temples on opposite banks of the Chao Phraya River. Wat Arun, with its prang, is on the west bank; Wat Pho, known for its Reclining Buddha, is on the east bank. Each requires its own admission ticket.

wat-phra-kaew.name: Wat Phra Kaew
wat-phra-kaew.thai: วัดพระศรีรัตนศาสดาราม
wat-phra-kaew.type: Royal temple within the Grand Palace complex
wat-phra-kaew.title: Wat Phra Kaew: Emerald Buddha and Grand Palace Visitor Guide | ThaiLiveNow
wat-phra-kaew.description: Wat Phra Kaew, inside Bangkok’s Grand Palace, is the royal temple that enshrines the Emerald Buddha. Explore the temple halls and palace architecture with one ticket; you do not need to find it as a separate temple or buy a second ticket.
intro: Wat Phra Kaew is the royal temple inside Bangkok’s Grand Palace where the Emerald Buddha is enshrined. The grounds bring together sights of very different scale and style, from the small image on its high altar to golden chedis, monumental guardians and gallery murals that tell a connected story.

Admission to Wat Phra Kaew is included with the Grand Palace ticket, so you do not need a separate temple ticket. Along with the Emerald Buddha, explore the Ramakien murals in the galleries and the decoration outside the halls for a closer look at Thai royal art and Buddhist architecture.
facts: **500 baht for international visitors** · Includes Wat Phra Kaew and the Queen Sirikit Museum of Textiles
Available from one month before your visit

experiences.title: The Emerald Buddha on a high altar
paragraphs: The Emerald Buddha sits in a meditative pose high on a golden wooden altar. The Grand Palace lists its height as 66 cm, including its base. It is small compared with the surrounding buildings, yet it is one of Thailand’s most deeply revered images.

The image has three sets of seasonal garments for the hot, rainy and cool seasons. On appointed lunar-calendar dates, the King performs a ceremony to change the garments. Made with gold and jewels, the robes also show the changing work of royal artisans through the seasons.

experiences.title: The Ramakien story across the gallery
paragraphs: The galleries surrounding the temple buildings show 178 scenes from the Ramakien, Thailand’s national epic. The story of Prince Rama rescuing Sida unfolds through scenes of gods, people, monkeys and giants, with palaces and forests along the way.

The murals show more than grand battles: everyday life inside and outside the palace appears alongside animals. Even if you do not know the full story, take time to look at the figures’ poses and clothing, and the buildings and forests. It is a rewarding stop for anyone travelling with an interest in art.

experiences.title: Six pairs of giants and a golden chedi
paragraphs: The giant guardians at the doors represent characters from the Ramakien. Six pairs face the main hall as a sign of reverence toward the Emerald Buddha, according to the Grand Palace. Compare their different colours, faces and headdresses.

The bell-shaped Phra Si Rattana Chedi was built during the reign of Rama IV to enshrine a Buddha relic. It was originally white, then covered in gold-coloured mosaics imported from Italy during the reign of Rama V. Look closely at the mosaic surface as you walk around the chedi.

experiences.title: Visit the temple as part of a Grand Palace itinerary
paragraphs: The 500-baht Grand Palace ticket for international visitors includes Wat Phra Kaew and the Queen Sirikit Museum of Textiles. You can continue from the temple to the palace buildings and textile museum, but admission does not grant unrestricted access to the interior of every building.

Royal ceremonies and worship still take place here. **Dress according to the Grand Palace clothing rules**, and follow on-site instructions in areas restricted for events or other reasons. To avoid confusion with temples of the same name elsewhere, navigate to Wat Phra Kaew inside Bangkok’s Grand Palace.

rules.title: Sleeveless tops and short bottoms are not allowed
paragraphs: Entry is restricted for clothing such as **sleeveless tops, short tops, see-through clothing, shorts and miniskirts**. Torn or tight-fitting trousers and pyjamas are also prohibited. Wear long bottoms and a top that covers your shoulders.

rules.title: Online tickets cannot be changed or refunded
paragraphs: **Online tickets cannot be refunded or changed to another date or time.** Buy after your travel plans are set, and double-check your visit date before paying.

rules.title: Visitor entrance and day-of restrictions
paragraphs: Since 2024, the operator has listed **Mani Noppharat Gate** as the visitor entrance. On days with royal events or temporary restrictions, follow the entrance instructions for that day. Drone flights over the Grand Palace are prohibited.

rules.title: Recommended clothing for visiting the temple
paragraphs: Visitors of all genders are advised to wear **clothing that covers the shoulders and knees**. A sleeved top with long trousers or a skirt that covers the knees is a practical choice. Please dress modestly rather than wearing a sleeveless top or short bottoms.

rules.title: Audio guides are rented separately
paragraphs: A personal audio guide is available to rent for **200 baht**, separately from the Grand Palace ticket. It is offered in eight languages: English, French, German, Japanese, Mandarin Chinese, Russian, Spanish and Thai; Korean is not available. You must leave a passport or an Amex, Mastercard or Visa credit card as a deposit. Ask the rental desk about availability and deposit requirements on the day.

accessSections.title: Navigate to the Grand Palace
paragraphs: Search for **The Grand Palace** or Wat Phra Kaew in Google Maps. Access by boat via Tha Chang Pier is listed. Wat Phra Kaew is inside the Grand Palace complex, so enter through the visitor entrance.

faq: Do I need to buy a separate ticket for Wat Phra Kaew?
No. Wat Phra Kaew is included in the 500-baht Grand Palace ticket for international visitors. The same ticket also includes the Queen Sirikit Museum of Textiles.

wat-saket.name: Wat Saket and the Golden Mount
wat-saket.english: Wat Saket and the Golden Mount
wat-saket.type: Golden Mount chedi and old-city viewpoint temple
wat-saket.title: Wat Saket and the Golden Mount: Bangkok Temple and Viewpoint | ThaiLiveNow
wat-saket.description: Wat Saket is known for the Golden Mount in Bangkok’s old city. Climb the steps up the man-made hill to the golden chedi and look out over the low rooftops and city streets.
intro: The Golden Mount is the gilded chedi rising above the rooftops of Bangkok’s old city. Climb the steps up the man-made hill to see worshippers near the chedi and take in the surrounding city from above.

Reaching the Golden Mount means climbing up and back down a flight of steps. If someone in your group may find stairs difficult, first check whether a visit to the summit will work for them. On a day when you can make the climb comfortably, take your time: you can see the worshippers beside the golden chedi and look out over the old city’s rooftops and roads.

experiences.title: The Golden Mount above the old city
paragraphs: The Golden Mount is a man-made hill built to support a chedi, not a natural mountain. Its Thai name, Phu Khao Thong, means “Golden Mountain.” Follow the steps uphill to reach the golden chedi, then look out over the old city from beside it.
The hill was completed during the reign of Rama V, and the chedi at the top enshrines a Buddha relic. This is more than a viewpoint: you will also see people worshipping around the chedi.

experiences.title: Royal history in the name Wat Saket
paragraphs: The temple dates to the Ayutthaya period and was originally called Wat Sakae. Its name was changed to Wat Saket in 1782, at the beginning of the Bangkok dynasty. The temple was already here before the Golden Mount was completed during the reign of Rama V.

The word “saket” relates to a royal expression for grooming the King’s hair. A story says that Chao Phraya Chakri, who later became Rama I, prepared for his coronation here. The name preserves a memory of the old city and the period when the dynasty began.

experiences.title: Bangkok views along the stairs
paragraphs: From higher up, the old city and the wider Bangkok streets spread out in several directions. Unlike a view through the glass of a high-rise, you look across the city’s rooftops and roads from beside a temple chedi. It is a good stop if you would like to photograph architecture and city scenery together.

You will need to walk back down the same steps you climbed. Take your time and rest along the way in hot weather. Follow the open stairs and on-site route, and avoid blocking the path of people praying near the chedi.

rules.title: Plan for the steps before you set out
paragraphs: Visiting the Golden Mount means **climbing the steps and walking back down again**. Allow enough time for the round trip as well as your time at the viewpoint.

rules.title: Recommended clothing for visiting the temple
paragraphs: Visitors of all genders are advised to wear **clothing that covers the shoulders and knees**. A sleeved top with long trousers or a skirt that covers the knees is a practical choice. Please dress modestly rather than wearing a sleeveless top or short bottoms.

accessSections.title: Get there from Sam Yot MRT Station
paragraphs: The Golden Mount is listed as about a 15-minute walk from **Sam Yot Station on the MRT Blue Line**. Search for Wat Saket or Golden Mount as your destination.

wat-phra-that-doi-suthep.title: Wat Phra That Doi Suthep: Chiang Mai Temple and Viewpoint | ThaiLiveNow
wat-phra-that-doi-suthep.description: Wat Phra That Doi Suthep sits on Doi Suthep mountain west of Chiang Mai. Visit the golden chedi, climb the naga-lined staircase and look out over the city from the terrace.
intro: After following the mountain road west of Chiang Mai, you reach Doi Suthep Temple and its long staircase guarded by naga figures. From the terrace above, the city spreads out below, bringing together a northern Thai place of worship and a sweeping urban view.

Inside the temple, you can see worshippers circling the golden chedi and details in the Lanna style. It also makes a rewarding stop after visiting temples in the Old City if you would like to look back over Chiang Mai from the mountain. If you take the paid cable car instead of the stairs, plan around its operating hours, which differ from the temple’s opening hours. Allow time for the mountain drive so you can take in the chedi and city views at an easy pace.
facts: About 06:00–18:00 · listed fare: 50 baht per person

experiences.title: The golden chedi enshrining a Buddha relic
paragraphs: Doi Suthep Temple is said to have been built by King Kuena, who ruled the northern kingdom. Its central golden chedi enshrines a Buddha relic. People come to the same grounds both to admire the gleaming architecture and to pray.

You may see worshippers walk clockwise around the chedi with lotus flowers and incense. A tradition is to make three circuits before offering the incense and flowers. Even if you do not join the ritual, step aside and watch respectfully without blocking the path.

experiences.title: 306 steps guarded by naga
paragraphs: The route up to the temple has 306 steps, with long naga figures—sacred beings shaped like serpents—running along both sides. From below, look up to see the staircase follow the length of the naga bodies toward the temple.

You can climb the stairs or take a separate paid cable car. Choose the steps if you want to walk beside the naga decorations; take the cable car if you prefer to avoid the climb. Cable car hours are separate from the temple’s opening hours, so check the operating schedule when planning your visit.

experiences.title: From the golden temple grounds to the city-view terrace
paragraphs: After looking around the golden chedi, step out onto the terrace. Chiang Mai spreads out below the mountain. You can enjoy the city view after seeing the Lanna-style temple architecture up close, making this a good visit if you want both a temple and a viewpoint.

This is an active religious site on a mountain. Even while taking photos of the view, avoid blocking worshippers’ paths. Plan enough time for both the mountain journey and the temple visit; this can be a more relaxed outing than walking between temples in the city.

rules.title: The cable car closes before the temple
paragraphs: The temple is listed as open into the evening, but **the cable car runs only until about 18:00**. If you plan to take the cable car, do not time your visit solely around the temple’s closing time.

rules.title: Check what your ticket includes
paragraphs: Temple admission and the cable car fare are listed separately. When purchasing a cable car ticket, check whether temple admission is included.

rules.title: Recommended clothing for visiting the temple
paragraphs: Visitors of all genders are advised to wear **clothing that covers the shoulders and knees**. A sleeved top with long trousers or a skirt that covers the knees is a practical choice. Please dress modestly rather than wearing a sleeveless top or short bottoms.

accessSections.title: Travel from Chiang Mai city up the mountain
paragraphs: The temple is high on the mountain west of Chiang Mai city. Search for **Wat Phra That Doi Suthep** as your destination and check the driving route to the temple on the mountain. Do not set your destination only to the broader Doi Suthep area.

wat-phra-singh.type: Old City temple with Lanna Buddha image and murals
wat-phra-singh.title: Wat Phra Singh: Lanna Art and Buddha Image in Chiang Mai | ThaiLiveNow
wat-phra-singh.description: Wat Phra Singh is a Chiang Mai Old City temple with Lanna-style halls, murals and the Phra Singh Buddha image. Look beyond the golden chedi to see the carved wood and paintings inside Viharn Lai Kham.
intro: At Wat Phra Singh in Chiang Mai’s Old City, you can see a golden chedi alongside Lanna-style wooden halls. Inside the grounds, Viharn Lai Kham houses the Phra Singh Buddha image; look closely at the hall’s wood carvings and murals.

Take your time with the carvings, murals and Buddha image inside Viharn Lai Kham. It is an easy stop while walking around the Old City if you would like to see Lanna art. If you also visit Wat Chedi Luang, with its large brick chedi, compare the materials and artistic details at the two temples.
facts: 50 baht · Check on site which halls are covered by the ticket

experiences.title: The Phra Singh Buddha image in Viharn Lai Kham
paragraphs: Viharn Lai Kham, inside the temple grounds, is the hall that houses the Phra Singh Buddha image, also known as Phra Phuttha Sihing. Delicate wood carvings and Lanna-style murals surround the image, so after viewing the Buddha, take time to look at the patterns and paintings too.

Inside the hall, look slowly at the Phra Singh image, the smaller decorative details and the paintings on the walls. After admiring the large golden chedi outdoors, you can see the woodwork and murals up close inside. Follow the day’s visitor instructions for access to the hall.

experiences.title: A royal temple founded in 1345
paragraphs: Wat Phra Singh was founded in 1345 by King Pha Yu of the Lanna Kingdom. It was first known by another name; later, King Saen Muang Ma brought the Phra Singh image from Chiang Rai, and the temple became known by its present name.

The Buddha image that gave the temple its name has long been revered in northern Thailand, and worshippers still come to pay their respects. After seeing the large golden chedi outdoors, visit Viharn Lai Kham to see the image. The carved wood and murals make it a place to linger.

experiences.title: The Buddha image carried through the city at Songkran
paragraphs: During Songkran, a tradition carries the Phra Singh image through Chiang Mai on a special platform. The image normally enshrined in the hall comes out to meet people during the New Year celebration. If you would like to see the procession, check the event announcement for the year of your visit and plan around its dates.

On an ordinary day, walk around the golden chedi and Viharn Lai Kham in turn. A companion interested in architecture can focus on the wood carvings, while someone who enjoys painting can spend longer with the murals.

rules.title: Recommended clothing for visiting the temple
paragraphs: Visitors of all genders are advised to wear **clothing that covers the shoulders and knees**. A sleeved top with long trousers or a skirt that covers the knees is a practical choice. Please dress modestly rather than wearing a sleeveless top or short bottoms.

accessSections.title: Find the temple in the Old City
paragraphs: The destination is **Wat Phra Singh on Sam Lan Road, at number 2**. Search for Chiang Mai as well to avoid confusing it with temples of the same name elsewhere.

wat-chedi-luang.thai: วัดเจดีย์หลวง
wat-chedi-luang.type: Old City temple with a large brick chedi
wat-chedi-luang.title: Wat Chedi Luang: Brick Chedi and Lanna Temple in Chiang Mai | ThaiLiveNow
wat-chedi-luang.description: Wat Chedi Luang is a Chiang Mai Old City temple with a large brick chedi at its centre. See its broken summit, naga sculptures and surrounding halls in the Lanna style.
intro: You have reached Wat Chedi Luang when you come upon the large brick chedi with its broken summit in the middle of Chiang Mai’s Old City. Its broad base and naga sculptures along the stairs give a sense of the scale of this old structure, quite different from a gleaming golden tower.

This temple brings together a large chedi holding the history of the Lanna Kingdom and halls that are still in use. First look at the chedi from a little distance, then go closer to see its base and details. Continue to the Lanna-style halls still used today to see how historic architecture and active places of worship share the same grounds.

experiences.title: A great chedi built in the heart of the city
paragraphs: “Chedi” means stupa, while “luang” means large in the northern dialect. The temple is said to have been founded in 1391 by King Saen Muang Ma in memory of his late father. The great chedi reflects both a royal memorial and the temple’s role at the centre of the city.

At the time, people believed the kingdom would prosper if a stupa modelled on Mount Meru was built at the centre of the capital, with temples placed in the eight surrounding directions. In Buddhism, Mount Meru is regarded as the centre of the world. The great chedi in the heart of the Old City also reflects this royal belief.

experiences.title: A damaged summit and restored brick structure
paragraphs: The upper part of the chedi was damaged in an earthquake in 1545 and has since been repaired into the form seen today. Rather than a completed spire rebuilt from scratch, this is a historic structure whose remaining brickwork hints at its former scale.

From farther away, you can take in the outline with its broken summit; up close, the layered base and brick surface come into view. If you would like to study what remains of the structure, look at it from several directions rather than taking a photo from just one spot.

experiences.title: Naga sculptures and Lanna-style halls
paragraphs: Several multi-headed naga sculptures stand around the chedi. Look at them together with the large base and staircase to get a sense of the imposing approach to the tower. The nearby Lanna-style halls have different materials and rooflines from the brick chedi.

If you also visit Wat Phra Singh in the Old City, compare the details at the two temples. Seeing Wat Phra Singh’s wood carvings and murals alongside the monumental brick structure at Wat Chedi Luang makes an interesting introduction to northern Thai temples.

rules.title: Recommended clothing for visiting the temple
paragraphs: Visitors of all genders are advised to wear **clothing that covers the shoulders and knees**. A sleeved top with long trousers or a skirt that covers the knees is a practical choice. Please dress modestly rather than wearing a sleeveless top or short bottoms.

wat-rong-khun.thai: วัดร่องขุ่น
wat-rong-khun.type: Contemporary Buddhist art temple known as the White Temple
wat-rong-khun.title: Wat Rong Khun (White Temple): Art and Visitor Guide | ThaiLiveNow
wat-rong-khun.description: Wat Rong Khun, the White Temple in Chiang Rai, is designed by local artist Chalermchai Kositpipat around Buddhist and mythological themes. Unlike an old brick ruin, it presents contemporary Buddhist art through white architecture and sculpture.
intro: Wat Rong Khun in Chiang Rai is known as the White Temple for its white architecture and fine, pointed sculptures that tell Buddhist stories. Conceived by Chiang Rai artist Chalermchai Kositpipat, it invites you to look at the bridge before the white hall and figures drawn from mythology as you would look at an artwork.

The White Temple is about 14 km from central Chiang Rai, so allow time to travel there and back. If you enjoy contemporary Thai art or architecture, take your time with the white hall, bridge and sculptures depicting mythological beings. Look at the overall form of the buildings as well as the fine details up close.

experiences.title: A white temple created by Chalermchai
paragraphs: Wat Rong Khun is a contemporary temple created to express an artist’s ideas, rather than a restoration of an old building. Chalermchai Kositpipat expresses Buddhist and mythological themes through white halls and sculptures. Details running along the roof edges and around the windows make the entire building feel like a work of art.
Up close, you can see different sculptures along the roof edges and around the windows of the white hall. Take time to notice their shapes and the ornament carved into their surfaces.

experiences.title: A Buddhist story told as you cross the bridge
paragraphs: The bridge leading to the main hall represents the cycle of rebirth. The route into the hall itself is part of the Buddhist story told at the temple. Decorative figures from Thai and Buddhist mythology continue around the bridge, so after taking a photo in front of the hall, look at the sculptures beside the crossing too.
Cross at an unhurried pace, following the direction set by the site, and notice the figures along the path.

experiences.title: The contrast between white halls and golden architecture
paragraphs: The grounds also include a restroom building with a golden exterior that contrasts with the white halls. Its detailed decoration shows how the artist gave different buildings distinct expressions, even for an everyday facility. Follow on-site directions to see which artworks and interiors are open to visitors.

If you also visit the Blue Temple in Chiang Rai, compare how white and blue are used in the architecture. The temples are in separate locations, so you will need to travel between them. Check on-site guidance for interior photography and access to any separate exhibitions on the day.

rules.title: Follow on-site photography instructions for each area
paragraphs: Taking photos of the exterior is different from photographing works inside the halls. If photography restrictions are posted indoors, put your camera away in those areas.

wat-rong-suea-ten.thai: วัดร่องเสือเต้น
wat-rong-suea-ten.type: Contemporary Buddhist temple with a blue hall
wat-rong-suea-ten.title: Wat Rong Suea Ten (Blue Temple): Chiang Rai Art and Visitor Guide | ThaiLiveNow
wat-rong-suea-ten.description: Wat Rong Suea Ten, the Blue Temple in Chiang Rai’s Rim Kok area, is known for its blue hall and naga guardians at the entrance. Its colour and sculpture offer a striking contrast with Wat Rong Khun, the White Temple.
intro: Wat Rong Suea Ten is Chiang Rai’s Blue Temple, with a large naga standing before its blue hall. The vivid building and curling sculptures at its entrance catch your eye together; look back and forth between the overall structure and its smaller decorations.

The hall in the Rim Kok area was created by a student of the artist behind the White Temple, while the naga design at the entrance was influenced by the craft of the artist behind the Black House. Look closely at the naga’s coiling body and head ornament in front of the blue building. If you are interested in contemporary art from Chiang Rai, the temple offers a chance to see distinct artistic approaches.

experiences.title: Follow the blue across the hall’s decoration
paragraphs: The nickname Blue Temple comes from the hall’s blue exterior. First take in the vivid colour of the building as a whole, then walk closer to see details around the doors and eaves. Sculptures in different forms continue across the blue-painted surfaces.

Figures inspired by Buddhism and mythology appear throughout the building. You can see the shape of a traditional temple roof alongside vivid colours and contemporary decorative details. It is also a rewarding place to photograph striking architecture.

experiences.title: A great naga guards the hall
paragraphs: A large naga stands in front of the main hall as if guarding the way inside. Look at the naga and hall together, then come closer to see the curves of its body and the decoration around its head. Even the large sculpture has fine patterns to examine.

The naga design was influenced by the work of Thawan Duchanee, the artist who created the Black House. First view the blue hall and naga together, then look closely at the details along the creature’s curling body and head.

experiences.title: A temple connected to Chiang Rai artists
paragraphs: The temple’s architect, Sura Nok, also known as Phuttha Kabkaew, was a student of Chalermchai Kositpipat, who created the White Temple. The teacher’s white temple and the student’s blue temple express Buddhist and mythological themes through different colours and forms.

If you are interested in contemporary Thai art, compare the two temples as distinct works. The Blue Temple is north of the city, while the White Temple is south of the city centre. They are not neighbouring halls in one complex, so plan separate journeys to each.

rules.title: Recommended clothing for visiting the temple
paragraphs: Visitors of all genders are advised to wear **clothing that covers the shoulders and knees**. A sleeved top with long trousers or a skirt that covers the knees is a practical choice. Please dress modestly rather than wearing a sleeveless top or short bottoms.

wat-chalong.name: Wat Chalong
wat-chalong.type: Phuket Buddhist temple honouring revered monks
wat-chalong.title: Wat Chalong: Phuket Temple and Local Worship | ThaiLiveNow
wat-chalong.description: Wat Chalong is a Buddhist temple southwest of Phuket Town. Its formal name is Wat Chaithararam. Visit the halls honouring highly respected local monks and see the temple’s Buddhist architecture.
intro: At Wat Chalong, ornate temple buildings stand alongside monk statues covered in gold leaf. Southwest of Phuket Town, this temple’s formal name is Wat Chaithararam. It remains an active place where local people pay their respects to revered monks.

Inside the halls, you can see layers of gold leaf offered by worshippers covering two monk statues. If you would like to add a temple visit to a day spent relaxing on Phuket’s beaches, take time to learn why local people honour these monks. The visit brings together ornate buildings and living traditions of worship.

experiences.title: The monks who helped local people during the 1876 unrest
paragraphs: The temple honours revered monks who helped save local villagers during the tin miners’ revolt of 1876. The story comes from the period when Phuket’s economy depended on mining, before the island became known as a beach destination. As you look at the monk statues in the hall, learn about the gratitude local people have expressed to them.

The statues are objects of gratitude and respect for local people. After looking around the temple buildings, step into the hall to see the gold leaf on the statues and quietly observe worshippers praying.

experiences.title: Layers of gold leaf as an expression of worship
paragraphs: Worshippers have placed layer upon layer of gold leaf on the monk statues. The fine covering reflects offerings made to express gratitude and respect for the revered monks. After seeing the ornate architecture, take a quiet moment inside the hall to observe the worship that continues today.

Look around without getting in the way when people are praying or making offerings. If you take photos, be mindful that this is a hall where worship is actively taking place, not just a display of statues.

experiences.title: A temple between Phuket Town and the beaches
paragraphs: The temple is about 8 km southwest of Phuket Town. It is a separate journey from the streets of Old Town or Patong Beach, so plan the order of your visit around where you are staying.

If you would like to visit after time at the beach, travel in time for the daytime visiting hours. You can explore inside and outside the halls, then quietly observe local people paying their respects to the monk statues.

safari-world.thai: ซาฟารีเวิลด์
safari-world.title: Safari World Bangkok: Safari Park, Marine Park and Visitor Guide | ThaiLiveNow
safari-world.description: On the outskirts of Bangkok, Safari World combines a drive-through Safari Park with the walk-through Marine Park. Spend time watching animals from a vehicle, then explore exhibits and scheduled programmes on foot.
intro: Safari World is a zoo on the outskirts of Bangkok. In Safari Park, you drive through areas where the animals live; in Marine Park, you can walk around the exhibits and programmes.

It suits families who want to spot giraffes and zebras from the car, then get out to see bird and marine-animal exhibits. Unlike a zoo visited entirely on foot, Safari World combines driving and walking. When choosing a ticket, check whether it covers both parks and the vehicle for the safari drive.

experiences.title: Giraffes and zebras across the grassland from your window
paragraphs: Safari Park is a drive-through area designed to evoke the African grasslands. Giraffes and zebras, deer and antelopes, and white rhinoceroses are among the featured animals; the route also includes areas for lions, tigers and bears. Different animals live in separate spaces, so the view outside your window changes as you pass through the zones.

Instead of walking between tanks and enclosures, you stay in a vehicle as you pass through the animals’ living spaces. Both driving your own vehicle and using the facility’s coach are listed options. Travellers without a car can still take the safari route by choosing a product that includes the vehicle tour.

experiences.title: Marine Park has more than marine animals
paragraphs: Marine Park is the walk-through area for exhibits and programmes. In addition to dolphin and sea lion programmes, the listed bird exhibits include macaws, flamingos and scarlet ibises. You can also see land animals such as lemurs from Madagascar and tapirs, as well as large freshwater fish. Despite its name, it is not an aquarium with only marine life.

Eggs World covers how birds hatch and care for their young. After seeing giraffes and zebras from the car, take time to explore the bird exhibits with your children. If they are curious about how eggs and chicks develop, you can read the explanations and stay a little longer.

experiences.title: Choose animal feeding separately from admission
paragraphs: The operator lists feeding activities for giraffes, birds such as lorikeets and sun conures, capybaras and other animals as separate services. You can get close to see animals accept food, but a general admission ticket does not necessarily include every feed or activity. Which animals and areas are available may also change according to on-site guidance.

Rather than trying to fit in every feeding activity and programme, choose the animals you most want to see. Watch animals from your vehicle in Safari Park, then walk around Marine Park and time your visit to a programme you want to see. Check separately whether your ticket includes both parks and the safari vehicle.

rules.title: Check which parks and vehicle are included in your ticket
paragraphs: First check whether **Safari Park and Marine Park are included**. Also check whether the safari vehicle and any separate activities are covered by the ticket. Do not assume older package prices are current admission prices.

faq: What is the difference between Safari Park and Marine Park?

Safari Park is the area where you travel by vehicle to view animals; Marine Park is where you walk around exhibits and programmes. When choosing a ticket, check separately whether it covers both parks and the safari vehicle.

khao-kheow-open-zoo.description: Khao Kheow Open Zoo is a large open zoo in Bang Phra, Si Racha, Chonburi. Explore the animal exhibits and scheduled programmes. Its location and scale make it a different outing from a small attraction within central Pattaya.
intro: Khao Kheow Open Zoo is a large open zoo in Bang Phra, Si Racha, Chonburi. Its exhibits include a range of animals, from large species such as giraffes and white rhinoceroses to a family of hippos, penguins and ring-tailed lemurs.

The zoo is also known as the home of Moo Deng, a pygmy hippo born in 2024. It suits families who want to watch animals at an easy pace or see programmes with different formats, such as elephant swimming and the penguin parade. It is some distance from central Pattaya and covers a large area, so allow time for getting around inside the zoo.
facts: 120 baht · Check the applicable height limit when purchasing

experiences.title: From giraffes and white rhinos to sloths and lemurs
paragraphs: See giraffes, white rhinos, deer and a family of hippos, then visit the areas for two-toed sloths and ring-tailed lemurs. The zoo also highlights pygmy hippos, giant anteaters, sloths, capybaras and wombats. Children can take their time comparing the sizes and shapes of animals, from long-necked giraffes to smaller species.

Ring-tailed lemurs live in an island-like habitat surrounded by water. Viewing the regular exhibits is separate from feeding animals or getting close to them as part of an activity. Follow staff instructions and join feeding or contact activities only in areas where they are allowed that day.

experiences.title: The pygmy hippo family, including Moo Deng
paragraphs: Moo Deng, the pygmy hippo born here on 10 July 2024, became known for her lively movements and daily antics. Her parents are Tony and Jonah, and her sibling is Moo Tun. If you plan to see Moo Deng, take time to observe the hippo family she lives with as well, rather than focusing only on the famous young animal.

Moo Deng may look different in person from videos you have seen online. Even if her viewing area is open, she may be resting or too far away to see clearly. Observe the animals in areas open that day without disturbing their rest.

experiences.title: Elephants swimming and penguins on parade
paragraphs: During the elephant swimming programme, you can watch elephants through the glass of a large tank. Look for how their large bodies move underwater and how they swim with their legs. The penguin parade offers a different kind of viewing, as penguins walk out in a line.

If you plan to watch a programme, allow time to move between viewing areas and wait for it to start. Show schedules, admission, feeding activities and products for getting around the zoo may have different inclusions. Check the official schedule and ticket conditions for your visit date.

experiences.title: Choose a few areas to explore rather than covering the whole zoo
paragraphs: Areas for wildlife conservation, education and research are also located beyond the visitor spaces. The entire zoo is not open to visitors; some areas are restricted for research and conservation. If you are visiting with children, allow time to watch animals they are interested in and read the exhibit information.

Transport between exhibits, including carts and vehicles, has separate costs and conditions from zoo admission. Plan around a few animal areas and perhaps one programme. This lets your family spend time with the animals they enjoy instead of hurrying to cover the entire large zoo.

rules.title: Transport and activity fees are separate
paragraphs: Zoo admission, cart rental and separate activity fees are charged separately. **If you are visiting with older adults or anyone who may find a long walk difficult, consider using a cart or another way to get around inside the zoo.** Choose how to travel based on the size of your group and the areas you want to see.

Golf cart rental is listed at **500–700 baht per vehicle for two hours**. At the rental counter, check the vehicle’s passenger capacity, fee and return time before renting. If you plan to use it longer, ask about extension charges as well.

faq: Is Khao Kheow Open Zoo in central Pattaya?

No. It is in Bang Phra, Si Racha, Chonburi. If you are visiting from accommodation in Pattaya, plan transport to the zoo and the return trip separately. Check the conditions for carts and trams inside the zoo separately from admission.

chiang-mai-zoo.description: Chiang Mai Zoo is at the foot of Doi Suthep. It has expansive animal-viewing areas and a separate aquarium, so check which facilities are covered by basic admission and which need an additional ticket.
intro: Chiang Mai Zoo sits at the foot of Doi Suthep, with spacious outdoor areas for viewing animals and a separate aquarium inside the grounds. Choose carefully between the basic zoo ticket and facilities such as the aquarium that require additional admission.

It is a good option for families who want to see capybaras, kangaroos and penguins, or add an outdoor animal visit to a day around Doi Suthep. If you also want to visit the aquarium, purchase that ticket separately from basic zoo admission. Chiang Mai Night Safari is a different facility.

experiences.title: The new capybara exhibit and animals at the foot of the mountain
paragraphs: Chiang Mai Zoo began as a private zoo established by Harold Mason Young and is now operated by the Zoological Park Organization of Thailand. You can move around its spacious grounds at the foot of Doi Suthep to see the animals.

In 2025, the zoo introduced a new capybara exhibit with more shade and living space. The zoo’s information from the same year also features separate areas for red kangaroos, penguins, red-shanked douc langurs and pygmy goats. Families who enjoy watching animals for a while can focus on the areas that interest them.

experiences.title: Feeding hippos, deer and elephants, plus behind-the-scenes activities
paragraphs: The zoo lists feeding activities with hippos, deer and Asian elephants, as well as staff-led behind-the-scenes programmes with penguins, ring-tailed lemurs and capybaras. You can choose between viewing animals in the exhibit areas and activities that bring you closer to them with staff guidance.

A general admission ticket does not mean you can feed or approach any animal. Some programmes require advance booking, so choose feeding and behind-the-scenes activities that are actually available on your visit date. Free entry, discounts and activity sessions from past special events are not ongoing conditions.

experiences.title: A separate aquarium known as the sea on the mountain
paragraphs: The Chiang Mai Zoo Aquarium inside the grounds has freshwater and marine exhibits connected by an underwater tunnel. After seeing land animals outdoors, you can also go inside to view animals from rivers and the sea.

The basic zoo ticket, aquarium and transport inside the grounds appear as separate items in the fare information. What you want to see—and how long you stay—depends on whether you visit the outdoor animal exhibits alone or add the aquarium. This is a different attraction from Chiang Mai Night Safari, so make sure you set your destination to the zoo.

rules.title: Golf carts are rented by the hour
paragraphs: Zoo admission, transport vehicles inside the grounds and the separate aquarium are different fare items. A golf cart is listed at **350 baht per vehicle per hour**.

The official fare list in English and Thai shows different tram prices, so a single fare cannot be stated with confidence. If you are travelling with someone who finds it difficult to get around, decide whether to use a cart or tram, and ask the ticket office which fare applies to international visitors before boarding the tram.

faq: Are Chiang Mai Zoo and Night Safari the same place?

No. Chiang Mai Zoo at the foot of Doi Suthep and Chiang Mai Night Safari are separate facilities. This page is about Chiang Mai Zoo on Huay Kaew Road. Choose your ticket and vehicle destination by the name of the facility.

chiang-mai-night-safari.description: Chiang Mai Night Safari has vehicle-based animal viewing and walk-through areas. Its vehicle routes are divided into the herbivore-focused Savanna Safari and Predator Prowl, which features predator habitats.
intro: Chiang Mai Night Safari combines vehicle-based animal viewing with areas you can explore on foot. The vehicle routes include Savanna Safari, featuring herbivores, and Predator Prowl, which focuses on predators.

It suits families who want to tour animal areas by vehicle or find an evening activity centred on wildlife. It is a different place from Chiang Mai Zoo near Doi Suthep, so choose a ticket for the Night Safari programmes.

experiences.title: Look for giraffes and zebras on the Savanna Safari
paragraphs: On the Savanna Safari, you sit in a vehicle and travel through the herbivore area. Giraffes, zebras and red kangaroos are among its featured animals. Rather than walking up to enclosures, you look through the vehicle windows as the route passes through the animals’ habitats.

From your seat, watch the size of the giraffes and zebras and how the herds move. Where the animals are when the vehicle passes can vary. They will not always come close to the vehicle, so observe what you can see on the day.

experiences.title: Predator Prowl, featuring tigers and lions
paragraphs: Predator Prowl is a predator-viewing route, separate from the Savanna Safari. Tigers and lions are among the animals featured. Although both are vehicle routes, the focus is different from the herbivore area.

It suits visitors who want to spend an evening seeing both herbivores and predators from a vehicle. Animals do not necessarily become active just because it is night. Stay in the vehicle, follow staff instructions and observe the animals as they are on the day.

experiences.title: Add walk-through exhibits and programmes between the vehicle routes
paragraphs: The facility also has walk-through exhibits and show programmes in addition to the vehicle tours. Decide whether you want only the two vehicle routes or would also like to see the walk-through areas and shows, then check that your chosen booking includes the routes and programmes you want.

Vehicle departures and show performances run at scheduled times. Travel according to the date and start times on your booking, and leave enough time to wait for the vehicle and reach the show area. This is a different facility from Chiang Mai Zoo near Doi Suthep, with separate tickets and location.

rules.title: Check your booked time and programme names
paragraphs: Review the **visit date, start time, vehicle tour and included shows** on your booking confirmation. This is a different product from a Chiang Mai Zoo ticket.

faq: Is Night Safari a zoo where you walk around the whole time?

It combines vehicle and walk-through viewing. Savanna Safari and Predator Prowl are routes where you travel by vehicle to watch animals. If you also plan to visit walk-through areas and shows, check what is included in your chosen product.

sea-life-bangkok.title: SEA LIFE Bangkok Ocean World: Exhibits, Feeding Times and Tickets | ThaiLiveNow
sea-life-bangkok.description: SEA LIFE Bangkok Ocean World is an indoor aquarium inside Siam Paragon in Bangkok. It suits visitors who want to pair marine-life exhibits with city shopping or families looking for an indoor activity with children.
intro: SEA LIFE Bangkok Ocean World is an indoor aquarium inside Siam Paragon in Bangkok. It suits visitors who want to pair marine-life exhibits with city shopping or families looking for an indoor activity with children.

This is a different attraction from Bangkok Aquarium, operated by the Department of Fisheries in Bang Khen. When navigating, search for SEA LIFE Bangkok Ocean World and Siam Paragon rather than entering only “Bangkok Aquarium.”

experiences.title: Coral reef fish, seahorses and jellyfish on Level B1
paragraphs: On Level B1, the exhibits are organised around different environments, including coral reefs, rainforest and jellyfish. The coral reef area features brightly coloured fish such as clownfish; the seahorse area shows how seahorses hold on to seaweed with their tails as they feed.

Take time to watch a small seahorse gripping seaweed with its tail. In the rainforest area, see aquatic plants alongside the forest theme; in the jellyfish area, watch the jellyfish drift through the water. It can be fun to compare the shapes and movements of small animals with children, not only look for large fish.

experiences.title: Look down at sharks, then see them overhead in the tunnel
paragraphs: At Shark Walk, you can look down through a clear acrylic floor into the shark tank below. Spot the sharks swimming under your feet. This exhibit lets you look down on them, unlike viewing a tank from beside it.

At the Ocean Tunnel on Level B2, walk through a passage inside the tank to see marine life around you. Look at both the large tunnel tank and the smaller coral reef tanks, and notice with your children where different animals spend their time.

experiences.title: Gentoo penguins, rocky shores and starfish exhibits
paragraphs: The Penguin Ice Playground on Level B2 features gentoo penguins. The Rocky Shore area separately presents turtles and African penguins. Although they are all called penguins in everyday conversation, the exhibits cover different species in separate spaces.

At Rockpool, you can observe starfish up close in several types of tanks. An exhibit being close to visitors does not mean you can touch everything. Follow the contact instructions for each tank before putting your hands in.

experiences.title: Choose aquarium admission separately from additional activities
paragraphs: The operator recommends allowing at least 90 minutes to visit the aquarium. Rather than squeezing it into a short break between shopping at Siam Paragon, set aside time for exhibits on both levels so you can see everything from small seahorses to the tunnel and penguins without rushing.

Tickets include options for aquarium-only admission and packages with extras such as a boat ride or 4D experience. Check the final booking screen for your visit date and the number of adults and children to see exactly what is included. The lowest listed price does not apply to every adult or every activity.

rules.title: Last admission is one hour before closing
paragraphs: The dedicated opening-hours information lists **last admission at 19:00 and closing at 20:00**. If visiting in the evening, arrive before the last admission time.

rules.title: Check the ticket type for adults and children
paragraphs: Do not treat the lowest online price as the adult admission price. Select your visit date and the number of adults and children, then confirm whether the ticket covers standard admission or a package with additional activities before paying.

faq: What exhibits can I see at SEA LIFE Bangkok?

The jellyfish, rainforest and coral reef exhibits, as well as Shark Walk, are on Level B1. The Ocean Tunnel and penguin exhibit are on Level B2. This indoor aquarium inside Siam Paragon is easy to combine with a shopping itinerary.

underwater-world-pattaya.description: Underwater World Pattaya is an aquarium on Sukhumvit Road. Walk through its 105-metre transparent tunnel, with separate coral reef, shark and ray, and giant freshwater fish sections.
intro: Underwater World Pattaya is an aquarium on Sukhumvit Road. Walk through its 105-metre transparent tunnel, which is divided into coral reef, shark and ray, and giant freshwater fish sections.

It suits families who want to see aquatic animals up close or visitors looking to add an indoor activity beyond the beach in Pattaya. In addition to the tunnel, the aquarium lists activity areas such as a touch pool.
facts: 320 baht · Check the height cutoff at the ticket office

experiences.title: A tunnel from coral reef to sharks and giant freshwater fish
paragraphs: The 105-metre transparent tunnel is divided into sections with different themes, including Coral Reef, Open Ocean and Giant of Siam. The Coral Reef section features colourful schools of tropical reef fish; Open Ocean highlights blacktip reef sharks, jacks and large groupers.

After the marine section, see large freshwater fish from Thailand in Giant of Siam, an exhibit designed around a shipwreck. With children, compare the sharks you saw earlier with the large freshwater fish here. The tunnel lets you explore animals from both the sea and rivers.

experiences.title: The touch pool and Magic Tank offer different ways to explore
paragraphs: The touch pool recreates a rocky pool on the Thai coast as a place to encounter marine life. Magic Tank is presented as a separate interactive tank; there are also reptile areas and otter exhibits beyond the tunnel. The aquarium is more than one long tunnel.

Join hands-on activities only at tanks where they are allowed and follow staff guidance. Regular exhibit tanks are not for touching or feeding at will. If you are visiting with young children, read the information beside each tank first and choose activities they can participate in.

experiences.title: Diver feeding shows and visitor feeding are separate activities
paragraphs: You can watch feeding sessions at the Coral Reef, Open Ocean and Giant of Siam tanks. Divers feed the animals in different tanks, so choose the session for the animals you would most like to see. Explore the exhibits freely, then head to the relevant tank before the session starts.

Visitors can also feed fish and turtles directly. This is a separate activity from watching divers feed the animals. Before participating, check which areas are open that day, the fee and what your ticket includes. It can be a fun indoor break with children during a day at the beach.

rules.title: Take part in activities only in designated areas
paragraphs: For animal contact or feeding, follow **staff guidance in areas where the activity is permitted**. Do not treat regular exhibit tanks as activity areas.

faq: What can I see in the Underwater World Pattaya tunnel?

Along the roughly 105-metre tunnel, you can see areas featuring coral reef life, sharks and rays, and large freshwater fish. The environments vary as you move through the tunnel, so follow the exhibit information in each section. Use the touch pool only in designated areas and as directed by staff.

aquaria-phuket.description: Aquaria Phuket is on Level B1 of Central Phuket Floresta. Explore freshwater habitats themed around forests and rivers, followed by coastal and ray exhibits and a large marine tank, each presenting a different underwater environment.
intro: Aquaria Phuket is on Level B1 of Central Phuket Floresta. Its exhibits move from freshwater habitats themed around forests and rivers to coastal and ray areas and a large marine tank, offering different underwater environments to explore.

It suits families who want to see fish, reptiles and marine life together, or visitors looking for an indoor stop between shopping. This is a different facility from Phuket Aquarium at Cape Panwa, so search for Aquaria Phuket as your destination.
facts: At least **3 hours before your visit**

experiences.title: From Himmapan Forest to freshwater river life
paragraphs: Mystic Forest presents an underwater setting with small and large freshwater fish and aquatic plants, inspired by the Himmapan Forest of Thai mythology. The connected Canopy Walk is an area where you can see freshwater fish in a setting that evokes the branches high above the ground.

At Jewels of the Jungle, look for reptiles; at River Cave, see a water-filled cave setting and Asian small-clawed otters. After the freshwater fish of Himmapan Forest, follow the route to the reptiles and otters.

experiences.title: From penguins and rays to the large marine exhibit
paragraphs: Coastal Haven presents penguins and sharks amid rocky coastal scenery. Stingray Bay has several exhibits themed around coral and different rays, bringing together a coastal environment and the movement of animals in their tanks.

South China Sea is the largest marine exhibit here. After seeing the freshwater fish and otters, walk to the large saltwater tank. With children, look for animals you have seen in rivers and compare them with those from the sea.

experiences.title: A shipwreck story, jellyfish and touch pool
paragraphs: The Largato area also tells the story of the U.S.S. Largato, a vessel that sank in the Gulf of Thailand. As you look at the animals in the tanks, you can learn about the shipwreck behind the exhibit.

Station Aquarius has a jellyfish exhibit and a touch pool. Watch the jellyfish, then take part only in activities permitted at the touch pool. Follow staff instructions in designated areas for any contact with animals. Families who want to see otters, reptiles and marine life can set aside time for the aquarium between shopping stops.

experiences.title: Choose between an aquarium-only ticket and a ticket that includes MAYA
paragraphs: The aquarium is on Level B1 of Central Phuket Floresta. The official sales page lists Aquarium Only tickets separately from combination tickets that include the MAYA Museum, so choose based on whether you want only the aquarium exhibits or another attraction as well.

Online tickets are listed for purchase at least three hours in advance. If buying close to your visit, first check whether the ticket can be used immediately. Choose a ticket based on your child’s height and check which facilities the selected product includes. Phuket Aquarium at Cape Panwa is a separate facility.

rules.title: Do not buy an online ticket just before setting out
paragraphs: The official guidance says to purchase online **at least three hours in advance**. If you want to use the ticket as soon as you arrive, first check when it becomes valid and its conditions.

rules.title: Choose a ticket based on your child’s height
paragraphs: Children’s tickets are based on height. Measure your child and check the eligibility for the selected product. In addition to adult or child pricing, confirm whether it is an **Aquarium Only ticket or a combination ticket with MAYA**.

rules.title: Online tickets cannot be cancelled, refunded or changed
paragraphs: Tickets purchased through the official online booking are **non-cancellable, non-refundable and non-changeable**. Confirm your visit date and party size before buying, and book **at least three hours in advance**.

faq: Is Aquaria Phuket the same place as Phuket Aquarium?

No. Aquaria Phuket is on Level B1 of Central Phuket Floresta; Phuket Aquarium is at Cape Panwa in the southeast of the island. If you are looking for the aquarium inside the shopping mall, set your destination to Aquaria Phuket.

intro: Phuket Aquarium is operated by a marine-resource research institute at Cape Panwa. Explore the underwater tunnel and display tanks to observe marine life and learn about marine resources and environmental conservation.

It suits families who want to read the exhibit information together while looking at sea life. This is a different place from Aquaria Phuket in Central Phuket; here you can pair an aquarium visit with the coastal scenery of Cape Panwa in southeastern Phuket.
facts: 16:00 · Based on the government visitor information for 2025

experiences.title: Cape Panwa marine exhibits shaped by a research institute
paragraphs: Phuket Aquarium has presented marine life since 1983. Operated as an educational space by a marine research institute, it combines tanks where you can observe living animals with explanations about marine resources and environmental conservation.

If you are visiting the Cape Panwa coast in southeastern Phuket, take time to look at the marine life with your children. Observe the animals in the tanks and read about their names and habitats. This is a different aquarium from Aquaria in Central Phuket shopping mall.

experiences.title: Watch marine life and divers together in the tunnel tank
paragraphs: The tunnel tank lets you view aquatic life up close. If you arrive for a diver feeding session, you can also watch the diver feed the animals. As a diver enters a tank you have been viewing, look for how the animals move around them.

The exhibits also include an area of dodecagonal tanks in addition to the tunnel. Rather than passing quickly by one tank, allow time to see how each space presents a different underwater environment. Diver feeding is a scheduled activity, separate from general viewing.

experiences.title: Touch pool, animation and a robotic mermaid
paragraphs: At the touch pool, you can observe animals that live on the seabed and learn about their behaviour up close. Not every animal is available to touch freely; take part only in ways permitted in that area.

After viewing the tanks, look for animation and a robotic mermaid from the Yeosu Expo in South Korea in the underwater-world exhibit. Alongside the living animals, children can explore educational displays that use video and robotics.

rules.title: Check the difference between holiday promotions and general admission
paragraphs: The government’s year-end **free admission promotion for Thai visitors** applies only to specified visitors and dates. Do not treat it as the regular admission price for travellers from other countries.

faq: What is Phuket Aquarium?

It is an aquarium operated by a marine research institute at Cape Panwa. See marine life in the underwater tunnel and display tanks, and learn about environmental conservation. It is a different facility from Aquaria Phuket inside Central Phuket shopping mall.

chatuchak-market.description: Chatuchak is a large Bangkok weekend market for clothing, bags, household goods and crafts. Each section specialises in different goods, so decide what you would like to shop for before setting out instead of trying to cover the entire market.
intro: At Chatuchak, browse everything from clothing and vintage finds to paintings, musical instruments and home décor. The large Bangkok weekend market moved here from a square in front of the Grand Palace in 1982. It also has shops for household goods, a plant section and food.

If you are visiting with a friend who enjoys clothes, explore the fashion and vintage areas; if you are looking for art or things for your home, head for the art and interior-decoration sections. Rather than trying to walk through the whole market, spend time browsing the areas that interest you and compare shops to find clothing or homewares you like.

experiences.title: From vintage clothes to everyday goods
paragraphs: The character of the shops changes by section. Fashion and vintage clothing areas lead into shops selling second-hand items and household goods, while other sections have musical instruments and paintings. Chatuchak is more than a place for travel souvenirs; it is a market where you can compare things and find something that suits your taste.

The market guide groups Sections 2–4 as fashion, Sections 5–6 as vintage, Section 7 as art, and Sections 25–26 as interior decoration. Start in the fashion and vintage sections if you are looking for clothes or accessories, or head to the art and interior-decoration areas for paintings or ceramics.

experiences.title: Browse paintings, ceramics and furniture
paragraphs: The art section has paintings, while the interior-decoration section includes pieces such as ceramics and furniture. Even if you do not buy anything, it is enjoyable to compare the different colours, materials and sizes. Take a look around with a companion interested in decorating a home or finding handmade crafts.

The central clock tower is a useful landmark for finding your way or meeting up with your group. Remember the section number if you find a shop you want to return to; it will make it easier to find after exploring other stalls.

experiences.title: The market changes with the day you visit
paragraphs: Plan general shopping around the weekend market hours. Treat the plant section and Friday evening retail hours as separate visits, since the shops open differ by day even though they are all part of Chatuchak.

The listed market hours do not mean every shop opens and closes at the same time. If there is a stall you especially want to visit, check its hours separately. If you plan to explore several sections, start with the goods you most want to find.

rules.title: Individual shops may have different hours
paragraphs: The market schedule does not mean every shop opens and closes at the same time. Check separately whether any shop you particularly want to visit is open.

accessSections.title: Travel by rail to the market
paragraphs: You can reach the market by **MRT at Kamphaeng Phet or Chatuchak Park stations, or BTS at Mo Chit station**. Check the market sections you plan to visit alongside the station locations on a map to choose where to get off.

intro: Or Tor Kor Market is a food market in Bangkok where the Marketing Organization for Farmers selects agricultural produce and ingredients for sale. Browse fruit and vegetables, meat and seafood, dried goods, rice snacks and sweets, as well as prepared foods.

If you are curious about ingredients used in Thai cooking, take your time walking among the stalls. Watch residents choose ingredients for their groceries, then eat in the food court or buy ready-to-eat dishes to take away. It is also an easy stop for fruit and food after browsing clothes and accessories at Chatuchak across the road.
facts: Marketing Organization for Farmers of Thailand (Or Tor Kor)

experiences.title: From fruit stalls to fresh ingredients
paragraphs: The large covered market has stalls selling fruit and vegetables, meat, seafood, dried goods and rice. If you are curious about the ingredients in a meal you enjoyed at a restaurant, look at the fish and vegetables up close and see what each stall has to offer.

As a market for produce selected by the Marketing Organization for Farmers, Or Tor Kor brings fruit and vegetables together with meat and seafood. Walk among residents choosing ingredients and see the everyday rhythm of grocery shopping in Thailand.

experiences.title: Eat freshly prepared food in the market
paragraphs: You can have breakfast or lunch in the food court, and buy prepared dishes to take away. A key advantage of Or Tor Kor is being able to browse fresh produce and ingredients, then sit down for a meal in the same place.

Take a look at the prepared food and choose what you would like to try. If you arrive without deciding on a restaurant in advance, browse the stalls and pick something that catches your eye for breakfast or lunch.

experiences.title: A food market with a different feel from Chatuchak
paragraphs: Or Tor Kor is close to Chatuchak across the road, but the two markets have different characters. Chatuchak is known for clothes, accessories and crafts; Or Tor Kor focuses on produce, ingredients and prepared food.
After browsing clothing and small goods at Chatuchak, cross the road to Or Tor Kor to choose fruit or have a meal.

khlong-lat-mayom-floating-market.description: Khlong Lat Mayom is a weekend market in Bang Lamad, west of Bangkok, where you can enjoy Thai food and explore the canal. The market has land-based stalls and dining areas as well as boats on the water.
intro: Khlong Lat Mayom is a community market along a canal in Bang Lamad, west of Bangkok, with food stalls and shops selling everyday goods. Eat Thai food by the water and walk around the land-based stalls; you can enjoy the floating-market atmosphere without taking a boat.

Try grilled fish and seafood or noodles, then choose traditional sweets and fruit. You will also find straw hats and woven bags among the food stalls. It suits a relaxed outing with family or friends, sharing food and strolling along the canal-side market.

experiences.title: Canal-side dining before the boat ride
paragraphs: While boats pass along the water, choose food from the canal-side stalls and dining area, then browse shops selling clothing, ceramics and household goods. You can enjoy a walk through the market and have a meal without taking a boat.

Choose grilled fish, seafood, som tam or grilled chicken for a meal. If you would like noodles, look for boat noodles or khanom chin; you can also add grilled prawns or squid and crispy hoi thot. Sharing several dishes with your companions is a good way to sample more of the market food.

experiences.title: Traditional sweets and locally made goods
paragraphs: After your meal, look for traditional sweets such as khanom krok, as well as fruit such as pomelo, bananas and coconuts. Rather than deciding in advance what to eat, browse the food and fruit in front of you to discover the market’s flavours.
Stalls also sell straw hats, woven bags and herbal products. After eating, browse with your family or friends for a hat to wear on your trip or a small item to take home.

experiences.title: A canal boat ride is a separate activity
paragraphs: A boat tour along the canal is a separate product you can choose. Walking around the market and eating there do not include a boat ride.

Before boarding, confirm the departure point, whether the fare is per person or per boat, passenger capacity, duration, stops and any extra charges. Clarifying the route and fare first makes it easier to decide whether to add a boat ride after your meal.

rules.title: Confirm the unit of the boat fare
