amphawa-floating-market.description: Amphawa Floating Market in Samut Songkhram has old houses and shops along both sides of a canal. Walk the waterside while choosing Thai food, seafood, desserts and souvenirs.
intro: At Amphawa, food boats moor among the old wooden houses and shops that line both sides of the canal. Cross an arched bridge to browse the stores, then sit on the waterside steps and eat seafood grilled to order from a boat. It is a market where you can spend an evening by the water.

Try Thai coffee and coconut ice cream, then browse seasonal fruit and souvenirs along the canal. A boat trip to see fireflies is a separate activity from visiting the market. Since sightings depend on natural conditions, allow time to enjoy a meal and a walk through the market as well.

experiences.title: Wooden shopfronts and bridges along the canal
paragraphs: The market route in Amphawa follows old wooden houses along both sides of the canal. Boats selling food moor by the water, while arched bridges and steps link the paths on either side.
Walk past shops or look along the canal from a bridge. Unlike a single large indoor market, the view changes with the waterside, lanes and bridges, making this a good place for an unhurried stroll.

experiences.title: Seafood grilled on boats and sweet treats
paragraphs: Seafood sellers prepare food by the water, and visitors sit on the steps or waterfront to eat—one of the defining scenes at Amphawa. Choose grilled seafood or enjoy an evening beside the canal with Thai coffee and fruit.

Try oliang iced coffee, coconut ice cream, pickled fruit or Thai sweets. Alongside the food, you can browse textiles, wooden toys and jewellery, then continue your walk after dinner to look for souvenirs.

experiences.title: Walk the weekend market and decide on a firefly boat separately
paragraphs: The market and town are liveliest around the Friday, Saturday and Sunday markets and public holidays. On weekdays, you should not expect the same stalls to be open. What you can experience depends on whether you visit on a market day or take a walk along the canal.

If you want a boat after sunset to look for fireflies, check the boarding point, route, price and return time separately. A boat tour is not included in a visit to the market. Firefly sightings depend on natural conditions, so boarding a boat does not guarantee you will see them.

mae-klong-railway-market.title: Mae Klong Railway Market: Train Times, Market and Safety | ThaiLiveNow
mae-klong-railway-market.description: Mae Klong Railway Market is set along an active railway near Mae Klong Station in Samut Songkhram. It is known for vendors folding back their awnings and goods as trains pass.
intro: Mae Klong Railway Market is a local market set along the active Mae Klong–Ban Laem railway. When a train approaches, vendors fold back their awnings and move their goods; after it passes, they put everything back. The market is famous for this scene, but it is also a place where people shop for fish, vegetables and fruit.

It suits visitors interested in pla thu fish, curry pastes, fruit and everyday goods, or the unusual setting where a railway runs through a market. When waiting for a train, keep the track clear and follow instructions from vendors and railway staff. Check the day’s service information separately; a train’s departure time from the station is not its time passing through the market.

experiences.title: Shopping beside the train tracks
paragraphs: Narrow stalls along the railway sell fish, vegetables, fruit, curry pastes and everyday goods. Look for pla thu, a local favourite, and see which ingredients are for sale. Even when no train is passing, residents shop and vendors continue arranging their goods and selling.

Display tables stand right beside the track, so you can browse goods and see the train route just next to you. Watch the train approach and, after it has passed, see vendors open their awnings and set the goods back out. Keep the tracks clear while you wait and follow on-site instructions.

experiences.title: Awnings folded back, then opened again
paragraphs: As a train approaches, vendors fold their awnings and move goods further back to clear the area around the railway. After the train passes, they reopen the awnings, set their displays back out and carry on trading. This scene of shops being folded away and reopened is what made the market widely known.

Standing on the track to take a close-up photo or blocking the path in front of stalls can get in the way of vendors and other visitors. Wait in a safe place as instructed by staff and vendors, and clear the route when a train passes.

experiences.title: Station departure time and market pass-through time differ
paragraphs: The time a train leaves the station is different from the time it passes the market. If you want to see the train at the market, do not wait based only on the station departure time; check same-day service information and on-site notices for the pass-through time. Avoid planning your visit based only on old timetables.
While waiting for the train, browse the fish and ingredient stalls too. You can see residents choosing pla thu and vegetables and vendors arranging their displays as they go about their business.

rules.title: Clear the track when a train approaches
paragraphs: This is an active railway. Follow **instructions from vendors and railway staff to clear the area**, and do not stay on the track to take photographs.

chiang-mai-sunday-market.title: Chiang Mai Sunday Market: Ratchadamnoen Walking Street | ThaiLiveNow
chiang-mai-sunday-market.description: Chiang Mai Sunday Walking Street runs on Sunday evenings from Tha Phae Gate along Ratchadamnoen Road. Browse crafts, household goods, aromatherapy products and food stalls.
intro: Chiang Mai Sunday Walking Street is a Sunday evening market stretching from Tha Phae Gate along Ratchadamnoen Road. Browse northern Thai handicrafts, household goods and aromatherapy products, then choose street food and fruit drinks. It is an easy way to combine a walk through the Old City with an evening at the market.

It suits visitors who want to take their time looking at crafts with a friend or try northern Thai snacks that may be new to them. Unlike Saturday’s Wualai market or the Night Bazaar, which opens every day, this market has its own location and schedule. Set aside a Sunday evening to see the street itself come to life.

experiences.title: Handicrafts along a road inside the old city walls
paragraphs: The market stretches along Ratchadamnoen Road from Tha Phae Gate in the direction of Wat Phra Singh. Stalls fill the road and surrounding spaces, so as you browse, look at the Old City’s historic buildings too.

You can find everyday items such as handmade soap, dolls, pillowcases, paintings, clothes and shoes. If you enjoy aromatherapy products or handicrafts, compare the materials and patterns at different stalls. It also suits a trip where you are looking for a small souvenir.

experiences.title: Kai pam and snacks from the market
paragraphs: Choose anything from a filling dinner to small snacks to sample as you walk. Kai pam is an egg dish cooked in a banana-leaf cup. You may also find crispy fish and mango salad served with peanuts and herbs.

There are fried wontons with fillings and fruit or herbal drinks too. If you are visiting with a friend, choose different snacks and share them. You can spend the evening browsing craft stalls and stopping along the way to try food.

experiences.title: An unhurried Sunday evening walk
paragraphs: Walk from Tha Phae Gate to Wat Phra Singh along Ratchadamnoen Road to see both the stalls and the historic centre of the Old City. There are outdoor massage tents along the road where you can rest between browsing and eating.
You do not need to hurry to the end of Ratchadamnoen Road. Spend time at craft stalls or snack shops that interest you.

accessSections.title: Start at Tha Phae Gate
paragraphs: The market follows **Ratchadamnoen Road from Tha Phae Gate**. Search for Sunday Market, Chiang Mai, and make sure your visit is on a Sunday.

wualai-saturday-market.description: Wualai Saturday Market takes place on Wualai Road, south of Chiang Mai Gate, on Saturday evenings. Browse crafts, clothing, accessories and food along a street known for silverwork.
intro: Wualai Saturday Market opens on Saturday evenings along the old silverworking street south of Chiang Mai Gate. The lane still has silversmiths, and craft, textile, household-goods and food stalls bring together Chiang Mai’s handmade arts and evening market atmosphere.

It suits visitors who enjoy crafts such as silver jewellery or lacquerware, or friends looking for an evening stroll with food. The permanent workshops open during weekday daytime hours offer a different experience from the Saturday stalls, so choose when to go based on whether you want to see silverwork or the weekend market.

experiences.title: Handmade goods in a silverworking community
paragraphs: Wualai is a street known as an old silverworking community. At the market, look for silver jewellery, lacquerware, carvings, lamps, silk, textiles and scarves. Compare the materials and patterns of similar items to find one you like.

You can also find bags and fabrics woven by hill-tribe communities, and household decorations. If you are visiting with someone who enjoys crafts, look beyond silver jewellery to textiles and wooden or lacquered goods. Compare work made from metal, fabric and wood along the same street.

experiences.title: Food for a Saturday evening
paragraphs: Have dinner with grilled fish, som tam or pad thai, then finish with coconut sweets or a fruit smoothie. You may also find satay with peanut sauce, so stop for a bite when you see something you would like to try.

experiences.title: Silversmith shops stay open; market stalls come out on Saturday evenings
paragraphs: The silversmith shops along the street are permanent businesses, while the Saturday market stalls appear on Saturday evenings. Visit on a Saturday evening if you want to browse the stalls; you are unlikely to find the same market atmosphere during weekday daytime hours.

On Saturday evenings, you can explore crafts and food along the street south of Chiang Mai Gate. The market on Ratchadamnoen Road is in a different place and runs on a different day, so keep the two evening markets in mind as you plan your weekend.

accessSections.title: Find the market from Chiang Mai Gate

chiang-mai-night-bazaar.description: Chiang Mai Night Bazaar is a night-time shopping district around Chang Khlan Road. Browse traditional handicrafts, clothing and souvenirs, and visit nearby restaurants.
intro: Chiang Mai Night Bazaar is a shopping and dining district around Chang Khlan Road in the evening. Browse shops selling traditional crafts, clothing and souvenirs, then continue to a nearby restaurant or café for a meal. It works well for an evening of shopping without having to wait for a particular day of the week.

Unlike the Sunday Ratchadamnoen or Saturday Wualai markets, the Night Bazaar is a shopping area open every day. Nearby Anusarn Market and individual shops may have different opening hours, so check the hours of any specific shop you want to visit.

experiences.title: An evening shopping area along Chang Khlan Road
paragraphs: Shops selling traditional crafts, clothing and souvenirs line Chang Khlan Road. Beyond the market area itself, you can also see the street’s mix of hotels, cafés and restaurants.

After browsing the crafts and souvenir shops, you can have dinner at a nearby restaurant. Take a break in a café and return to the street if you like. Shops and restaurants are clustered around Chang Khlan Road, so choose places that catch your interest and enjoy the evening.

experiences.title: A different market from the weekend walking streets
paragraphs: The Night Bazaar is in a different place from the Saturday market on Wualai Road and the Sunday market along Ratchadamnoen Road. Some vendors may sell at other markets on weekends, but seeing a familiar shop does not mean you are at the same market. Set your destination around Chang Khlan Road when visiting the Night Bazaar.

Finding souvenirs each evening can be useful for travellers with a tight itinerary. If you are looking for a particular craft or shop, do not assume the same hours apply to the whole Night Bazaar; check information from the individual shop.

experiences.title: Continue to Anusarn for food
paragraphs: After looking at clothes and crafts, walk toward nearby Anusarn Market if you want to browse more food stalls. Its food area offers options for dinner.
The Night Bazaar and Anusarn Market are separate areas. If people in your group want different dishes, take a look around nearby restaurants and Anusarn’s food stalls and choose what suits you.

lard-yai-sunday-market.description: Lard Yai Walking Street is a Sunday market on Thalang Road in Phuket Old Town. Food and souvenir stalls gather against the backdrop of the neighbourhood’s historic shop-house architecture.
intro: Lard Yai Walking Street is a Sunday evening market on Thalang Road in Phuket Old Town. Stalls selling batik, crocheted dolls, handmade crafts and street food line the old Sino-Portuguese shop-houses. Walk past the building façades and signs as you browse for something to buy or a snack to try.

If you enjoy old architecture and independent shops, explore Old Town during the day, then come back in the evening to try Phuket food at the market. You can visit Old Town on other days, but go on Sunday if you want to see the stalls on Thalang Road.

experiences.title: A market in front of Sino-Portuguese shop-houses
paragraphs: Old shop-houses line Thalang Road, with stalls appearing in front of them on Sundays. The market began as a community project to preserve local culture, so the surrounding buildings and neighbourhood are also part of what you can see.
Walk among the stalls and look at the old shop-house façades and signs. Old Town is worth exploring on other days too, but visit on Sunday if you want to see the Thalang Road stalls.

experiences.title: Batik and handmade souvenirs
paragraphs: Stalls sell batik fabric and bags, crocheted dolls, hats, jewellery and handicrafts. Look closely at the patterns on the fabrics and the details of the dolls; if you find something you like, choose it as a gift or keepsake from Phuket.

Products vary from shop to shop, so instead of walking quickly along the entire row, pause when you see a pattern or material you like. You can explore different stalls with family or friends and meet again near the food stalls.

experiences.title: Hor mok, grilled food and Thai snacks
paragraphs: For dinner, choose hor mok fish custard, grilled squid, chicken or pork, or pad thai. There are also juices, ice cream and Thai sweets, so you can pick a dessert along Thalang Road after your meal.

accessSections.title: Find the market on Thalang Road

cicada-market.description: Cicada Market in Nong Kae, Hua Hin, is a weekend night market with art and crafts, food and performance spaces. It suits a visit focused on creative work and design rather than everyday shopping.
intro: Cicada Market in Hua Hin is a weekend art market bringing together handmade crafts and artworks, food and music spaces. Rather than a market for everyday essentials, it focuses on creators’ designs and art, making it especially appealing if you enjoy paintings and handicrafts.

Browse home décor, clothes and jewellery, then have dinner in the tropical-garden-like food area and look for the outdoor stage beneath the large trees. Although there is a performance venue, the stages and programmes may vary by date.

experiences.title: A design market with handmade details
paragraphs: The Handmade & Idea section has home décor, clothes, jewellery and souvenirs made by local creators. Look at who made each item and compare the designs from stall to stall. If you enjoy painting or handicrafts, take time to look closely at pieces that catch your eye.
If you are looking for something to decorate your home or a travel gift, browse both small artworks and everyday items.

experiences.title: Artworks and exhibitions at ArtFactory
paragraphs: ArtFactory displays and sells original artworks. After looking through the outdoor stalls for souvenirs, stop by to see the works on display. It is a good place to talk about paintings with a companion who is interested in art.

experiences.title: An evening of food and music in the garden
paragraphs: The food area offers Thai dishes and menus from several countries. Sasi Open Air Theatre, beneath a large tree, is an outdoor stage for music programmes. If you would like to combine art, a meal and music, check what is scheduled on the stage that day.

Cicada has a performance venue, but the same show does not run at the same time every visit. If you want to see a particular performance, check that day’s programme separately. If a show is not your main reason for visiting, the weekend market still offers plenty to see and eat.

grand-palace.description: Explore Bangkok’s Grand Palace and Wat Phra Kaew together. See the Emerald Buddha and royal architecture, and visit the Queen Sirikit Museum of Textiles, which is included with the same ticket.
intro: Bangkok’s Grand Palace is a complex where you can visit royal halls and Wat Phra Kaew, home of the Emerald Buddha. The grounds bring together different forms of architecture and art, from golden buildings and Ramakien murals to Chakri Maha Prasat, a European-style building topped with a Thai roof.

If this is your first visit to a Thai royal palace and temple, look closely at the golden roofs, murals and hall decorations. The Queen Sirikit Museum of Textiles is included with admission too. Some buildings remain in use for royal ceremonies, so not every interior is open to visitors.
facts: **500 baht** · Includes Wat Phra Kaew and the Queen Sirikit Museum of Textiles

experiences.title: Chakri Maha Prasat: a Thai roof above a European-style building
paragraphs: One building to look for at the Grand Palace is **Chakri Maha Prasat Hall**. European-style windows and columns sit beneath the pointed roof of a traditional Thai palace. Look first at the arched windows and decorative columns at the lower level, then look up to see the three-tiered Thai roof.

Built at the direction of King Rama V, the hall is used for royal ceremonies. You can see the exterior, but the throne and rooms inside are not always open to the public. Focus on the roof, windows and column decorations from outside rather than expecting access to the interior.

experiences.title: Ramakien murals among the golden buildings
paragraphs: The galleries around Wat Phra Kaew are lined with murals depicting **the Ramakien**, Thailand’s national epic. Princes, monkey armies and giants appear in scenes filled with small figures, palaces, forests and battles.

After seeing the Emerald Buddha and golden halls, walk along the galleries with the murals. Up close, you can make out expressions and clothing on small figures, as well as details of forests and palaces. Along with the building exteriors, you can enjoy paintings that tell an old Thai story.

experiences.title: A ticket that also covers the textile museum
paragraphs: The 500-baht ticket for international visitors includes admission to Wat Phra Kaew and the Queen Sirikit Museum of Textiles. Decide whether you want to visit only the temple or also spend time in the museum.

**The audio guide costs 200 baht separately from admission.** You need a passport or credit card to rent one. Korean is not available; the guide is offered in English, Japanese and other languages. Choose from the available language list if you plan to use it.

rules.title: Dress appropriately before you set out
paragraphs: Clothing such as **sleeveless tops, short tops, see-through clothing, shorts and miniskirts** is not allowed. Torn trousers, tight-fitting trousers and pyjamas are also restricted. Wear a top that covers your shoulders and long bottoms.

rules.title: Online tickets cannot be changed or refunded
paragraphs: Online tickets **cannot be refunded or changed to a different date or time**. Buy after your travel plans are set and check your visit date once more before paying. Tickets for the day can also be purchased at the on-site ticket office.

rules.title: Follow day-of entrance and access instructions
paragraphs: Visitors enter the Grand Palace through **Mani Noppharat Gate**. Follow on-site directions if the entrance or viewing areas change for royal events or other reasons. Drones may not be flown over the palace.

accessSections.title: Go to the visitor entrance
paragraphs: Search for **The Grand Palace** on a map and go to the visitor entrance, **Mani Noppharat Gate**. If travelling by boat, Tha Chang Pier is an access option. A map pin may point to the centre of the complex, so show the entrance name as well if you arrive by car.

faq: Do I need separate tickets for the Grand Palace and Wat Phra Kaew?
No. The 500-baht ticket for international visitors includes Wat Phra Kaew and the Queen Sirikit Museum of Textiles. One ticket covers the complex.

museum-siam.description: Museum Siam in Bangkok explores Thai culture through food, clothing, architecture and everyday objects. Find out about the 14-room permanent exhibition, interactive displays, admission and the route from Sanam Chai MRT Station.
intro: Museum Siam explores Thai culture through food, clothing, architecture and everyday objects. Rather than listing royal artefacts or archaeological collections, it uses everyday things and stories to ask where the ideas we associate with being Thai come from.

Visit after exploring the Grand Palace if you would like to see an indoor exhibition, or if you are curious about the Thai food and daily life you have encountered on your trip. Some displays invite you to handle objects or take part in games, giving you another way to explore beyond reading the explanations. The museum is accessible from Exit 1 of Sanam Chai MRT Station and is closed on Mondays.

experiences.title: What makes something Thai, explored through food, clothes and architecture
paragraphs: The permanent exhibition, “Decoding Thainess,” explores how the meaning of “being Thai” has changed over time through history, architecture, traditions, food and clothing. Across 14 rooms, you can see objects from daily life in the past and present and read the stories behind them.

If you have wondered how people ate and dressed while visiting temples and palaces, explore this exhibition. Look for connections between clothing and food you have seen on the streets and the stories told in the museum.

experiences.title: Culture through everyday objects and games
paragraphs: The exhibition on traditions and festivals is arranged like a storeroom. Learn about customs through information and images in boxes, objects you can touch, and games.

In the photography room, choose clothes, accessories, backdrops and props to take a picture. It suits a visit with family or friends who enjoy hands-on exhibitions where you can choose objects and take part rather than only read the displays.

experiences.title: Books and souvenirs to browse after the exhibitions
paragraphs: After viewing the exhibitions, stop by the Muse Shop. It sells stationery, jewellery, household goods and history books related to the museum’s themes. There is also a small DIY space.

The museum offers audio guides, lockers and wheelchairs. If you plan to visit in a wheelchair, ask the information desk which exhibitions and routes are accessible. The fact that wheelchairs are available does not mean every exhibition can be reached without limitations.

rules.title: Choose the ticket that matches your free or student admission
paragraphs: General admission is **100 baht for Thai and international visitors alike**. **Thai and international visitors under 15 and visitors aged 60 or older enter free**; students aged 15 and above pay 50 baht. Bring proof of student status if you are applying for the student fare. Ask the ticket office which ticket applies to the documents you have.

rules.title: Audio guides and lockers are available
paragraphs: The museum provides **audio guides, wheelchairs and lockers**. You can listen to exhibition information or leave your belongings in a locker while you explore.

accessSections.title: Arrive from Sanam Chai MRT Station
paragraphs: If you are travelling by rail, use **Exit 1 at Sanam Chai Station on the MRT Blue Line**. Search for Museum Siam on a map.

national-museum-bangkok.description: Explore Thai history, archaeology and art in the former Front Palace buildings and later exhibition halls at National Museum Bangkok. See Buddhist art, traditional crafts and royal funeral chariots in one visit.
intro: National Museum Bangkok presents Thai history, archaeology and art in the former Front Palace buildings and later exhibition halls. Its collections include Buddhist art, traditional crafts and royal funeral chariots.

Visit if you are curious about the different styles of Buddha images you have seen in temples, or would like to look more closely at Thai royal crafts. Explore several exhibition halls, from small sculptures and crafts to large funeral chariots. The museum is closed on Mondays, Tuesdays and public holidays, so plan your visit on another day.

experiences.title: Compare Buddha images from different periods
paragraphs: The museum displays Thai cultural heritage from prehistoric times to the present Chakri dynasty. Buddhist sculptures and traditional royal crafts are among the collections, so if you are curious about Buddha images and decorations seen at temples, you can look more closely here.

When looking at Buddha images, compare facial features, folds in the robes and body decorations. Different halls present Buddhist art, royal crafts and other collections. Take your time with a work in the hall that interests you.

experiences.title: Monumental chariots used in royal funerals
paragraphs: You can also see **large, ornate chariots used for royal funerals**. After looking at small objects in display cases, the scale of a chariot stands out. Up close, examine the details covering its surface.

Compare small craft objects with the huge ceremonial chariots. If you are interested in Thai royal ceremonies and traditional crafts, take time to look at the chariots’ decorations as well as their size.

experiences.title: The Sihing Buddha image and murals in the former Front Palace
paragraphs: The former Front Palace buildings used by the museum are also worth seeing. Inside the chapel housing the Sihing Buddha image, you can see the image and murals depicting the life of the Buddha on the interior walls. After exploring the objects, take a look at the building and murals too.

accessSections.title: Walk from Tha Chang Pier

jim-thompson-house.description: Visit the teak houses and Asian art collection at Jim Thompson House Museum in Bangkok. Find details about guided tours of the main house, admission and children’s fares, and how to get there from Exit 1 at BTS National Stadium.
intro: Jim Thompson House Museum lets you visit the home of Thai silk entrepreneur Jim Thompson and the Asian art he collected. Six teak houses stand in a garden beside a canal in central Bangkok. It suits visitors who want to see traditional Thai house architecture and historic artworks close up amid the shopping malls and tall buildings around Siam.

You visit the main house with a guide who explains the building and collection. This is different from a shop where you browse silk products. Visit with a friend who enjoys architecture or art, or add a historic house to your Bangkok itinerary. See the wooden houses together with the garden around them.
jim-thompson-house.addressKo: 6 Kasem San 2 Alley, Rama I Road, Wang Mai, Pathum Wan, Bangkok

experiences.title: Six teak houses moved to Bangkok
paragraphs: Jim Thompson acquired old houses from different parts of Thailand and moved them to Bangkok. The houses were dismantled and transported, then reassembled by carpenters from Ayutthaya to form one residence of six connected houses. Construction began in 1958 and was completed the following year. This was the home where Jim Thompson lived.
Across the canal in front of the house is Ban Khrua, a weaving community. A garden surrounds the wooden houses, so alongside the art inside, you can also see the garden and canal-side scenery.

experiences.title: Asian art collected by a silk entrepreneur
paragraphs: Jim Thompson was a silk entrepreneur and art collector, and he had studied architecture. In the late 1950s, as he collected Asian artworks and antiques, he decided to build a home to house the collection. Today, you can see both the teak house where he lived and the art he kept inside.

The same complex also has an art centre and other exhibitions and shops. These are separate from the museum’s main house, so check the admission conditions for each exhibition if you plan to visit them too.

experiences.title: From Buddha images to blue-and-white porcelain and Benjarong ceramics
paragraphs: The collection includes Buddhist sculptures and Thai paintings, Chinese and Annamese blue-and-white porcelain, and Benjarong ceramics made for the Thai royal court. See artworks from different periods and regions in one place.

Benjarong ceramics include bowls painted with flowers and animals in several colours, while blue-and-white porcelain has blue designs on a white ground. If you are curious about the collection, browse photos and information in the foundation’s online exhibition.

faq: Can I visit Jim Thompson House without a reservation?

Yes. You can visit in person without booking in advance. The museum says same-day on-site visits are available even if online reservations are sold out. To buy online, use the ticket provider linked from the Admission page on the museum website.
Which languages are the guided tours available in?
The museum lists guided tours in Thai, English, French, Chinese and Japanese. Korean is not included. The main house is visited with a guide, so choose a language you can follow.

ancient-city-muang-boran.name: Muang Boran (Ancient City)
ancient-city-muang-boran.thai: เมืองโบราณ
ancient-city-muang-boran.title: Muang Boran (Ancient City): Architecture and Visitor Guide | ThaiLiveNow
ancient-city-muang-boran.description: Muang Boran is a large outdoor museum in Samut Prakan, with recreated architecture and displays from across Thailand. Despite its name, not every building is an ancient ruin preserved in its original location.
intro: Muang Boran is an outdoor museum in Samut Prakan where you can see palace and temple architecture from different parts of Thailand in one place. Some buildings to explore inside and out include Sanphet Prasat, a reconstruction of the lost Ayutthaya palace, and Dusit Maha Prasat, recreated with reference to historical records.

Visit with friends or family who enjoy photographing and comparing the roofs, doors and windows of palaces and temples. Unlike historic cities where ruins remain in their original locations, this museum also includes reconstructed buildings that no longer survive. If you have visited the remains of the palace in Ayutthaya, you can also see here how a palace has been recreated from historical records.

experiences.title: Sanphet Prasat, a reconstruction of the lost Ayutthaya palace
paragraphs: Sanphet Prasat recreates the central hall of the Ayutthaya royal palace. The original palace burned during the fall of Ayutthaya, leaving only its base. At Muang Boran, researchers studied the surviving remains and historical records to recreate its architecture and interior decoration.

**Layered roofs, pointed spires, and doors and windows decorated with mother-of-pearl** were made with reference to historical architectural sources. Inside, you can see golden pillars, mirror decoration and murals depicting stories of Vishnu’s avatars. Photograph the whole building, then look closely at the small details on the doors and windows.

experiences.title: Dusit Maha Prasat, recreated from historical records
paragraphs: You can also visit Dusit Maha Prasat. Rather than copying the current appearance of the Grand Palace in Bangkok, this building recreates an earlier form based on old photographs and records. Its murals and pillar decoration also offer a look at Thai palace architecture.

If you have already visited the Grand Palace in Bangkok, compare its roofs, pillars and interior decoration with this building. The outdoor museum is large, so choose which architecture you most want to see and allow time accordingly.

experiences.title: An outdoor museum for comparing regional architecture
paragraphs: Areas organised by northern, northeastern, central and southern Thailand present palace and temple architecture from each region. You can compare regional styles in one place without travelling between cities across the country.

Choose the palaces and temples you want to see on the map first. Use a golf cart if you are travelling together, or rent a bicycle if you want to pedal around yourself. If you bring your own car into the park, there is a separate **400-baht vehicle entry fee per car for international visitors**.

At the remains of the palace in Ayutthaya, you see what survives at the original site; here you can see a palace recreated from historical records. It is a display that offers a sense of what the palace may have looked like, though it is not an original structure preserved in its original location.

rules.title: Vehicle entry fee and golf-cart driving conditions
paragraphs: The fee to bring your own car into the park is separate from golf-cart rental. **For international visitors, vehicle entry costs 400 baht per car and does not include the driver’s admission.**

To drive a golf cart yourself, you must be **at least 18 and hold a Thai or international driving licence**. If you are visiting with older adults or anyone who finds long walks difficult, consider a golf cart as a way for your group to get around together.

erawan-museum.description: At Erawan Museum in Samut Prakan, see the enormous three-headed elephant building, its three levels of exhibits and the surrounding garden. The museum includes interior galleries as well as the sculpture outside.
intro: Erawan Museum in Samut Prakan is known for its enormous building topped by a three-headed elephant. After viewing the sculpture outside, go indoors to explore three levels: antiques and ceramics below, a stained-glass ceiling and religious decoration, then Buddha images and a celestial ceiling painting inside the elephant.

It suits visitors who want to photograph unusual architecture or enjoy Thai religious art and ceramics. There are small decorative details to see inside as well as the large sculpture outside, and after the museum you can walk around the garden with its mythical-animal figures. The museum is operated in connection with Muang Boran, but the two are separate facilities in different locations.
facts: 250 baht · Check applicable age and height when purchasing

experiences.title: Antiques and Benjarong ceramics on the Suvarnabhumi level
paragraphs: The underground Suvarnabhumi level displays antiques and ceramics collected by founder Lek. Alongside pieces such as Benjarong pottery decorated in several colours, the small objects offer a different experience from the building’s grand exterior.

The exhibition is divided into three levels representing the underworld, the human world and heaven. After viewing the enormous elephant outside, enter to explore the antiques below and the religious decoration on the upper floor.

experiences.title: A stained-glass ceiling showing the earth in four colours
paragraphs: Inside the round building supporting the elephant sculpture is a **stained-glass ceiling**. Yellow, white, red and blue represent earth, wind, fire and water, with zodiac signs around the edge. After seeing the elephant outside, go in and look up at the ceiling.

The pillars are decorated with scenes from Buddhism, Hinduism, Mahayana Buddhism and Christianity. Before going upstairs, look at the pictures on the pillars and the small patterns made from ceramic pieces. There is plenty of detail to notice up close if you enjoy religious art and crafts.

experiences.title: A different atmosphere inside the elephant
paragraphs: The celestial space is an exhibition hall **built inside the elephant’s body**. Unlike the colourful decoration on the floor below, the lighting is subdued and Buddha images are displayed in a quiet space. The ceiling is painted with the sun, stars and the Milky Way.

After viewing antiques in the underground level and the decoration of the human-world floor, you reach the celestial space depicting the universe. Exhibits and lighting change from one level to the next. The garden outside also has mythical-animal sculptures to see after your visit indoors.

experiences.title: A garden with animals from Thai mythology
paragraphs: The surrounding garden has trees from Thai literature and figures of mythical animals, making it a good place for a walk after the indoor exhibits. Garden admission, flowers, incense and lotus flowers are included with the ticket. The museum’s audio guide is also available in Korean.

rules.title: Use the lift in the elephant’s left leg to reach the celestial level
paragraphs: The route to the celestial level inside the elephant’s body is divided between an **elevator in the left leg** and **stairs in the right leg**.

ayutthaya-historical-park.name: Ayutthaya Historical Park

ayutthaya-historical-park.description: Ayutthaya Historical Park spans the former royal capital, with palace remains and temple ruins at several locations. It is not one enclosed park where every site can be reached on foot from a single entrance.
intro: Ayutthaya Historical Park lets you explore palace remains and temple ruins in Siam’s former capital. Founded around 1350, the city grew into a centre of international trade and diplomacy before it was destroyed in the war of 1767. Its chedis and the remains of halls still tell that story.

Each site has a different character: Wat Mahathat is known for a Buddha head embraced by tree roots, Wat Phra Si Sanphet has three chedis in a row, and Wat Chaiwatthanaram stands beside the river. It suits visitors interested in history and architecture, or those who want to see both Bangkok’s Grand Palace and the former capital. The ruins are scattered through the modern city rather than enclosed within one park.
facts: Visit separate ruins · admission and travel are handled site by site

experiences.title: Traces of an international trading city
paragraphs: Ayutthaya was founded around 1350 and became Siam’s capital after Sukhothai. Its position surrounded by three rivers helped it grow into a centre of trade and diplomacy, but **the old city was destroyed in the war of 1767 and remained as ruins**.

The main sights are therefore not furnished palace interiors, but tall towers, collapsed halls and extensive temple grounds. The scale of the surviving structures gives you a sense of how large the former capital was. The old city of Ayutthaya is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage property.

experiences.title: The Buddha head at Wat Mahathat and the three chedis of a royal temple
paragraphs: Visit Wat Mahathat for the Buddha head embraced by tree roots, Wat Phra Si Sanphet for its three aligned chedis and former royal temple grounds, or Wat Chaiwatthanaram for a central tower and surrounding galleries beside the river.

At Wat Mahathat you can see the Buddha head among the roots; at Wat Phra Si Sanphet, large chedis and the remains of the royal temple. Add riverside Wat Chaiwatthanaram to compare the different layouts of towers and galleries. If you have visited Bangkok’s Grand Palace, you may also enjoy seeing what remains of the palace and temples in the old capital.

experiences.title: Palaces, temples and a living city
paragraphs: The ruins are scattered through parts of the present-day city where people still live. Choose the sites you want to visit and allow time to travel between them.
Active temples and ruins that have fallen into disrepair are both part of the area. Dress requirements, admission fees and access arrangements are not necessarily the same at every site.

experiences.title: Choose a pass for the sites you plan to visit
paragraphs: A combined pass does not cover every temple and museum in Ayutthaya. Check which sites are listed on the ticket and how long it is valid before planning your route.

rules.title: Plan around each site’s opening hours
paragraphs: Check the **visiting hours and last entry** separately for every site on your itinerary. If you want to visit at night, plan around the sites actually open to visitors on that date and their entry times.

sukhothai-historical-park.description: Sukhothai Historical Park has temples, chedis and Buddha images inside and outside the old city walls. Plan for separate central, northern and western zones, as their locations and tickets differ.
intro: Sukhothai Historical Park lets you explore temples, chedis and Buddha images inside and outside the walls of the old city. See Sukhothai architecture and Buddhist sculpture up close, from Wat Mahathat’s lotus-bud-shaped chedi to the large seated Phra Achana Buddha at Wat Si Chum.

It suits visitors who want to walk among historic temples and take in the architecture and scenery. The central, northern and western ruins are in separate zones with different tickets. Exploring several temples in the central zone offers a different experience from visiting the large Buddha beyond the city walls.
facts: 400 baht · check included zones and validity when buying

experiences.title: A lotus-bud chedi and a monumental seated Buddha
paragraphs: Wat Mahathat in the central zone was an important temple of the Sukhothai Kingdom. Its signature structure is the **lotus-bud-shaped chedi** rising at the centre. Buddha images and the remains of halls surround it, so you can explore them after seeing the main chedi.

Outside the walls, Wat Si Chum is home to the large seated Buddha known as Phra Achana. After exploring several temple remains in the central zone, you can travel beyond the walls to see the image up close. It is a good choice if you want to see Sukhothai Buddhist sculpture as well as chedis and buildings.

experiences.title: The old city seen on foot among the ruins
paragraphs: Sukhothai’s heritage is not limited to a single temple. Temples and chedis are scattered inside and outside the city walls, and together with the old cities of Si Satchanalai and Kamphaeng Phet they form a UNESCO World Heritage property. Which ruins you see depends on where you go, from Wat Si Sawai and Wat Sa Si inside the walls to Wat Si Chum outside them.

You can walk among temples such as Wat Si Sawai and Wat Sa Si within the walls, or get around by bicycle. Allow extra travel time for sites outside the walls. Rather than rushing through every zone, you can choose the temples that interest you and take in the architecture and surrounding scenery.

experiences.title: Zone tickets and Saturday evening lighting
paragraphs: The Tourism Authority’s August 2026 information distinguishes central, northern and western zone tickets as well as an all-zone ticket. Decide whether you plan to visit more than one zone or stay in one before choosing a ticket.

The park is listed as illuminated until 21:00 on Saturdays. However, this does not establish that every ruin and ticket booth offers the same evening admission. Check the day’s information for the zone you plan to visit.

rules.title: Check your ticket covers the northern ruins
paragraphs: If you want to see Wat Si Chum and its large Phra Achana Buddha, check that **the northern zone and entry to Wat Si Chum are included** in your ticket. A ticket for the central zone is different from one covering additional zones.

rules.title: A tram is an option if your group finds long walks difficult
paragraphs: If walking long distances between ruins is difficult, you can take the **on-site tram for 60 baht per person**. The Tourism Authority says it runs approximately every 15 minutes. The tram fare is separate from the central-zone admission ticket.
A bicycle lets you set your own pace. K-Shop on the eastern side lists a rate of **30 baht per day, payable after use**. Do not assume every nearby rental shop charges the same amount.

phimai-historical-park.description: Phimai Historical Park preserves a Khmer stone temple in Phimai, northeast of Nakhon Ratchasima. See Buddhist and Hindu carvings, layered petal-like roof details and the temple courtyard together.
intro: Phimai Historical Park is a place to see a Khmer stone temple in Nakhon Ratchasima, in northeastern Thailand. Walk from a bridge guarded by a seven-headed naga through gateways and galleries to the central sandstone sanctuary.

Look for carved Buddhas and Hindu deities, petal-like roof ornaments and a courtyard with ponds. The stone colours and carvings offer a different experience from temples with extensive gold decoration. Phimai was connected by a route to the old Khmer capital of Angkor, making it a compelling stop for anyone interested in Khmer-era temples in Thailand.

experiences.title: See stone Buddhas and deities up close
paragraphs: Phimai’s appeal lies not only in the overall scale of its Khmer stone sanctuary but also in its carved details. Its **carvings depict both Buddhas and Hindu deities**, letting you see how Buddhist and Hindu imagery appears in temple architecture.

The colour and material differ from the gold-rich temples of Bangkok. Walk around the towers, then look more closely at the small figures and patterns carved near the gateways. If you enjoy stone architecture, take time to study the surface and carvings.

experiences.title: A religious site connected to Angkor
paragraphs: A route once connected Phimai with Angkor, the old capital of the Khmer Empire. The region is now divided between Thailand and Cambodia, but religion and culture once travelled along this route.

The courtyard has four ponds, and layered roof decorations resemble overlapping flower petals. After seeing the central tower, look around the courtyard and gateways too. Accounts differ on the construction date and relationship with Angkor Wat, so it is difficult to describe Phimai simply as a copy of that temple.

experiences.title: A bridge guarded by a seven-headed naga
paragraphs: At the southern entrance, a sandstone bridge is carved with a **seven-headed naga**. Its long body forms the balustrade, with the heads fanning out at the end. Even as you pass through the gateway, take a moment to look at the rails and the lion carvings below the steps.

In Buddhist and Hindu cosmology, naga bridges are interpreted as paths connecting the human world with the heavens. The approach to the sanctuary carries religious meaning too. Cross the bridge towards the central tower and notice the carvings on the balustrade, gateway and steps.

experiences.title: Ruins restored by reassembling original stone
paragraphs: The central sanctuary was built from light sandstone. Other structures, including red stone towers and galleries, also remain around it. The layout of gateways and galleries around the central sanctuary lets you compare the colour and texture of the stone used in different buildings.

The site combines ancient remains with modern restoration. In the 1960s, Thailand’s Fine Arts Department worked with France to restore the central sanctuary by fitting scattered architectural pieces back into their original positions. This is a conserved historic site, not a newly built themed attraction.

accessSections.title: Distinguish Phimai from central Korat
paragraphs: The destination is **Phimai Historical Park, Nai Mueang, Phimai**. It is listed as about 59 km from central Korat, so plan separately for the return journey.

phanom-rung-historical-park.description: Phanom Rung Historical Park is a Khmer temple complex on an ancient volcanic hill in Buriram. Follow a long stone walkway, steps and gateways through the site’s architecture.
intro: Phanom Rung Historical Park is a Khmer temple complex on an ancient volcanic hill in Buriram. Follow the long stone walkway and steps through its gateways and stone architecture; from the upper area, you can also look out over the surrounding fields.

It suits visitors who want to climb past a stone temple and take in the fields below. The site is also known for sunlight passing through all 15 doorways in a line. This does not happen every day, but on an ordinary visit you can still walk the long approach and see the doorways and sanctuary aligned in perspective. If anyone in your group has difficulty with steps, ask in advance which routes are available.
facts: 150 baht combined ticket with Muang Tam ruins listed

experiences.title: Khmer architecture that made a volcanic hill a sacred place
paragraphs: Phanom Rung means “large hill” in Khmer. It is a **temple built on an ancient volcano**, first associated with Hinduism and later also with Buddhism. Follow the long stone walkway and steps through a series of gateways to reach the temple on higher ground.

Rather than seeing a building as soon as you enter, you approach the temple along a path, steps and gateways. The stone architecture and surrounding fields make this a good choice if you enjoy walking through historic buildings and taking in the landscape more than visiting indoor exhibits.

experiences.title: Doorways aligned to let sunlight pass through
paragraphs: Phanom Rung has **15 doorways arranged in a line**. When the sun’s direction matches their alignment, sunlight passes through from one doorway to the next. Even at other times, you can look through the passage and see the doorways layered in perspective.

The special light effect depends on the date, weather and access conditions. For a regular visit, focus on the stone temple and hilltop scenery. If seeing the alignment is essential, you will need to plan around the dates announced for that year’s event.

rules.title: Plan for steps and movement on a hill
paragraphs: Reaching the temple involves a stone walkway and steps. If you are travelling with someone who finds steps difficult, first check **which routes and parts of the site are actually accessible**.

siam-amazing-park.description: Siam Amazing Park combines amusement rides and water attractions in Bangkok. The rides area and water park have different hours, so plan your order if you want to visit both.
intro: Siam Amazing Park is a place to enjoy rides and water attractions on the same day in Bangkok. Water World has a large wave pool, a lazy river and fast slides, while the rides range from the Vortex roller coaster to smaller attractions for children.

Ride a roller coaster with friends who enjoy fast attractions, or spend time at the smaller rides and pools with children. If you plan to do both, arrange your day around the different opening hours of the two areas. Tickets also differ in which areas they include.

experiences.title: A relaxed wave-pool day or fast water slides
paragraphs: Water World has a **large wave pool**. Play in the pool as artificial waves roll in, or float along the Flowing Pool on an inner tube. It is an option for enjoying water attractions during a Bangkok trip without travelling to the coast.

If you like fast slides, try the Speed Slide and Super Spiral. Families with young children can look for Siam Lagoon and its family water-play area with mini slides. **Some areas require children to be accompanied by an adult**, so check the conditions at each attraction before letting a child ride alone.

experiences.title: Enjoy water attractions and roller coasters in one day
paragraphs: The park has an amusement area as well as a water park. On the Vortex, you sit in a suspended seat with your feet off the floor as the ride passes through twists; the Giant Drop takes you down from a height. If your friends like fast rides, you may want to set aside more time for this area.

For young children, look for Small World, which has attractions such as a mini boat ride and small carousel. Decide whether you also want to ride attractions as well as enjoy the water park, then choose a ticket that includes the areas you want.

experiences.title: Food and architecture at Bangkok World outside the park
paragraphs: Outside the park, **Bangkok World** has recreated old Bangkok-style buildings, food and craft shops. Browse regional products and handmade goods from around Thailand, or stop for something to eat.

These are recreated buildings, not original historic structures from Bangkok’s old town. Bangkok World is a separate area outside the water park, so do not assume it is included with a water-park ticket. It is a place for companions who are skipping the fast rides to see the architecture or enjoy food.

rules.title: Outside food and drinks are not allowed
paragraphs: **You cannot bring outside food or drinks into the park.** Leave them out when packing for the water park. You can store your belongings in one of the paid lockers listed below.

rules.title: You need your ticket and a hand stamp to re-enter
paragraphs: The operator says re-entry is allowed with a **valid ticket and a hand stamp**. If you plan to leave the park temporarily, get the re-entry mark before you go out.

rules.title: Height and health restrictions vary by ride
paragraphs: Entry to the park does not mean every ride is suitable for you. Follow the **height, weight, health and accompanying-adult requirements** posted at each attraction.

dream-world.description: Dream World is an amusement park in Pathum Thani, north of Bangkok. It has rides and separate attractions such as Snow Town, and the experiences included depend on the ticket you choose.
intro: Dream World is an amusement park in Pathum Thani, north of Bangkok. Alongside rides such as Sky Coaster and Viking, you can visit Snow Town for indoor sledding below zero, or see photo spots inspired by a giant’s house and storybook settings.

Ride coasters and spinning attractions with friends, or enjoy photo spots and snow play with children. You can spend the day moving between rides and storybook-inspired photo settings. Keep in mind that admission-only tickets cover different things from packages that include rides and Snow Town.

experiences.title: A day of coasters and spinning rides with friends
paragraphs: The park has fast coasters and spinning rides such as Sky Coaster, Black Hole Coaster, Viking and Hurricane. **There are also rides for children.** If you are visiting with a child, choose attractions that meet the child’s height requirements and any rules about accompanying adults.

Spend the day talking with your group about which rides to try. It suits visitors who want to add a full amusement-park day to a Bangkok itinerary centred on temples and shopping, or friends who want to ride several attractions. Actual access is subject to each ride’s height and accompanying-person requirements.

experiences.title: Go sledding at Snow Town
paragraphs: Snow Town is an indoor attraction below zero, with a **large sledding slope** and snowy scenery. You can step inside for snow play after riding attractions outdoors in the heat. If you are travelling with a child who cannot ride coasters, Snow Town is another activity to try together.

Snow Town is not included with every ticket. Admission, rides and Snow Town may be covered differently by each product. Even when choosing the Trip.com Super Visa above, check the booking screen to see whether Snow Town is included. Base your choice on the listed inclusions rather than assuming every experience is covered.

experiences.title: Take photos at the Giant’s House and storybook settings
paragraphs: The park also has **the Giant’s House and a cable car**, Love Garden and Photopia. Photopia has settings for photos, including an upside-down castle, a hobbit house and a fairytale princess castle. Companions who are not riding fast attractions can explore the settings and take photos too.
The Color of the World parade also takes place on weekends. Unlike the photo settings, it is not something you can see every day. If you want to watch it, plan your visit for a weekend.

rules.title: Choose a ticket that is valid for your group
paragraphs: When buying, check **whether the product is available to foreign visitors and which of admission, rides and Snow Town it includes**. Discounts for specific customers, such as a promotion for holders of a Thai bank card, are only available if you meet the stated eligibility requirements.

andamanda-phuket.description: Andamanda Phuket is a water park themed around Thai mythology and the Andaman region. Its wave pool, slides and children’s areas make it a day out for families and friends.
intro: Andamanda Phuket is a water park themed around Thai mythology and the Andaman region. Enjoy different kinds of water play across the wave pool, slides and children’s areas, whether you are visiting with family or friends.

Try the fast slides with friends or spend time with your family in the children’s areas. The Village is themed around a Thai market, while Tropical Beach serves seafood, giving you places to stop for a meal and a break.

experiences.title: Water attractions inspired by Thai mythology and the Andaman landscape
paragraphs: Andamanda draws its themes from Thai mythology, Phuket’s Sino-Portuguese architecture and the limestone scenery of the Andaman region. Move between the wave pool, slides and children’s areas to enjoy both the water attractions and the park’s themed details.

Plan a day with family in the children’s areas or head for the slides with friends. Height, weight and health requirements vary by ride, so check the restrictions at each entrance before choosing what to try.

experiences.title: Andaman scenery at the wave pool and island-inspired decor
paragraphs: Andamanda Bay has a wave pool and an area designed to look like a sandy beach, along with a Koh Tapu island-shaped feature. You can enjoy the water while looking at **a park landscape inspired by the Andaman’s limestone islands**, without going out to an actual island.

For fast attractions, look for Dragon’s Drop, a capsule-style ride with a trapdoor floor; Eagle Flyer, which runs up and down a wall; and Racing Naga, where you race a friend down side by side. Each water slide has a different ride, so you can choose what suits you.

experiences.title: Water-play areas for children and families
paragraphs: Little Reef has small slides, while Wonder Waterland has interactive structures that splash water. At Atoll Adventures, **water pours from a large tipping bucket**. These children’s areas are a way to enjoy water play with a child who is not ready for the larger slides.

There is also the tube ride Rolling Ripples and a raft-style attraction for families. Height, weight and adult-accompaniment rules differ between children’s areas and larger slides; park admission for the whole family does not mean everyone can ride every attraction together.

experiences.title: What to bring for swimming
paragraphs: Wear suitable swimwear. Clothing with metal decorations or zippers may be restricted on rides. Children who need diapers should wear swim diapers.
It is best to leave valuables in a rented locker. If your booking includes a towel, locker or shuttle, check the inclusions before packing or booking those items again.

rules.title: Do not leave children unattended
paragraphs: **Children must not be left alone without a guardian.** The park strongly recommends that visitors **under 18 be accompanied by an adult**. This is a general park recommendation; any mandatory adult-accompaniment rule posted at an individual ride must also be followed.

rules.title: Restrictions on food and cameras
paragraphs: **Outside food and drinks are prohibited.** Handheld cameras cannot be used on rides, and photography is not allowed in restrooms or changing areas.

rules.title: Attractions may close in severe weather
paragraphs: Pools and rides may temporarily stop operating in severe weather. Follow the safety team’s instructions and updates on operations and queues on the day.

ramayana-water-park.description: Ramayana Water Park, south of Pattaya, has slides and pools for adults and children. Plan a visit around both thrill rides and water play with children.
intro: Ramayana Water Park, south of Pattaya, has a range of slides and pools. Choose from attractions with different levels of intensity, such as the Aqua Coaster with its rising and falling tube, the trapdoor Freefall, a children’s splash area and a lazy river.

Ride in a shared tube with friends or race side by side on the Mat Racer. Families with children can centre their visit on the children’s areas and pools. You can also take a break on the sun loungers provided between rides.
facts: Visitors **under 15 must be accompanied by an adult**

experiences.title: Shared tubes and a slide with a trapdoor
paragraphs: If you want to ride with friends, try attractions such as the Aqua Coaster, where the tube moves up and down, or Python and Aquaconda, which take larger tubes through enclosed passages and bends. **Mat Racer** sends riders down parallel lanes together.

For a stronger drop, try the trapdoor Freefall or Aqua Loop, which circles around. These rides have different characteristics. Height, weight and health restrictions vary, and meeting the height rule for the affiliated ticket listed above does not mean you are eligible for every individual ride.

experiences.title: From a children’s splash area to the lazy river
paragraphs: Hanuman Splash has multiple slides and a large tipping bucket. Mermaid Lagoon and Lanka Town are areas for young children. If a child is not ready for fast rides, enjoy the water together in one of these sections.

**On the lazy river, float on a tube past caves and water features.** The wave pool lets you play as waves roll in. Spend the day moving between slides and pools with friends, or stay in the children’s areas with your family.

experiences.title: A day of slides and pools
paragraphs: A regular admission ticket provides access to slides and pools during operating hours. Sun loungers, tubes, mats and life jackets are also available. Tubes and life jackets are provided first come, first served, so your preferred size may be unavailable or you may have to wait.
Children under 15 must stay with a responsible adult. The rules for using flotation aids made for children in a pool differ from the rules for taking them onto adult slides.

experiences.title: Wristband payments and rental items
paragraphs: Bars and stalls in the park primarily use cashless payments via the QR code on your wristband. Top up at designated locations and get the remaining balance refunded at a shop before leaving.

**Towels cost 150 baht each**; lockers cost **169 baht for medium and 259 baht for large**. Tubes and life jackets are provided free, first come, first served. If you need a refund for your wristband balance, complete it before the shop refund deadline of 17:45.

experiences.title: Operations and compensation in rainy weather
paragraphs: Rain alone does not automatically qualify you for a refund. Compensation depends on how long the safety team officially suspends operations of the pools and rides continuously.

If pool and ride operations are suspended **for more than 2 consecutive hours, you may receive a 50% discount voucher for a future visit**; **if they are suspended for more than 3 hours, you may receive an admission ticket for a future visit**. Each is valid for 6 months after issue. **Neither option is a cash refund**, and separate shutdown periods are not added together if operations resume in between.

rules.title: A new ticket is required to re-enter
paragraphs: One ticket covers one entry and exit. **If you leave, you need a new ticket to re-enter**, so bring everything you need with you.

rules.title: Outside food is allowed only by exception
paragraphs: Outside food and drinks are generally prohibited. Exceptions listed include **baby food and special diets supported by medical documentation**.

rules.title: Follow camera rules for each ride
paragraphs: Cameras cannot be used on body slides. Tube slides have conditions for action cameras secured with a designated strap, and **selfie sticks are prohibited on all rides**.

columbia-pictures-aquaverse.description: Columbia Pictures Aquaverse in Chonburi is a water park themed around movie characters and scenes. Enjoy areas inspired by Hotel Transylvania, Jumanji and Ghostbusters, among others.
intro: Columbia Pictures Aquaverse in Chonburi is a water park themed around movie characters and scenes. Explore areas inspired by Hotel Transylvania, Jumanji and Ghostbusters while enjoying the water attractions.

If you like Ghostbusters, Jumanji or Hotel Transylvania, enjoy water attractions in areas inspired by scenes from the films. Ride slides with friends or explore character-themed splash areas with children. Go-karts and mini golf are also available, but whether they are included depends on the ticket product.

experiences.title: Turn a Ghostbusters ghost hunt into water rides
paragraphs: In the Ghostbusters area, **Proton Stream** takes you on a raft-style ride into the Stay Puft Water Dome. Ghost Trap Adventure is a fast water coaster, while Slimer Speed Racer is a set of side-by-side tube slides. Look for your favourite characters and try rides with different formats.

Part of the fun is spotting the ghost-catching gear and characters in the ride themes. With a friend who enjoys the films, compare how scenes and names from the movies have been reimagined as water attractions.

experiences.title: Jumanji’s jungle and Hotel Transylvania splash area
paragraphs: The Jumanji area has **Viper, Jungle Stampede and Jaguar Mountain**. Hotel Transylvania is an Aquaplay area with several slides and water-play structures, making it a place for families who enjoy the film’s characters.
A child’s ticket does not mean the child can ride every attraction in this area. Follow the **height and adult-accompaniment requirements** for each ride, including in character-themed areas.

experiences.title: Spend time at the lazy river and large wave pool
paragraphs: Swallow Falls lazy river takes you on a tube through a setting themed around a movie’s imagined world filled with food. There is also a large wave pool and an outdoor performance space, giving you other ways to enjoy the water between slides.
Shows and events may take place on the outdoor stage. The schedule varies by date, so the same show is not available every day.

experiences.title: Treat go-karts and mini golf as separate activities
paragraphs: At Gran Turismo Racing Club, you can drive go-karts themed around the film and game. Emoji Mini Golf offers a round of golf against character backdrops. These are options for groups who want to do something beyond the water attractions.
**Whether go-karts and mini golf are included depends on the admission ticket you choose.** Also distinguish the affiliated product’s Wednesday exclusion from the park’s own operating days.

intro: Vana Nava Water Jungle is a jungle-themed water park in Nong Kae, Hua Hin. Its attractions include a lazy river that passes trees, caves and bridges, children’s splash areas, and adult slides such as the Abyss, which drops into a giant funnel, and Boomerango, which climbs a wall.

Play among fountains and small slides with children, or share a large tube on a fast ride with friends. The park also has a surf simulator, ropes and climbing facilities, so you can combine water attractions with other activities. Conditions vary by attraction, and not every activity is included with every admission ticket.

experiences.title: A lazy river through a jungle and family splash areas
paragraphs: On the lazy river, float on a tube along **a waterway that passes trees, caves, bridges and islands**. Unlike a fast slide that takes you down in one run, this attraction lets you drift along and take in the scenery.

Kiddie Cove has fountains, play structures and children’s slides. Rain Fortress has water-play structures and several slides, and Bana Wonderland is also a children’s area. If you are visiting with young children, enjoy these spaces instead of the larger slides.

experiences.title: The Abyss drops into a giant funnel
paragraphs: **The Abyss sends a multi-person tube into a giant funnel, where it circles around.** Sharing a tube with your group is part of the experience. Its ride feels different from Boomerango, which climbs up and down a high wall.

The park also has a surf simulator and climbing and rope facilities. Between slides, you can try balancing on the water or climbing a wall. Activity-specific ride requirements and ticket inclusions apply separately.

experiences.title: Surf and climbing activities that put you in motion
paragraphs: At Surf Zone, **the Double FlowRider is an artificial wave machine with fast-flowing water**. Instead of sliding down in a tube, you try to keep your balance on the moving water. You can do this inside the park without going to the beach.

If you enjoy active challenges, look for the rope course and climbing wall. A child’s admission ticket does not automatically cover every facility. Follow the **height, weight and health restrictions** for each activity.

wat-traimit.description: Wat Traimit is the Golden Buddha temple near Bangkok’s Chinatown. The main visit is to the golden seated Buddha in its hall, and you can continue on foot into Yaowarat afterwards.
intro: Wat Traimit is a temple near Bangkok’s Chinatown where you can see the Golden Buddha. Knowing the story that the statue, once concealed beneath plaster, was revealed when it was moved makes the golden image in the hall all the more striking.

Explore the hall housing the Golden Buddha and the large mondop building, then walk to the streets and restaurants of Yaowarat. It makes a good day out for visitors interested in Buddhist art and the story of the statue, with time for a meal and a stroll in Chinatown too.
facts: 100 baht · check whether museum entry is included

experiences.title: The Golden Buddha revealed from beneath plaster
paragraphs: Wat Traimit’s Buddha image was once covered in plaster, concealing the gold inside. According to the story, the plaster cracked while the image was being moved, revealing a golden Buddha. It was not always displayed in gold as it is today.
Take time to look at the seated image’s face, hands and posture in the hall.

experiences.title: The mondop that houses the Golden Buddha
paragraphs: The Golden Buddha’s formal name is Phra Phuttha Maha Suwanna Patimakon. Explore the large mondop hall that houses it too. Inside, see the golden seated image; outside, look at the building constructed to enshrine the statue.
The worship area housing the Golden Buddha and the museum are separate areas for visitors. If you want to visit the museum as well, check whether it is included in the ticket you are buying.

experiences.title: Continue from the temple to Yaowarat
paragraphs: The temple is near the edge of Chinatown. After seeing the temple architecture and Buddha image during the day, you can continue on foot to Yaowarat’s shops and restaurants. Set aside time for the statue as well as a meal in the neighbourhood.

Even if you are mainly interested in Chinatown’s evening atmosphere, plan your temple visit around its daytime opening hours. Arrive before your evening meal so you can explore the temple first and experience both a place of worship and the neighbourhood streets in one area.

rules.title: Suggested clothing for a temple visit
paragraphs: For all visitors, we recommend wearing clothing that **covers the shoulders and knees**. A sleeved top with long trousers or a skirt that covers the knees is a good choice. Please dress modestly rather than wearing a sleeveless top or short bottoms.

accessSections.title: Getting there from Hua Lamphong MRT station

wat-benchamabophit.description: Wat Benchamabophit is a marble temple in Bangkok’s Dusit district. See the hall built with marble imported from Italy and the gallery lined with Buddha images.
intro: At Wat Benchamabophit, light marble and stained glass sit beneath a Thai-style roof. The temple in Bangkok’s Dusit district is known as the Marble Temple because marble imported from Italy was used in its construction.

After admiring the marble exterior and Thai-style roof, look inside the main hall at the Phra Buddha Chinnarat image and the bronze Buddhas lining the outer gallery. The pale stone, coloured windows, golden Buddha and gallery columns each have a different character, making this a good place to enjoy architecture and Buddhist art together.

experiences.title: Italian marble beneath a Thai-style roof
paragraphs: The temple was designed by Prince Narisara Nuwattiwong during the reign of Rama V. Italian Carrara marble and stained glass were added to traditional Thai architecture, creating light surfaces and colours unlike brick ruins or wooden halls.

From a distance, the symmetrical rooflines and halls stand out first. Up close, look separately at the stone surfaces and windows. Visitors who enjoy architecture can compare traditional building forms with materials brought from Europe in one place.

experiences.title: A bronze replica based on the Phra Buddha Chinnarat
paragraphs: The golden Buddha image in the main hall is a bronze replica based on the Phra Buddha Chinnarat. The original is enshrined at Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat in Phitsanulok. Here in Bangkok, you can see the form of the Chinnarat image through a separately made statue.

Notice the contrast between the blue-toned interior and the golden image behind it. After seeing the light marble outside, step into the main hall to experience the different colours and atmosphere inside.

experiences.title: The outer gallery lined with bronze Buddha images
paragraphs: Bronze Buddha images also line the gallery around the hall. Rather than stopping at the main building, walk around the gallery to see the images and architecture together. The repeated figures between the columns are another feature of the temple.

After seeing the bright marble exterior, continue to the Phra Buddha Chinnarat image in the main hall and the outer gallery. Look closely at the statues, then walk through the gallery and take in the columns and roof. The main hall is listed as open until 17:00, so leave enough time for the interior visit.

rules.title: Suggested clothing for a temple visit
paragraphs: For all visitors, we recommend wearing clothing that **covers the shoulders and knees**. A sleeved top with long trousers or a skirt that covers the knees is a good choice. Please dress modestly rather than wearing a sleeveless top or short bottoms.

accessSections.title: Travel by road after taking the BTS
paragraphs: The Tourism Authority describes reaching the temple by road from **Phaya Thai BTS station**. Enter Wat Benchamabophit, Dusit as the destination. The temple is not directly beside the station.

wat-suthat.type: Temple with murals, Buddha images and a separate museum
wat-suthat.title: Wat Suthat and the Giant Swing: Murals, Carved Doors and Museum | ThaiLiveNow
wat-suthat.description: Wat Suthat is an old-city Bangkok temple near the Giant Swing. Highlights include the hall murals, carved wooden doors and the Si Sakyamuni Buddha. The large red swing outside is a separate structure.
intro: In old Bangkok, Wat Suthat is where you can pass the large red Giant Swing and discover murals and carved wooden doors inside the temple halls. Look at the Si Sakyamuni Buddha on its high pedestal and the paintings on the walls for details beyond the temple’s street-facing appearance.

After taking a photo by the large swing in front of the temple, set aside time for the interior, where you can see Buddhist paintings and woodcarving. If you plan to visit the museum too, check its schedule separately because its opening days and hours differ from those of the temple.
facts: Friday, Saturday, Sunday and public holidays, 09:30–16:00 · 200 baht

experiences.title: The Si Sakyamuni Buddha on a high pedestal
paragraphs: Si Sakyamuni is a large bronze Buddha image made during the Sukhothai period. The image is about 8 m tall and stands on a pedestal about 6 m high. Step into the hall and look up at the Buddha to take in the scale of both the image and its pedestal.

After seeing the red Giant Swing outside the temple, go into the hall to see the Buddha on its high pedestal and the wall paintings. Rather than just taking a street photo and moving on, set aside time to look up at the large image and take in the murals at a slower pace.

experiences.title: Murals and intricately carved wooden doors
paragraphs: Construction of the temple began in the early 19th century during the reign of Rama I. It is known for its murals and intricately carved wooden doors, so the walls and entrances are part of the visit as well as the Buddha image. Take time to look at both the large paintings and the smaller carvings.

Near the doors, examine the patterns carved into the wood; inside, look at the murals depicting a series of scenes. Even if Buddhist art is new to you, you can take in the temple by following the fine lines of the carving and then looking across the wall paintings.

experiences.title: The red swing outside and the separate museum
paragraphs: The Sao Chingcha, or Giant Swing, in front of the temple consists of red pillars and a crossbar. It is a separate structure outside the temple. After seeing the swing, enter the paid temple area if you also want to explore inside.

The museum has separate hours on Fridays, Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays. Even if the temple stays open into the evening, that does not mean the museum is open too. Check the **visiting areas covered by the temple and museum tickets**, and plan around the museum schedule if you want to see the exhibits.

rules.title: Check the separate temple and museum tickets
paragraphs: Admission for the temple and museum is listed separately. If you plan to visit both, check the **areas covered** on each ticket at the venue before buying.

rules.title: Suggested clothing for a temple visit
paragraphs: For all visitors, we recommend wearing clothing that **covers the shoulders and knees**. A sleeved top with long trousers or a skirt that covers the knees is a good choice. Please dress modestly rather than wearing a sleeveless top or short bottoms.
