wat-paknam.name: Wat Paknam Phasi Charoen
wat-paknam.thai: วัดปากน้ำภาษีเจริญ
wat-paknam.type: Temple with a giant Buddha and an interior chedi ceiling painting
wat-paknam.title: Wat Paknam: Giant Golden Buddha and Chedi Ceiling Art in Bangkok | ThaiLiveNow
wat-paknam.description: Wat Paknam is a royal temple in Bangkok’s Phasi Charoen district. It is known for the large golden Buddha outside and a ceiling painting inside the upper level of the chedi.
intro: Wat Paknam is a royal temple in Bangkok’s Phasi Charoen district, known for its large golden seated Buddha and colourful ceiling painting. Outside, the towering Buddha image makes an impression; inside the upper level of the chedi, a ceiling painting depicts the life of the Buddha.

Go up to the chedi’s upper level to see the ornate ceiling, a different experience from viewing the golden Buddha outside. The temple has a history of monastic education and meditation. After photographing the large Buddha, take time to look at the images of the Buddha’s life. It is a good visit for companions interested in Buddhist art both inside and outdoors.

experiences.title: The large golden seated Buddha completed in 2021
paragraphs: The large golden seated Buddha outside the temple was completed in 2021. This bronze image is 69 m tall and sits in a meditative posture. It is large enough to see from around the temple grounds. First take in its overall form from a distance, then move closer to look at its face and seated posture.

From farther away, view the Buddha together with the temple surroundings; up close, take in the seated figure and hall separately. The monumental image outside and the paintings indoors are different highlights in different spaces.

experiences.title: Ceiling paintings depicting the life of the Buddha
paragraphs: On the upper level of the chedi, you can see ceiling paintings depicting the life of the Buddha. After seeing the large golden image outside, go inside and look up at the paintings. You can explore Buddhist art in the temple interior as well as the scale of the Buddha image.

Please be considerate of worship and religious practice while viewing the paintings. Follow on-site information about which upper areas are open. If anyone in your group needs to use stairs or a lift, it may be helpful to ask about the route before your visit.

experiences.title: An Ayutthaya-era temple and a tradition of meditation
paragraphs: Wat Paknam is a royal temple whose history dates to the Ayutthaya period. It is also known for training monks in Pali and the meditation teachings of Phra Mongkhon Thepmuni, known as Luang Pho Sot. The newly built large Buddha stands within a longer history of education and religious practice.

Separate from tourist visits, Dhamma talks and meditation programs are held at Charoen Vipassana Hall. **Meditation and Dhamma talks are free and conducted in Thai.** White clothing is recommended for participants; it is not a requirement for every visitor. If you would like to join, check the schedule and conditions separately.

rules.title: Be considerate of worship and meditation
paragraphs: When viewing the ceiling paintings or taking photos, be considerate of worshippers praying and of areas used for religious practice. If you want to join meditation, check the program schedule and participation conditions separately from the general visitor information.

rules.title: Suggested clothing for a temple visit
paragraphs: For all visitors, we recommend wearing clothing that **covers the shoulders and knees**. A sleeved top with long trousers or a skirt that covers the knees is a good choice. Please dress modestly rather than wearing a sleeveless top or short bottoms.

wat-mahathat-ayutthaya.thai: วัดมหาธาตุ พระนครศรีอยุธยา
wat-mahathat-ayutthaya.type: Ayutthaya temple ruins with a Buddha head and brick remains
wat-mahathat-ayutthaya.title: Wat Mahathat Ayutthaya: Buddha Head in Tree Roots and Brick Ruins | ThaiLiveNow
wat-mahathat-ayutthaya.description: Wat Mahathat in Ayutthaya is a temple ruin known for a Buddha head embraced by tree roots. The grounds also contain collapsed brick walls, hall foundations and headless Buddha images.
intro: At Wat Mahathat in Ayutthaya, tree roots embrace the face of a sandstone Buddha. The site is known for this single image, but looking around reveals a large temple complex, including headless Buddha images, collapsed brick walls and the foundations of halls.

After photographing the Buddha head, explore the collapsed brick walls, hall foundations and surviving carvings. It suits visitors who want to photograph the landscape where trees and ruins of the old capital meet. Search specifically for the Ayutthaya ruins to distinguish this site from temples of the same name in Bangkok and Sukhothai, then take time to look at the places where buildings once stood.

experiences.title: A sandstone Buddha face embraced by roots
paragraphs: The Buddha head that represents the temple is made of sandstone. Tree roots embrace the face, which remains without its body or hall. Look closely at the roots running around the face, then step back to take in the tree and Buddha image together.

The Tourism Authority tells the story that the head fell beneath a tree during the war. Rather than assert precisely how it came to rest in its current position, take a moment to appreciate the Buddha and tree as they appear together today, after many years.

experiences.title: Temple ruins with brick walls and headless Buddha images
paragraphs: The temple is said to have once had a chedi with a golden spire before becoming a ruin after the war. Today, headless Buddha images, hall floors and collapsed walls remain. Although the buildings are no longer intact, you can walk among the image locations and surviving foundations to picture the scale of the former temple.

After photographing the Buddha head, look at the direction of the brickwork and where the Buddha images were placed. Even without roofs and walls, the foundations and arrangement of carvings show traces of a religious space. It suits visitors interested in historic architecture and ruins.

experiences.title: Gold artifacts found beneath the ruins
paragraphs: Gold Buddha images, jewellery and other objects were found during restoration in 1956. The excavated items are listed as being on display at Chao Sam Phraya National Museum. There was once a space beneath the brick ruins where valuable objects were kept.

Explore the temple grounds and architecture at Wat Mahathat, then visit Chao Sam Phraya National Museum separately to see the excavated objects. If you plan to see multiple ruins, check the sites included and the validity period of tickets sold on site. The price and current conditions of an older combined pass may have changed.

rules.title: Check which ruins your ticket covers and its validity
paragraphs: If you plan to visit several ruins, check the **sites included and validity period** of tickets sold on site before choosing. Individual admission to Wat Mahathat and a combined pass for multiple ruins may cover different areas.

wat-phra-si-sanphet.name: Wat Phra Si Sanphet
wat-phra-si-sanphet.thai: วัดพระศรีสรรเพชญ์
wat-phra-si-sanphet.type: Royal temple ruins in the former Ayutthaya palace
wat-phra-si-sanphet.title: Wat Phra Si Sanphet: Three Royal Chedis in Ayutthaya | ThaiLiveNow
wat-phra-si-sanphet.description: Wat Phra Si Sanphet was the royal temple connected to Ayutthaya’s former palace. Its three aligned chedis and the remaining building foundations give a sense of the temple’s scale within the old royal palace.
intro: At Wat Phra Si Sanphet, three large bell-shaped chedis stand in an east–west line. This royal temple was connected to the former palace of Ayutthaya. Walk among the surviving chedis and hall foundations to appreciate the scale of a place where royal ceremonies took place.

Each chedi enshrines the remains of an Ayutthaya king. The extensive foundations of halls used for royal ceremonies also remain, reflecting a temple built for royal remembrance and religious rites. After viewing the three aligned towers, follow the foundations to see where the halls once stood.

experiences.title: Three chedis for three kings
paragraphs: The eastern, central and western chedis each enshrine the remains of a king: Borommatrailokkanat, Borommarachathirat III and Ramathibodi II. The three bell-shaped towers stand side by side as memorials to the kings.

From a distance, take in the arrangement of the three structures; up close, look at each rounded body and its rising spire. The Fine Arts Department explains that smaller surrounding chedis also enshrine members of the royal family.

experiences.title: From former royal palace to royal ceremonial site
paragraphs: This site was originally a royal palace. After King Borommatrailokkanat moved the palace north, the former palace grounds became a temple used for royal religious and state ceremonies. An oath of allegiance to the king and royal family was also held here.

The halls and palace buildings are not all intact today. Look at the foundations and the direction of the towers to picture the layout of the temple beside the palace. This is a site from a different dynasty and city from Wat Phra Kaew at the present-day Bangkok Grand Palace.

experiences.title: The lost golden standing Buddha and its story at Wat Pho
paragraphs: The royal hall once housed a standing Buddha covered in gold, Phra Si Sanphet. The Fine Arts Department explains that when Ayutthaya fell, the gold was stripped away and the bronze core remained; King Rama I later moved it to Bangkok’s Wat Pho, where it was enshrined inside a chedi.

There is no large golden Buddha remaining at the hall foundations today. Picture the former hall as you look at the place where the image was enshrined and the building base. If you also visit Wat Pho in Bangkok, you can see the chedi where the damaged statue was re-enshrined. The history of the same Buddha connects the two cities.

rules.title: Choose a combined pass based on current sales conditions
paragraphs: The Fine Arts Department’s 2026 event information lists Phra Si Sanphet and the palace as one item in a combined pass. Event hours should not be assumed to match regular opening hours, so plan using the information for your visit date and tickets currently on sale.

wat-chaiwatthanaram.thai: วัดไชยวัฒนาราม
wat-chaiwatthanaram.type: Khmer-style temple ruins beside the river
wat-chaiwatthanaram.title: Wat Chaiwatthanaram: Riverside Khmer-Style Temple Ruins in Ayutthaya | ThaiLiveNow
wat-chaiwatthanaram.description: Wat Chaiwatthanaram is a temple ruin on the west side of the Chao Phraya River in Ayutthaya. See Khmer-influenced architecture arranged around a large central tower, surrounding towers and galleries.
intro: On the west side of the Chao Phraya River in Ayutthaya, Wat Chaiwatthanaram is a temple ruin where the large central tower and surrounding towers come into view together. Its clear arrangement of towers and galleries makes it a good place to see the influence of Khmer architecture.

Walk along the surrounding towers and galleries and view the central tower from different angles. Up close, take in the brick structure and ornamentation; from farther away, see how the towers overlap. It is a relaxed visit for companions who want to photograph Ayutthaya’s temple architecture.

experiences.title: A temple arranged around a large central tower
paragraphs: A main tower about 35 m tall stands at the centre of a square compound, with four towers around it. A gallery runs along the perimeter, and towers in eight directions surround the compound. Step back to see at a glance how the large central tower and surrounding structures are arranged.

The layout, influenced by Khmer architecture, is also compared with Angkor Wat. The large central tower with smaller towers around it represents Mount Meru, the centre of the Buddhist cosmos. You can take in both the visible arrangement and its religious meaning.

experiences.title: A king’s temple built in memory of his mother
paragraphs: The temple is said to have been built in 1630 by King Prasat Thong in memory of his late mother. It was later used for royal memorial ceremonies. The impressive towers that remain today have this royal commemorative history behind them.

The temple was burned and abandoned during the war of 1767, then restored in later years before becoming the ruins seen today. The Tourism Authority also describes restoration work in 1987. Walk among the surviving towers and galleries to take in the old temple’s layout and architecture.

experiences.title: A riverside view with overlapping towers
paragraphs: The way the towers overlap in a photograph changes with your position. First look closely at the brickwork, then step back to see the outlines of several towers together. Take your time finding a composition that you like if you are travelling with someone who enjoys architectural photography.

At dusk, the outlines of the central tower and surrounding towers overlap in the view. Visiting hours are listed as **08:00–18:00**, so if you plan to arrive around dusk, schedule your visit using both the sunset time and the closing time for that date.

wat-ratchaburana-ayutthaya.thai: วัดราชบูรณะ พระนครศรีอยุธยา
wat-ratchaburana-ayutthaya.type: Temple ruins with a prang in Ayutthaya
wat-ratchaburana-ayutthaya.title: Wat Ratchaburana Ayutthaya: Prang, Temple Ruins and Royal Artifacts | ThaiLiveNow
wat-ratchaburana-ayutthaya.description: Wat Ratchaburana in Ayutthaya is a temple ruin north of Wat Mahathat. Its large prang surrounded by galleries and the remains of halls offer a look at the layout of an early Ayutthaya temple.
intro: At Wat Ratchaburana in Ayutthaya, see a large prang surrounded by galleries and the remains of halls. North of Wat Mahathat, the site preserves the story of a temple built after a royal succession struggle and gold artifacts found inside its tower.

Explore the remaining halls and large tower at the ruins, then visit Chao Sam Phraya National Museum separately to see the excavated objects. If you are interested in both architecture and royal craftsmanship, set aside time for both places. This Ayutthaya site, distinct from the Bangkok temple of the same name, offers a look at the scale of an old royal temple and the artifacts once kept inside it.

experiences.title: A royal temple built in memory of two elder brothers
paragraphs: The dynastic chronicles say that King Borommarachathirat II had this temple built in 1424 on the cremation site of his two elder brothers. After the brothers died together in a fight over the throne while riding elephants, their younger brother became king and established a place to honour them.

experiences.title: The prang and hall foundations on an east–west axis
paragraphs: A gallery surrounds the main prang. The wihan is to the east and the ubosot to the west behind it, arranged along the same axis. The direction of the surviving floors and walls helps you read how the central tower and ceremonial spaces connected.

The Fine Arts Department explains that early Ayutthaya murals influenced by Chinese art remain in a chamber within the tower. The paintings depict past Buddhas, reflecting cultural exchange in royal temple art. **The areas actually open to visitors inside the tower depend on on-site access controls.**

experiences.title: Royal gold objects excavated after looting
paragraphs: After looting in 1956, the Fine Arts Department excavated the tower chamber and found valuable objects, including royal gold artifacts and several Buddha images. These excavated objects are kept at Chao Sam Phraya National Museum.

At the ruins, see the tower and temple grounds where objects were enshrined; at the museum, explore the royal gold pieces and Buddha images found there. The excavated objects are not all exhibited inside the tower, so allow separate time and travel for a museum visit if you want to see the craftsmanship.

wat-lokayasutharam.thai: วัดโลกยสุธาราม
wat-lokayasutharam.type: Outdoor reclining Buddha ruins in Ayutthaya
wat-lokayasutharam.title: Wat Lokayasutharam: Outdoor Reclining Buddha in Ayutthaya | ThaiLiveNow
wat-lokayasutharam.description: Wat Lokayasutharam is a ruin in Ayutthaya where you can see a large reclining Buddha outdoors. Unlike the indoor reclining Buddha at Bangkok’s Wat Pho, the sky and surrounding grounds remain in view.
intro: At Wat Lokayasutharam, a large reclining Buddha lies beneath the open sky, without a hall roof. This Ayutthaya ruin offers a view of the image’s face and long body outdoors, a different setting from the indoor reclining Buddha at Wat Pho in Bangkok.

After looking closely at the Buddha’s expression and taking photos, walk around the remains of the old temple. Foundations of large buildings, galleries and a prang remain and give you a sense of the temple that once enshrined the image. As this is an outdoor visit, prepare for sun or rain so you can explore the reclining Buddha and ruins at a relaxed pace.

experiences.title: A Buddha image beneath the open sky
paragraphs: The reclining Buddha is made of brick covered with plaster. A lotus-shaped support rests beneath the head, whose expression is serene. Look closely at the face and hands, then step back to see the full length of the body and appreciate both its details and scale.

There is no complete hall remaining, so the sky and surrounding grounds form the background to the image. Unlike visiting a long Buddha image beneath a roof, you experience the light and weather of an outdoor setting too.

experiences.title: Remains of the old temple around the reclining Buddha
paragraphs: The site is also known as Wat Pha Non, or the temple of the reclining Buddha. The provincial government explains that Ayutthaya chronicles mention King Borommakot travelling to pay respects to the image. The temple grounds are near the old palace and Wat Phra Si Sanphet.

Large building and gallery remains, as well as the main prang, are still on the grounds. After seeing the reclining Buddha, look along the direction of the building foundations and former gallery. What may look like empty ground today was once a large temple with multiple buildings.

experiences.title: The present appearance after restoration in 1956
paragraphs: The reclining Buddha was restored in 1956 and remains in its present form. After looking at the face and long body, explore the traces of old buildings around it. The restored image and the surrounding structures left in ruins can be seen at the same site.

Look back and forth between the complete outline of the Buddha and the collapsed architecture around it to see what remains and what has disappeared. Visitors interested in history and archaeology can take a photo of the Buddha and then explore the temple grounds at a slower pace.

wat-yai-chai-mongkhon.type: Ayutthaya temple with a large chedi and Buddha images
wat-yai-chai-mongkhon.title: Wat Yai Chai Mongkhon: Large Chedi and Buddha Images in Ayutthaya | ThaiLiveNow
wat-yai-chai-mongkhon.description: Wat Yai Chai Mongkhon is a temple in Ayutthaya with a large chedi and Buddha images around the grounds. Unlike sites where only brick ruins remain, worship still takes place here alongside the historic architecture.
intro: At Wat Yai Chai Mongkhon, the large chedi visible from a distance and Buddha images across the grounds make a striking combination. See the scale of the brick tower and worshippers in the hall to experience both the history of the old capital and present-day religious practice.

Explore the chedi and surrounding Buddha images, and learn about King Naresuan’s victory. Monks practised at this temple even before the large chedi was built. People still pray in the halls today, so take time to appreciate both Ayutthaya’s old architecture and the quiet scene of worship.

experiences.title: A monastery founded in 1357
paragraphs: The temple is listed as having been founded in 1357 by King U-Thong, who established Ayutthaya. It is said to have been a place for meditation by monks who had studied in Sri Lanka. The temple is also known by the name Wat Phra Chao Phraya Thai.

It is interesting that monks practised here before the present large chedi was built. As you explore the tower and surrounding halls, picture the beginnings of a long-standing monastery alongside the history of the royal capital.

experiences.title: A chedi commemorating King Naresuan’s victory
paragraphs: The large chedi is known as a memorial to King Naresuan’s victory over the Burmese army in 1592. A story tells of a duel fought on elephants. The temple itself was founded earlier, so the large chedi commemorating the victory was added to an older place of meditation.

First look up at the towering chedi from a distance, then approach it to see the Buddha images around it. Take a photo of the whole tower, then walk among the images and look closely at their faces and postures. You can see both the scale of the chedi and the many Buddha images.

experiences.title: A temple where people still come to pray
paragraphs: People visit these grounds both to see the old architecture and to worship. Follow on-site guidance about footwear and visitor routes when exploring the religious spaces. Please leave room for worshippers praying before the Buddha images and look around quietly.

Use the chedi steps and interior only in sections **that are open on the day**. Even when you cannot climb to the top, you can look at the whole tower from outside and see the surrounding Buddha images. Follow on-site access guidance and explore at a comfortable pace.

wat-phanan-choeng.thai: วัดพนัญเชิง
wat-phanan-choeng.type: Ayutthaya temple housing a large golden seated Buddha
wat-phanan-choeng.title: Wat Phanan Choeng: Luang Pho To Buddha and Temple Visit | ThaiLiveNow
wat-phanan-choeng.description: Wat Phanan Choeng is an Ayutthaya temple housing a large golden seated Buddha about 19 m tall. Unlike visits to ruined brick temple grounds, the focus here is the hall enshrining the image.
intro: Enter the hall at Wat Phanan Choeng and a large golden seated Buddha, about 19 m tall, fills the space. The temple predates Ayutthaya’s time as a capital, and you can see Chinese-influenced decoration as well as worship that continues today.

Wat Phanan Choeng adds a living place of worship to a tour of Ayutthaya’s old ruins. Alongside the large Buddha known as Luang Pho To, there are other Buddha images and a hall housing Guanyin. After seeing the large image, take time to explore the different worship spaces inside and around the halls.

experiences.title: The large seated Buddha known as Luang Pho To and Sam Po Kong
paragraphs: The golden seated Buddha, about 19 m tall, is called Phra Phuttha Trairattana Nayok, or Luang Pho To. Among Chinese devotees, it is also known as Sam Po Kong. The large image seen from inside the hall and the Chinese-influenced decoration around it are striking together.

An offering ceremony, in which devotees drape cloth over the Buddha image, is another feature of the temple. If you see the ceremony taking place, quietly move aside from the route used by worshippers. It is not a scheduled performance for tourists, so do not plan your visit on the assumption that you will always see it.

experiences.title: A temple that predates Ayutthaya’s time as a capital
paragraphs: Wat Phanan Choeng was built in 1324, before Ayutthaya became the capital. The area also has a long history of Chinese residents. At a temple visited by both Thai and Chinese devotees, you can see Chinese-influenced decoration and worship traditions too.

experiences.title: Other Buddha images and worship spaces in the main hall
paragraphs: The main hall enshrines other Buddha images as well as the large seated one, including gold images, plaster-covered images and a copper-alloy image. After admiring the golden Buddha, look at the other images in turn. You can see statues made from different materials together.

There is also a shrine to Soi Dok Mak and a shrine to Guanyin on the grounds. Visitors interested in religious art can see several Buddhist and Chinese devotional figures in one temple. Please explore quietly without blocking people praying in the halls.

wat-umong.description: Wat Umong is a temple in the Suthep area of Chiang Mai, with tunnels and a chedi surrounded by trees. Its forest setting is different from the ornate halls of the Old City.
intro: At Wat Umong in Chiang Mai, old tunnels run beneath a chedi surrounded by trees. “Umong” means tunnel. The passageways, built for monks to meditate, and the forest grounds remain distinctive features of the temple.

Wat Umong in the Suthep area is known for the setting where the forest meets old architecture, rather than ornate halls. It is separate from the temple of the same name in the Old City, so look for Wat Umong Suan Phutthatham on the map. General sightseeing and joining a meditation program are separate activities.

experiences.title: Four tunnel entrances and meditation
paragraphs: The tunnels are said to have been built for monks to meditate. The Tourism Authority describes a 14th-century king commissioning a tunnel with four entrances. Enter one of the passages open to visitors to experience the brick interior, a different setting from the forest outside.
After seeing the tunnels, look at the chedi above them. Follow on-site guidance distinguishing spaces for meditation from paths open to visitors, and walk slowly along the routes that are open.

experiences.title: A forest history connected with monks from Sri Lanka
paragraphs: A story says that around the time King Mangrai, the first king of Lanna, founded Chiang Mai, he donated a bamboo forest so monks from Sri Lanka could practise there. The temple’s architecture is also described as reflecting Sri Lankan styles.

The forest was set aside for monks to practise away from the city. After seeing the chedi and tunnels, take a slow walk among the trees. The historic architecture and forest make a place to pause and enjoy scenery different from the ornate temples in the Old City.

experiences.title: Buddhist teachings among the trees
paragraphs: Signs around the grounds share Buddhist teachings from Panyananda Bhikkhu, who served as abbot from 1949 to 1966. Look for the signs as you walk among the trees after seeing the chedi and tunnels. The temple invites a leisurely visit among architecture and writing scattered through the forest.
If you want to join a meditation program, ask separately about the schedule and language. Please keep your voice down near areas where practitioners stay, even during a general visit.

wat-pha-lat.description: Wat Pha Lat is a forest temple on the road from Chiang Mai to Doi Suthep. Halls and chedis sit among trees and small streams, creating a mountain setting unlike city temples.
intro: Wat Pha Lat is a forest temple on the route from Chiang Mai up to Doi Suthep. Chedis and halls sit among small waterfalls, streams and trees, bringing together mountain scenery and temple architecture.

This is a different temple from the golden chedi at the summit of Doi Suthep, so allow travel time between the two if you plan to visit both. Driving to the temple and walking the Monk’s Trail are different routes. If you want to hike, check the trail condition and starting point separately. Even without hiking, you can enjoy the quiet mountain scenery of streams, trees and halls within the temple grounds.

experiences.title: A legend about the white elephant’s journey
paragraphs: A legend says that a white elephant carrying a Buddha relic to Doi Suthep slipped here. The Tourism Authority explains that the name Pha Lat comes from a Chiang Mai expression meaning “slip.” The temple is described as a site with about 600 years of history, dating to around the time of Wat Phra That Doi Suthep.

A well in the grounds is said to have been made when the elephant procession carrying the relic stopped to rest. Knowing the stories connected with the well and the temple’s name may help you picture the procession pausing in the forest on its way up the mountain. Treat the legend as a legend, distinct from documented history.

experiences.title: Chedis among waterfalls and trees
paragraphs: Small waterfalls and streams pass through the grounds, with halls and chedis beside them. Rather than a visit focused on the interior of one building, it is a place to walk through a setting where nature and religious architecture meet. Look back and forth between the chedis and buildings visible among the trees.

The chedi also reflects Burmese and Mon influences added during later restoration. As a resting place on the way to Doi Suthep, the temple is also worth seeing as a place of worship and architecture shaped by different periods.

experiences.title: Choose between a temple visit and a forest hike
paragraphs: The temple is partway along the road up to Doi Suthep, so it can be included in an itinerary to visit both temples. However, the two are not adjoining halls in the same compound. Allow separate time to see the temple and travel to the next site.

If you want to hike the Monk’s Trail, find the forest trail entrance separately from driving directions to the temple. In particular, check trail conditions and access information on site when it has been raining. You do not need to hike to enjoy the scenery where water, trees and architecture meet within the temple grounds.

wat-huai-pla-kang.title: Wat Huai Pla Kang: Guanyin Statue and Nine-Storey Pagoda | ThaiLiveNow
wat-huai-pla-kang.description: Wat Huai Pla Kang is a temple complex on a hill in Chiang Rai’s Rim Kok area. Its large Guanyin image and multi-storey pagoda are among the main sights.
intro: Wat Huai Pla Kang is a temple complex on a hill in Chiang Rai’s Rim Kok area, where you can see a large white Guanyin image and a multi-tiered pagoda together. It is easy to mistake the white image for a Buddha, but the site’s signature statue is Guanyin.

A large Guanyin image, a nine-storey pagoda with a red roof and a white hall stand together at Wat Huai Pla Kang. Rather than seeing only the Guanyin, also look at the pagoda’s Chinese and Lanna styles and the plaster decoration on the hall. One visit brings together different colours and forms of religious art.

experiences.title: A large white Guanyin image on the hill
paragraphs: The large white Guanyin image on the hill is listed by the provincial tourism information as 69 m tall. A multi-storey pagoda and white hall also stand near the image. First view the whole statue from a distance, then explore the pagoda and hall. The grounds bring together religious buildings in different sizes and colours.

From farther away, view Guanyin with the hill; up close, look at the form across its white surface. To enter the statue, check which areas are open and what tickets are available on site. Conditions for exploring the outside grounds and using the lift inside the Guanyin image may differ.

experiences.title: A nine-storey pagoda with a red roof and dragon guardians
paragraphs: Phop Chok Tham Chedi is a nine-storey pagoda combining Chinese and Lanna styles. Its red roof and rising tiers contrast with the white Guanyin image. Long dragon sculptures run along both sides of the stairway, making the approach to the pagoda a highlight too.

The pagoda houses several Buddha and sacred images, including a large Guanyin carved from fragrant wood. After seeing the monumental white image outdoors, look at the wooden Guanyin inside the pagoda. The two images portray Guanyin in different materials. Smaller pagodas associated with the year of birth are also around the main pagoda.

experiences.title: Decorative details on the white hall and visiting the hillside temple
paragraphs: The white hall has finely detailed plaster decoration. After seeing the red-roofed pagoda, look closely at the small patterns on the surface of the white hall. Within the same grounds, you can compare the pagoda’s stacked red tiers with the hall’s delicate decoration.

The local administrative organization says that the route up the nine-storey pagoda includes narrow, steep sections. If anyone in your group finds stairs difficult, begin by seeing the exterior buildings rather than pushing to climb the levels. Follow on-site information about which areas are open and how to move around inside.

paragraphs: For all visitors, we recommend wearing clothing that **covers the shoulders and knees**. A sleeved top with long trousers or a skirt that covers the knees is a good choice. Please dress modestly rather than wearing a sleeveless top or short bottoms.

wat-phra-yai-samui.title: Wat Phra Yai Koh Samui: Big Buddha Temple on Ko Fan Island | ThaiLiveNow
wat-phra-yai-samui.description: Wat Phra Yai is Koh Samui’s Big Buddha temple on Ko Fan, a small island off the northeast coast. A stone causeway connects the island to the main island, and a golden seated Buddha is its landmark. This is separate from Phuket’s Big Buddha.
intro: Wat Phra Yai on Koh Samui is a Big Buddha temple on the small island of Ko Fan. The visit includes crossing a stone causeway from the main island to see the large golden image. This is a site in northeast Koh Samui, distinct from Phuket’s Big Buddha.

If you want to add a temple visit to a beach day, follow the stone causeway to Ko Fan. To distinguish it from Phuket’s Big Buddha on the map, search for Wat Phra Yai, Koh Samui. See how the small island connects to the main island and take a closer look at the golden Buddha seated above it.

experiences.title: A golden seated Buddha created in 1972
paragraphs: The Koh Samui municipal office says the large golden Buddha was created in 1972. It is also known as Phra Phuttha Kodom and sits in the Mara-subduing posture, with one hand touching the ground. This is an image at a temple where people still worship, not an ancient ruin.

Look closely at the face and seated posture near the image, then step back to see the golden Buddha and temple together. After enjoying the sea at the beach, stop here to see the large seated Buddha and quietly observe worshippers praying.

experiences.title: From a wooden bridge to a stone causeway
paragraphs: Ko Fan was originally a small island surrounded by seawater. The municipal office explains that the first wooden bridge built by residents lasted only about 2–3 years, after which people worked together to build a permanent causeway from stone. The route you take into the temple reflects the work of local residents.

As you enter the temple, notice how the stone causeway connects Ko Fan to the main island of Koh Samui. The path built by residents leads across the water to the Buddha image on the small island. You can take in the shape of the once-water-surrounded island and the temple together.

experiences.title: A place of worship in northeast Koh Samui
paragraphs: The temple is on Ko Fan, near Bophut Beach in the north of Koh Samui. You can also visit Wat Plai Laem in the same part of the island, but they are separate sites. Visit each temple individually to see the golden seated Buddha here and the pond and Guanyin image at the other temple.

Travellers who come to see the large Buddha share the site with worshippers. Please be considerate when taking photos of people praying. Ask in advance about whether stairways and alternate routes are accessible, and follow on-site information about the areas open on the day.

wat-plai-laem.description: Wat Plai Laem in northeast Koh Samui brings together a pond and large religious sculptures. Its Guanyin, smiling figure and halls look different from the Big Buddha temple, known for its single golden seated image.
intro: At Wat Plai Laem, a white Guanyin image, a large smiling figure and temple halls come together around a pond. This temple in northeast Koh Samui offers the experience of viewing figures above the water from a distance and then crossing a bridge to get closer.

See the white Guanyin and smiling figure individually, then visit the hall by the water. The Koh Samui municipal office identifies the smiling figure as Phra Sangkatchai. If you also visit the nearby Big Buddha temple, allow time for each site. At Wat Plai Laem, take in the pond and its sculptures; at the Big Buddha temple, see the golden seated Buddha.

experiences.title: The white Guanyin image in the middle of the pond
paragraphs: The white Guanyin image stands in the middle of a pond. The municipal office lists it as about 20 m tall. Its many outstretched arms and position over the water make it a landmark visible from a distance.

Cross stone and marble bridges to get closer to the image. First take in the view of the statue and pond together, then look at its face and the decorative details around the arms from nearby. Follow routes open to visitors in the temple.

experiences.title: The smiling figure and its meaning of happiness
paragraphs: The Koh Samui municipal office identifies the large smiling figure as Phra Sangkatchai (พระสังกัจจายน์). Its description presents the image as a source of love and happiness. Its rounded form and expression differ from the long, outstretched arms of the white Guanyin.

Look closely at the Guanyin’s outstretched arms and the smiling figure’s rounded face, then view both sculptures and the halls from across the pond. The different expressions, colours and waterside architecture make for a leisurely visit and photographs.

experiences.title: A temple founded in 1880 and halls beside the water
paragraphs: Wat Laem Suwannaram is also used as the temple’s full name. The municipal office says the temple was founded in 1880. That date does not mean that the present large Guanyin image or every building was made then.

The temple is beside Route 4171, a main road in the northeast of the island, between the Big Buddha temple and Choeng Mon Beach. Follow the pond around to see the sculptures and halls in turn. As you cross bridges and pass the water, be considerate of worshippers and take your time.

phra-pathom-chedi.type: Temple centred on a large bell-shaped chedi in Nakhon Pathom
phra-pathom-chedi.title: Phra Pathom Chedi: Nakhon Pathom’s Great Bell-Shaped Stupa | ThaiLiveNow
phra-pathom-chedi.description: Phra Pathom Chedi is a temple centred on a large bell-shaped stupa in Nakhon Pathom. See its outline from a distance, then explore the galleries and standing Buddha to the north up close.
intro: Phra Pathom Chedi is a temple in Nakhon Pathom centred on a huge bell-shaped chedi. About 120 m high, the stupa is visible from a distance; nearby, you can walk through the gallery, see the northern standing Buddha and observe worshippers at the temple.

If you travel from Bangkok by train, plan the walk from the station and the return train in advance. Once you reach the chedi, walk along the galleries to see it from different angles, and visit the standing Buddha to the north. Take your time exploring the large stupa, other Buddha images and the local worship scene.

experiences.title: A bell-shaped chedi visible across the city
paragraphs: A tall spire rises above the large bell-shaped body, the temple’s signature form. The Tourism Authority lists the height as 120.45 m. Its outline from far away differs from its scale when viewed from below, so the approach to the stupa is part of the experience.

The temple preserves an old story of Buddhism’s arrival in the region, and the chedi underwent several restorations during the reigns of Rama IV and Rama V. The large structure seen today brings together a long religious history and later royal restoration work.

experiences.title: The northern standing Buddha and temple galleries
paragraphs: To the north is the standing Phra Ruang Rojanarit, built during the reign of Rama VI. After seeing the large chedi, visit the area enshrining the Buddha image as well. Walk along the galleries and see the Buddha image to explore further into the temple where worshippers gather.

You can also see Buddha images in Dvaravati style on the grounds. A portion of King Rama VI’s ashes is said to be enshrined here as well. Spend time exploring the galleries and Buddha images after viewing the great chedi to see Buddhist art from different periods and learn about royal restoration of the stupa.

experiences.title: Annual festival and local food
paragraphs: The Phra Pathom Chedi festival, held according to the lunar calendar, is described as bringing worshippers, local food and products, and a market in front of the temple. It is an event that connects temple worship with local food and shopping.

If you want to visit for the festival, check the **actual dates for the year you plan to go**. As it follows the lunar calendar, the dates on the Gregorian calendar vary each year. On an ordinary day, explore the temple at a relaxed pace; during the festival, you can also enjoy local food and products at the market in front of the temple.

wat-phra-mahathat-nakhon-si-thammarat.description: Wat Phra Mahathat in Nakhon Si Thammarat is a southern Thai temple centred on a large Buddha relic chedi with a golden spire. It remains an important place of local worship and religious tradition, distinct from the Ayutthaya ruins of a similar name.
intro: Wat Phra Mahathat in Nakhon Si Thammarat is a southern Thai temple centred on a large Buddha relic chedi with a golden spire. Religious and architectural traditions brought along maritime routes meet here, and the temple has continued as an important centre of Buddhism in the south.

The temple is associated with an annual ceremony in which cloth is draped around the chedi, the Nora dance drama and local chronicle traditions. If you want to visit for an event, check the schedule for that year first. Search specifically for the Nakhon Si Thammarat temple to distinguish it from the similarly named Ayutthaya ruins, and experience a major relic chedi alongside southern Thailand’s continuing worship traditions.

experiences.title: A large Buddha relic chedi with a golden spire
paragraphs: The large Buddha relic chedi is the temple’s signature structure. Considered a sacred place enshrining relics beneath its golden spire, it is important to local residents and devotees from across southern Thailand.
Worshippers still pray in front of the relic chedi. When viewing the stupa or taking photos, please give worshippers room to pass and explore quietly.

experiences.title: Traditions that arrived along maritime routes
paragraphs: UNESCO explains that the temple dates to the 8th century and has continued as a regional centre of Buddhism. Religious and architectural traditions from northeastern India, Java, Sri Lanka and the Mon region of southern Myanmar arrived through trade networks between the Pacific and Indian oceans.

Influences of Brahmanism, Hinduism and Mahayana and Theravada Buddhism are reflected in the temple’s buildings, ceremonies and culture. As you explore the chedi and surrounding buildings, consider how different religious and architectural traditions arrived by sea. The southern temple also offers a glimpse into this history of regional exchange.

experiences.title: The cloth-wrapping ceremony and World Heritage
paragraphs: The temple was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2026. The listing’s value includes living cultural practices such as the annual ceremony of wrapping cloth around the large relic chedi, Nakhon Si Thammarat’s chronicle traditions and the Nora dance drama.

If you want to see a related ceremony, check the event information for that year separately. World Heritage inscription does not mean every hall is open for sightseeing at all times. Follow on-site guidance and be considerate of worshippers wherever ceremonies or temple activities are taking place.

wat-phra-that-lampang-luang.description: Wat Phra That Lampang Luang is a Lanna temple in Ko Kha, Lampang. See its chedi, wooden halls and the decoration on its arched entrance. Search for it separately from temples in Lampang city.
intro: At Wat Phra That Lampang Luang in Ko Kha, Lampang, see a golden chedi and wooden halls at a Lanna temple. Walk through the arched entrance and look closely at the wooden halls and carvings. There are details to notice beyond the large chedi.

Take time to see the columns and doors of the Lanna wooden halls and the Buddhist art. Behind them is a space where an inverted image of the chedi appears. This is separate from temples in Lampang city, so look for Lampang Luang, Ko Kha on the map. The arched entrance, wooden halls and golden chedi let you see decoration in different materials together.

experiences.title: A golden Buddha relic chedi and an old northern temple
paragraphs: The Tourism Authority describes the temple as a site dating back to the 11th century and the Hariphunchai Kingdom. The chedi enshrines a Buddha relic, making this both a place to admire historic architecture and a temple that remains an object of worship.

After looking at the golden chedi, walk to the surrounding halls. The chedi and several religious buildings remain together, so you can explore the grounds at a relaxed pace, taking in the stupa’s surface and the wooden halls’ columns and roofs.

experiences.title: Lanna craftsmanship on the wooden halls and doors
paragraphs: The wooden Wihan Nam Taem is presented as a preserved example of Lanna architecture. Instead of bright marble or brick, look closely at the shapes of the wooden columns, roof and decorative details.

Also see the arched entrance, the hall enshrining Phra Chao Lan Thong and the intricate woodcarving. After viewing the golden chedi from a distance, look closely at the doors and wooden decoration. You can enjoy the large architecture and small-scale craftsmanship in turn.

experiences.title: An inverted image of the chedi
paragraphs: Inside Mondop Phra Phutthabat, behind the temple, there is a phenomenon where an image of the chedi appears inverted. You can see the stupa you viewed outside reflected inside the building.

If you want to see the inverted image, first check whether Mondop Phra Phutthabat is open that day. Access can differ between halls. Even on a day when that area is closed to visitors, you can explore the arched entrance, the wooden hall decorations and the golden chedi to see Lanna architecture.

wat-si-chum-sukhothai.description: Wat Si Chum in Sukhothai is a ruin where a large Phra Achana Buddha appears through a narrow opening between thick walls. It is northwest of the historical park’s city walls, so travel and ticket coverage differ from a visit to the central zone alone.
intro: At Wat Si Chum in Sukhothai, the face of a large Buddha image appears through a narrow opening between thick walls. Once inside, look up at the seated Phra Achana, about 15 m tall. The contrast between the narrow view from outside and the image’s scale inside is striking.

Wat Si Chum is northwest of the historical park’s city walls, so check travel routes and ticket coverage separately from the central zone. Search for Wat Si Chum, Sukhothai to distinguish it from the temple of the same name in Lampang. First see the face through the narrow entrance, then step inside to look up at the Buddha and take in its scale within the thick-walled building.

experiences.title: The Phra Achana seated Buddha beyond a narrow opening
paragraphs: Achana means “immovable” or “unchanging” in Pali. A large seated Buddha, about 15 m tall, fills the space enclosed by thick walls. Enter and look up at the serene face while reflecting on the meaning of its name.

From outside you first see the face through the gap in the wall; inside, the Buddha’s body appears along with the thickness of the walls around it. Look first from the entrance, then from up close at the statue. It is interesting to see how the architecture reveals the Buddha image.

experiences.title: A Bodhi grove in the name and thick-walled structure
paragraphs: The name Si Chum is said to derive from a Bodhi grove. The building housing the Buddha image has walls about 3 m thick, with a passage inside the left wall that runs behind the image towards the former roof. It is a structure with a separate path built within the solid outer walls.

The passage is described as having once contained images related to the Buddha. A legend says that someone inside the wall spoke as though the Buddha were speaking, giving the temple the nickname “the temple of the talking Buddha.” Understand this as a legend associated with the architecture.

experiences.title: Visit the open floor area instead of the passage
paragraphs: **The passage within the wall is closed to visitors according to the Tourism Authority.** Even if you know the old route exists, do not climb inside or try to go behind the Buddha. View the image and building from the areas open to visitors on the ground.

Wat Si Chum is in the historical park’s northern zone. If you have a central-zone ticket, check whether it includes this site before visiting. Even to see one additional Buddha image, you may need separate travel arrangements and admission coverage.

rules.title: Check the ticket for the northern zone
paragraphs: If you bought a ticket for the central zone, check whether **it includes the northern zone where Wat Si Chum is located**. If you plan to visit several ruins, choose a ticket after checking the zones it covers and its validity period.

rules.title: Do not enter the passage inside the walls
paragraphs: The passage inside the wall beside the Buddha is **closed to visitors** according to the Tourism Authority. Do not climb into it; use the areas open to visitors on site.

rules.title: Suggested clothing for a temple visit
paragraphs: For all visitors, we recommend wearing clothing that **covers the shoulders and knees**. A sleeved top with long trousers or a skirt that covers the knees is a good choice. Please dress modestly rather than wearing a sleeveless top or short bottoms.

experiences.title: An Isan zoo inspired by the African savanna
paragraphs: Nakhon Ratchasima Zoo has shaped flat land with gentle contours to create exhibits that resemble savanna grasslands. Featured animals include lions, leopards, African elephants, white rhinoceroses and African buffalo. You can also see giraffes, zebras and antelope, making it a place for families interested in observing African animals.

Visit animal exhibits while moving outdoors between areas. Look at how large giraffes are with children, then seek out lions or zebras in other areas. You can also spend more time in a particular section to see the animals you are most interested in.

experiences.title: Beyond the large animals, learn about crane conservation
paragraphs: Nakhon Ratchasima Zoo has also worked on breeding and conserving Thai sarus cranes. After seeing large animals such as lions and elephants, read the exhibit information to learn about crane conservation too.

The zoo’s work to conserve cranes does not mean every breeding or research area is open to visitors. Observe the animals and read the information in areas open to the public. Do not expect to see particular breeding animals or research activities in person.

experiences.title: Choose animal exhibits, programs and facilities separately
paragraphs: Alongside animal exhibits, Nakhon Ratchasima Zoo has also listed separate programs and facilities such as a water park. Families who want to focus on seeing animals and those who also plan to swim will need to allow different amounts of time and choose tickets accordingly.

The official price list separates admission for foreign visitors from vehicle charges for motorbikes, cars and buses. A basic ticket does not necessarily cover transport within the zoo, the water park or every program. Decide which facilities you plan to use and distinguish basic admission, add-on tickets and vehicle costs.

rules.title: Check whether separate facilities are included
paragraphs: Do not assume a basic ticket includes the water park, internal transport or every program. Decide which facilities you want to use and prepare separately for **basic admission, add-on tickets and vehicle charges**.

faq: Does admission to Nakhon Ratchasima Zoo include every program?

Admission, Animal Shows and vehicle charges are listed as separate items. Do not assume that one zoo admission ticket covers all programs and transport; check what is included for the activities you want.

From the skywalk, take in the wide animal exhibits and surrounding scenery together. You can enter only areas open on your visit date. Plan separately for round-trip transport from your accommodation and for getting between zones inside the zoo.

experiences.title: From giraffes and capybaras to giant anteaters
paragraphs: The zoo has featured giraffes, Asian elephants, capybaras, white lions and sun conures, among other animals. A 2025 government article also covered giant anteater breeding and conservation, including a male relocated from Khao Kheow Open Zoo. Families interested in more than large herbivores can choose exhibits with a variety of different-looking animals.

Veterinarians and animal-care staff look after the animals’ health and adaptation to the exhibits. An animal or offspring mentioned in an older feature may not be visible in the same location on your visit date. Explore the areas open that day and read the exhibit information alongside observing the animals.

experiences.title: Feeding experiences, seal programs and water play are separate options
paragraphs: Khon Kaen Zoo has publicized feeding activities, seal programs and a water park, among other experiences. It combines areas for wildlife conservation and research with exhibits for families, but not every facility and activity is bundled with one basic admission ticket.

A past free-admission event on a public holiday or water-park promotion had specific dates and eligibility. First decide whether you want to focus on seeing animals or include water play, then check the facilities included in tickets sold for your visit date and any separate conditions for internal transport.

rules.title: Do not treat a past promotion as a current offer
paragraphs: The free water-park promotion in April 2025 was time-limited. If you want to swim, check **operations and the facilities included in tickets for your visit date** separately.

experiences.title: A jungle park that preserves Dong Phu Wuan forest
paragraphs: Ubon Ratchathani Zoo is designed as a jungle park, with animal exhibits arranged while preserving the trees and vegetation of Dong Phu Wuan National Forest. Rather than a series of animal enclosures in isolation, it is a place to move between exhibit areas in a continuous forest setting.

Families interested in animals and plants can spend time at exhibits they like and look at the trees and forest on the paths to the next area. Observe animals and read exhibit information in an environment that preserves the Dong Phu Wuan forest.

experiences.title: Giraffes, ostriches and Kaki the pygmy hippo
paragraphs: A 2025 government feature presented giraffes, ostriches and Kaki the pygmy hippo as featured animals at Ubon Ratchathani Zoo. Kaki was also used in an animal-themed design for a local festival celebrating its 12th anniversary, and was presented as a recognisable animal at the zoo.

After seeing the long-necked giraffes and ostriches, look for the smaller pygmy hippo too. It can be fun to compare how each animal looks with children. An animal featured in a past article may not always be visible in the same place, and what you see can vary depending on exhibits and rest periods.

paragraphs: Ubon Ratchathani Zoo has also held illuminated candle displays connected with the local candle festival. experiences.title: Malayan tapirs, mouse deer and giraffes in a southern zoo
paragraphs: Songkhla Zoo is described as the first zoo in southern Thailand, with development beginning in 1989. It has extensive outdoor grounds in Khao Rup Chang and exhibits a range of animals, including Malayan tapirs, mouse deer, giraffes, bears, tigers and monkeys.

You can see Thai wildlife alongside animals from other regions. Spend time watching the animals that interest your child and reading about their appearance and behaviour. The visit is more engaging when you read the information about animals of the tropical rainforest and large mammals too.

experiences.title: Explore bird exhibits and southern scenery
paragraphs: The zoo also features birds such as parrots, macaws, cassowaries and flamingos. After seeing large mammals, compare the colours and shapes of the birds. Take your time in this area to watch how they walk and move their wings.

As you move between outdoor exhibit areas, you can also take in the scenery around Songkhla. If you plan to watch a program, allow time to get to its venue before it starts. Before and afterwards, you can watch animals in the exhibits that interest you at a relaxed pace.

experiences.title: Wildlife, penguin and tiger programs have different days off
paragraphs: Existing official information lists different closed days for programs: wildlife on Wednesdays, seals and penguins on Tuesdays, and tiger feeding on Mondays. Public holidays are exceptions, so a day when the zoo is open may not be a day when you can see the program you want.

Feeding programs are not activities where visitors can feed animals at their own discretion. Watch according to the day’s schedule and staff instructions. Songkhla Aquarium on the Laem Son On coast is a separate facility, so zoo tickets and transport arrangements do not apply there.

rules.title: Follow the day’s program schedule
paragraphs: Program sessions can change in addition to their weekly closed days. After entering, first check the **time and location of the programs you want to see that day**.

faq: Can I see all of Songkhla Zoo’s programs every day?

Programs have different weekly closed days. Wildlife programs are listed as closed on Wednesdays, seals and penguins on Tuesdays, and tiger feeding on Mondays, with public-holiday exceptions. Also check the day’s program time and location.

experiences.title: Observe small creatures in a rocky tide pool
paragraphs: The Bang Saen seawater aquarium presents Thai marine life by habitat. Its intertidal exhibit recreates pools left in the rocks between high and low tides, with small fish and creatures such as hermit crabs, sea urchins, sea anemones and starfish.

Rather than looking only for large swimming fish, enjoy searching around the rocks and at the bottom for smaller creatures. Tank labels include common and scientific names, so it is a good place to read and explore slowly with a child who is curious about what they have seen at the beach.

experiences.title: The colours of the reef and fish that hide among it
paragraphs: The coral reef area includes colourful fish such as clownfish and butterflyfish. Coral also provides a habitat where these animals can find food and hide. As you look at the fish’s colours, read about how they live around the reef.

An area covering unusual body shapes and venomous fish includes lionfish, moray eels, pufferfish and rays. Look at the shape of each animal in the tank and read its description. Even if a creature looks small or beautiful, do not touch it unless the tank is specifically designated for touch experiences.

experiences.title: Seahorses, food fish and the inhabitants of the large tank
paragraphs: Exhibits also cover fish used for food, such as groupers and sea bass, as well as ornamental fish. Look for seahorses and fish with unusual shapes and colours. It is a chance to see and read about species used as food and those kept for display in one place.

The Big Tank is a separate main exhibit for larger fish. Compare its scale with the smaller tanks earlier in the visit. If a diver-feeding program is running, you can also watch the animals and the diver’s movements together. Follow current information for session times.

experiences.title: An aquarium and marine museum at a university
paragraphs: The Burapha University Institute of Marine Science began as a marine animal museum and seawater aquaculture facility in 1969, opened as a centre in 1984 and became an institute in 1985. Its history of education and research is part of why it combines an aquarium with a museum about marine knowledge.

Closed-loop aquarium systems and tanks designed to resemble natural habitats underpin the exhibits. Separate from time spent at Bang Saen Beach, this is an indoor visit for families who want to see and read about small intertidal creatures through to larger fish.

faq: Is Bangsaen Aquarium a general aquarium?

It is an aquarium and marine museum at the Burapha University Institute of Marine Science. It is suited to a visit where you can learn about marine life by reading names and exhibit information alongside seeing the animals. It is also a university research and education facility.

experiences.title: Aquatic environments from rivers and mangroves to the sea
paragraphs: Waghor Aquarium is an ocean science and natural history education facility within King Mongkut Memorial Park of Science and Technology. It divides aquatic environments from mountain streams to the sea into six zones, covering freshwater, brackish water and marine ecosystems.

Exhibits feature mangroves, sandy and rocky shores, seagrass beds and coral reefs, showing how the same marine life depends on its habitat. Dolphins and dugongs also appear in model exhibits explaining ecology; this does not mean every animal described is kept alive at the aquarium.

experiences.title: View underwater at different levels in the large tank and tunnel
paragraphs: The Big Tank and glass tunnel are main visiting areas for seeing larger aquatic life. Look for animals moving near the surface, in mid-water and near the bottom. You can see that different species use different parts of the same tank.

In the tunnel, you can watch animals swimming overhead. Diver-feeding sessions are also offered; if you want to see one, go to the tank for a session on the day’s schedule. You can explore the exhibits at your own pace and also see a diver feed the aquatic life.

experiences.title: Explore specimens of shells, coral and starfish
paragraphs: The aquatic specimen area covers six groups: sponges; corals and sea fans; molluscs; crustaceans; sea urchins and starfish; and fish. Unlike watching living animals move in tanks, this exhibit lets you compare shapes and species at a slower pace.

If you or a child want to know the names of shells or starfish seen at the beach, read the descriptions beside the specimens. You can compare the shapes that may have been hard to notice while watching moving animals. Group tours for schools and organisations are listed as requiring an application 2 weeks in advance. This differs from a general visit, so apply early if you want a guided tour.

faq: Does Waghor Aquarium have a tunnel?

Yes. The large tank and glass tunnel are described as main visiting areas. You can also see exhibits about aquatic habitats from mountains and rivers to the sea, as well as aquatic specimens. Look for the aquarium as your destination within the science park.

intro: Nong Khai Aquarium is an exhibit at Khon Kaen University’s Nong Khai Campus, also known as the Sirindhorn Aquarium. It displays marine and freshwater fish, with an education and research focus on the Mekong River and regional freshwater species.

It is a good visit with a child who is curious about the differences between river fish and marine life. Although it belongs to Khon Kaen University, the site is in Nong Khai. Add it to a visit to the Mekong region to learn about underwater ecosystems.
facts: Khon Kaen University, Nong Khai Campus

experiences.title: A tunnel descending from upper-floor marine fish to freshwater fish below
paragraphs: Nong Khai Aquarium is also known as Sirindhorn Aquarium. Its 34 m tunnel is a sloping passage from the upper-floor marine fish area to the freshwater area below, connecting different environments, the sea and the river.

After seeing marine life, look for local freshwater fish on the lower floor. The aquarium is on Khon Kaen University’s Nong Khai Campus, but its address is in Nong Kom Ko, Nong Khai. Check its location on a map so you do not head to the zoo in Khon Kaen city or the university’s main campus instead.

experiences.title: See fish that live in the Mekong
paragraphs: The exhibits are arranged in nine groups and 18 systems. On the lower floor, local freshwater fish and Mekong species are presented in surroundings designed to resemble their natural habitats. The university also uses the aquarium for collecting Mekong fish and conducting fisheries education and research.

If you have enjoyed the views above the river along the Mekong, come here to see fish that live in it. Look at the tanks and read about animals that are harder to observe from the riverside. Marine exhibits are also present, so it is a good visit with a curious child who wants to compare river and sea fish.

experiences.title: Find the exhibition on campus
paragraphs: The aquarium’s contact number is **042-415-623**.

The aquarium is an exhibition facility at Khon Kaen University’s Nong Khai Campus. Its address is in Nong Kom Ko, Nong Khai. Check the aquarium building’s location on a map so you do not confuse it with the main campus in Khon Kaen or another facility.

faq: Is Nong Khai Aquarium in Khon Kaen?

No. Although it belongs to Khon Kaen University, the exhibit is in Nong Kom Ko on the university’s Nong Khai Campus. It is also known as Sirindhorn Aquarium, and its signature feature is a tunnel connecting marine fish exhibits upstairs with freshwater fish exhibits downstairs.

songkhla-aquarium.description: Songkhla Aquarium is the name of an aquarium building on the Laem Son On coast in Songkhla. It is a different location and facility from Songkhla Zoo.
intro: Songkhla Aquarium is on the Laem Son On coast in Songkhla. The facility has covered freshwater, brackish-water and marine exhibits, and is separate in both location and operator from Songkhla Zoo in Khao Rup Chang.

experiences.title: A former exhibit divided into freshwater, brackish water and marine life
paragraphs: Materials about the Songkhla area preserved by a public agency describe the aquarium as having three sections: freshwater, brackish water and seawater. Its freshwater section featured an environment inspired by a waterfall in southern Thailand and freshwater fish, while the brackish-water section covered mangrove plants and animals.
The marine section was described as having a large viewing window for groupers and leopard sharks. The layout moved from a freshwater waterfall and fish through mangroves to the sea.

experiences.title: Distinguish the Laem Son On coast from Songkhla Zoo
paragraphs: The aquarium building is known as a site on the Laem Son On coast, while Songkhla Zoo is a separate facility in Khao Rup Chang. They are in different locations and have different visitor arrangements, so zoo tickets and transport details do not apply to the aquarium.
The aquarium at Laem Son On and the zoo in Khao Rup Chang are separate places. When searching on a map, check the facility name and area together.

bueng-boraphet-aquarium.description: Bueng Boraphet Aquarium is an exhibit facility in the Bueng Boraphet lake visitor complex in Nakhon Sawan. See a freshwater fish tunnel and tanks in a separate building from the lake and visitor centre.
intro: Bueng Boraphet Aquarium is an exhibit facility in the Bueng Boraphet lake visitor complex in Nakhon Sawan. Its building has a freshwater fish tunnel and several tanks, a different visiting area from the lake itself or the visitor centre.

It suits visitors who want to see aquatic life as part of a trip around the lake. Check visitor information for the aquarium building separately rather than relying only on the opening hours of the wider complex.

experiences.title: From lakeside scenery into a freshwater fish tunnel
paragraphs: Bueng Boraphet Aquarium is inside the lake visitor complex in Nakhon Sawan. The building has several tanks and a 24 m freshwater fish tunnel. It suits visitors who want to look out over the lake and then see aquatic life up close.

The lake, visitor centre and aquarium are separate visiting areas. If you plan to visit the aquarium after a walk by the lake, set the aquarium building as your destination on the map. Inside, you can observe freshwater fish up close, unlike at the lakeshore.

experiences.title: Marine life and overseas species in tanks beyond the freshwater tunnel
paragraphs: In addition to the tunnel, the aquarium has more than 33 tanks. It also exhibits marine life and species from other countries, so not every fish on display lives in Bueng Boraphet Lake. After walking through the freshwater fish tunnel, explore the other tanks too.

After taking in the large underwater view in the tunnel, spend time reading about the animals in individual tanks. Exhibit species and open areas may change, so explore the displays available that day rather than expecting a particular fish to always be in the same tank.

experiences.title: The visitor complex and aquarium building have different hours
paragraphs: The name Bueng Boraphet is also used for the lake and wider visitor complex. The visitor centre has separately listed hours, so using those as the aquarium’s admission times may not match when the aquarium building is open.
If you plan to see both the lake and the tunnel, check your destination for driving and the aquarium admission information for that day, then decide the order of your visit.

faq: Is Bueng Boraphet Aquarium the same as visiting the whole lake?

It is an aquarium building inside the lake visitor complex. The operator describes a 24 m freshwater tunnel and several tanks. It is a separate visiting area from the lake and visitor centre, so check the aquarium’s admission information for the day separately.

damnoen-saduak-floating-market.name: Damnoen Saduak Floating Market
damnoen-saduak-floating-market.thai: ตลาดน้ำดำเนินสะดวก
damnoen-saduak-floating-market.title: Damnoen Saduak Floating Market: Morning Boats, Food and Boat Tours | ThaiLiveNow
damnoen-saduak-floating-market.description: Damnoen Saduak Floating Market in Ratchaburi is a morning market with boats on the canals and stalls selling food, fruit and souvenirs. It developed around cultural preservation and tourism, and is a trip outside central Bangkok.
intro: At Damnoen Saduak, boats carrying fruit and food share the canals with shops along the water in a morning floating market in Ratchaburi. It developed to preserve and introduce the culture and scene of waterborne trade to visitors. Unlike a market in central Bangkok, the boats on the canals are a large part of the experience.

Plan an early visit if you want to see fruit boats, noodles, seafood and souvenirs. A private boat is a separate product from walking around the market. Before choosing one, agree on the number of passengers, price per boat, route and any additional costs.

experiences.title: Canals busy with boats carrying fruit
paragraphs: Boats carrying fruit and food travel along the narrow canals, with shops lining the water. Look for fruit such as mangoes, coconuts and bananas, and take in the floating-market scene created by boats and stalls.

The sight of boats laden with goods moving through the narrow canals is one of Damnoen Saduak’s highlights. Visit in the morning to browse the waterside stalls, see boats selling fruit and food, and take photos of the market scene.

experiences.title: Noodles and fruit by the canal
paragraphs: Boats and shops beside the water sell noodles, seafood and fruit. If you want to have a meal at the market, look at the boats selling food as well as the surrounding shops before choosing what to eat.

Fruit orchards are found around the canals, and the market has fruit such as mangoes, coconuts and bananas. Rather than seeking out a particular variety or price, choose from what is available in stalls and boats that day.

experiences.title: Check the market and boat products separately
paragraphs: If you want to see the market in the early morning, consider arriving by around 9:00, as recommended by the Tourism Authority. A boat takes you through the inner canals to see the market. Boat services are a separate product, not included with entry to the market.

The Tourism Authority’s reference fare starts at about 500 baht per boat for 2–4 people and 30 minutes. Before boarding, confirm whether the total price is per person or per boat, how many people can ride, and where the route goes. Also check whether stops such as a coconut farm are included and whether there are additional costs.

rules.title: Agree on the boat’s total price and route first
paragraphs: Before boarding, agree on **whether the fare is per person or per boat, how many people are travelling and where the boat will go**. Visiting the market without a boat and taking a boat tour are separate options.

taling-chan-floating-market.description: Taling Chan Floating Market is a weekend market around the canal in front of the Taling Chan District Office in Bangkok. Explore dining rafts and land-based stalls, and choose a separate boat trip if you wish.
intro: Taling Chan Floating Market is a weekend market where dining rafts and land-based shops gather around the canal in front of the Taling Chan District Office in Bangkok. Alongside boats and meals by the water, you can see local fruit and vegetable growing and orchid cultivation, connecting the market to life in the west of Bangkok.

It is a good choice if you want seafood, boat noodles, som tam and Thai sweets. It is another floating market in west Bangkok, separate from Khlong Lat Mayom. Eating at the market and taking a canal boat trip are also separate activities, so choose the boarding point and route separately if you want to go by boat.

experiences.title: Dining rafts on the canal and market stalls on land
paragraphs: At Taling Chan, rafts moored by the water are used as dining areas, with shops continuing onto land nearby. You can walk around, choose something to eat and watch people dining by the water without taking a boat.

If you plan to visit Khlong Lat Mayom as well, explore the food and waterside areas at each market separately. At Taling Chan, the scene includes dining rafts in front of the district office and land-based stalls along the canal.

experiences.title: Seafood and Thai market food
paragraphs: Choose seafood, boat noodles or som tam for a meal. Afterwards, look for Thai sweets such as khanom krayasat or the crispy noodle dish mee krop mae lek. Enjoy a mix of spicy and savoury dishes with sweet snacks as you take a break by the water.

After choosing something to eat, sit in a waterside dining area and watch boats and visitors moving around the market. It is well suited to families and friends who want to combine food with a canal-side atmosphere.

experiences.title: Local produce and a separate canal tour
paragraphs: Fruit, vegetables and ornamental orchids are grown around the market. After sampling the food, browse local produce too. Walk between waterside stalls and dining areas to see how people shop and eat beside the canal.

If you want a longtail-boat canal tour, separately agree on the boarding point, return time, route and fare as part of your plan for a meal at the market. You can also enjoy Taling Chan’s atmosphere simply by eating by the water and walking around the market, without taking a boat.

bridge-over-river-kwai.description: The Bridge Over River Kwai is a railway bridge across the Kwai Yai River in Kanchanaburi. It connects the history of the Thailand–Burma Railway during the Second World War with wartime losses and postwar restoration.
intro: The Bridge Over River Kwai is a railway bridge crossing the Kwai Yai River in Kanchanaburi. It is a place to consider the history of the Thailand–Burma Railway during the Second World War, the wartime losses and the bridge’s postwar restoration.

If you know the name from the film The Bridge on the River Kwai, you can see the actual railway bridge on the riverfront in Kanchanaburi. Trains still use it. Viewing the bridge from the riverbank and taking a train are separate activities. On the bridge, follow train operations and railway staff instructions.

experiences.title: A real wartime heritage site, known to many through a film
paragraphs: You may know the name from the film The Bridge on the River Kwai. This is not a film set, but **an actual railway bridge used by the Thailand–Burma Railway to cross the Kwai Yai River during the Second World War**. See its steel arches over the river and consider the history of railway construction and wartime losses at the site.

The bridge was damaged during the war and restored in 1946. Not everything visible today is exactly as it was during the war. The bridge combines surviving arches with sections restored after the war.

experiences.title: See the railway bridge from the riverbank or travel by train
paragraphs: From the riverbank, you can see the whole railway bridge above the water, and walking across the bridge is also described as possible when access is permitted. The view of the steel structure from nearby differs from its long outline as seen from across the river.

If you also want to take a train, plan a railway trip separately from your visit to the bridge. The Tham Krasae section along the cliff is somewhere else. On the bridge, follow **train operations and railway staff instructions** first, and do not block the tracks to take photos.

rules.title: Follow on-site controls while on the railway
paragraphs: Follow **train operations and railway staff instructions** first. Do not occupy the tracks to photograph a train or move into an area where access is not permitted.

accessSections.title: Find the railway bridge in Kanchanaburi
paragraphs: The address is **Maenam Khwae Road, Tha Makham**. Search for The Bridge Over River Kwai, Kanchanaburi on your map. Distinguish a trip to the railway station from the riverside viewing area.
