khao-san-road.description: Khao San Road is a roughly 300 m street in Bangkok’s Old City lined with accommodation, restaurants, pubs and clubs. Once known as a backpacker base, it now also has hotels and boutiques. It suits visitors who want to browse a short stretch of shops or enjoy dinner and drinks with friends in the evening.
intro: Khao San Road is a roughly 300 m travel district in Bangkok’s Old City, with accommodation, travel agencies, restaurants, pubs and clubs. It grew from a backpacker lodging street into a place to find hotels, boutiques and international food. The atmosphere changes considerably between day and night along its short length.

It suits visitors who want to try Thai and international dishes, spend an evening with friends or experience the energy of a traveller district. Music can be loud at night, so it is a better fit if you are looking for food and nightlife than a quiet stroll.

experiences.title: From a backpacker street to a mix of places to stay and shop
paragraphs: Khao San Road once had a concentration of backpacker accommodation and travel agencies, with pubs, clubs, hotels and boutiques added over time. Today people visit not only to stay but also to eat, shop and enjoy the music at night.

If you plan to stay here, read the accommodation description to see whether it is a dormitory or a hotel room and whether it has air conditioning. Room types and facilities vary even along Khao San Road, so choose based on the conditions of the room you plan to book.

experiences.title: From pad Thai to food from around the world
paragraphs: Restaurants serve not only pad Thai and Thai egg dishes but also pizza, falafel, sushi and pasta. If members of your group want different things to eat, walk along the street and choose a restaurant together. You can find food from several countries along this short stretch.
Shops also sell graphic T-shirts, clothes, accessories, books and magazines. Have a meal and browse small items as you walk to experience the international traveller atmosphere of Khao San.

experiences.title: Shops by day and music at night
paragraphs: After sunset, music from pubs, clubs and restaurants grows louder, and the street becomes livelier. It suits an evening out with friends or a visit for nightlife, but the sound may feel overwhelming if you want a quiet conversation or a peaceful family stroll.

Not every shop stays open all day, and there is no single opening or closing time for the whole street. If you have a particular restaurant or club in mind, check its operating information separately.

accessSections.title: Find Khao San Road on a map

yaowarat-chinatown.name: Yaowarat · Bangkok Chinatown
yaowarat-chinatown.type: Neighbourhood of gold shops, Chinese temples and food lanes
yaowarat-chinatown.title: Yaowarat, Bangkok Chinatown: Food, Temples and Old Shophouses | ThaiLiveNow
yaowarat-chinatown.description: Yaowarat is the main street of Bangkok’s Chinatown, lined with red-and-gold gold-shop signs, Chinese temples and shrines, restaurants and grocery shops. It is a neighbourhood where you can see both long-standing commerce and worship traditions, not just look for food.
intro: Yaowarat is the commercial heart of Bangkok’s Chinatown, with gold shops bearing red-and-gold signs, Chinese temples and small shrines, restaurants and grocery stores. Seafood and Teochew-style food from southern China cluster along the main road, while nearby Wanit Road has wholesale shops selling clothes, shoes, toys and stationery, creating different market scenes.

Walk with someone who enjoys gold shops and temple architecture and wants to experience Chinese food culture. The main road, wholesale lanes and nearby streets such as Song Wat are distinct areas; choose the scenes you want to see rather than treating them all as one place.

experiences.title: Gold-shop signs and a historic commercial street
paragraphs: Along Yaowarat’s main road, gold-shop signs in red and gold catch the eye one after another. Gold jewellery shops and old shophouses line the street, so even if you are not shopping, you can take in Bangkok Chinatown’s commercial character as you walk.

Turn into the side streets to find temples associated with Mahayana Buddhism and Taoism, as well as small shrines. Local residents still come to burn incense and pray. As you browse the shops, you can also see worship traditions that continue at the temples and shrines.

experiences.title: Teochew food and seafood
paragraphs: Try steamed fish, crab and seafood dishes made with shrimp and squid. Browse restaurants serving Teochew-style food, and look for dried squid and shrimp in grocery shops. You can sample food from southern China while seeing where some of the ingredients are sold.

If you are walking to find a meal, look along the main road for restaurants and tea shops. If you want to see food ingredients, browse the shops in the side streets too. As not every shop keeps the same hours, choose places to visit based on what you are looking for.

experiences.title: Wanit Road’s wholesale lanes and nearby streets
paragraphs: Wanit Road has wholesale shops selling clothing, shoes, toys and stationery. The goods differ from the food businesses along Yaowarat’s main road, so even when shopping in Chinatown, what you see depends on which street you walk along.
If you extend your walk from Yaowarat to Song Wat or Talat Noi, you can move between different scenes, including food streets, old shophouses and residential alleys.

song-wat-road.description: Song Wat Road is a Bangkok street near Chinatown where you can explore historic architecture, cafes and restaurants. Different styles of eateries and shops line the old commercial street. It suits visitors who want to continue walking after Yaowarat to see buildings and cafes.
intro: Song Wat Road is a historic commercial street in Samphanthawong, Bangkok. Alongside shophouses more than 100 years old and long-established restaurants, cafes, galleries and craft shops run by younger owners have opened, putting old architecture and contemporary creative spaces side by side.

It suits anyone who wants to look at old building facades, try coffee or local desserts, and explore small shops on a longer walk through Chinatown. It is a separate street from Yaowarat’s food district, so set Song Wat Road as your destination on a map and take time to explore.

experiences.title: Walk past historic shophouses
paragraphs: Song Wat is within the old commercial area of Samphanthawong. Traditional shophouses remain along the road; some continue to operate as they did before, while others have become new shops and spaces. Visitors who enjoy architecture can find plenty to see simply by walking past the facades and through the side streets.

Look at old shophouses alongside the newer businesses that have opened inside them. The walk along Song Wat is appealing because the streetscape of an older commercial area meets today’s cafes and galleries.

experiences.title: Long-established restaurants and new cafes
paragraphs: Cafes and galleries run by younger owners sit among long-established restaurants and local dessert shops. After admiring the shophouse facades, stop for a break inside a restaurant or cafe. You can eat or have coffee inside an old building and take in the street.

experiences.title: Street art and local crafts
paragraphs: Song Wat has spaces where you can find street art, galleries, handicrafts and local products. It suits a walk to discover small exhibitions and shops in an old neighbourhood rather than shopping in a large commercial centre.

After looking at the building facades, stop at a gallery or craft shop that catches your eye. Old commercial streets and contemporary creative spaces stand side by side, making it a good area for people interested in both architecture and local culture.

talat-noi.name: Talat Noi
talat-noi.type: Riverside historic Chinese neighbourhood with alley art
talat-noi.title: Talat Noi Bangkok: Chinese Heritage, Street Art and Riverside Lanes | ThaiLiveNow
talat-noi.description: Talat Noi is a neighbourhood near the Chao Phraya River where you can see old Chinese homes, alley murals and cafes. It is around Wanit 2 and Charoen Krung 22. Despite “market” in the name, it is a place to explore on foot rather than a single indoor market building.
intro: Talat Noi is a neighbourhood of Chinese community lanes formed as trade expanded from Sampheng, near the Chao Phraya River. Old brick walls and shrines, murals of everyday life and festivals, and an orange Fiat are part of the alley scenery. Former rice mills and workshops have also found new uses as museums and cafes.

It suits visitors who want to take their time looking at murals and old houses, or explore the local history of Bangkok’s Chinese communities. Residents still live in the neighbourhood, so follow public lanes and places open to visitors, and do not enter private rooms or restricted areas.

experiences.title: Chinese community and traces of the workshop lanes
paragraphs: Talat Noi grew as trade expanded from the Sampheng wholesale area. Alleys around Wanit 2 and Charoen Krung 22 still have old homes, shops and shrines. At Rong Kueak Shrine by the river, you can glimpse a local community worship tradition.

A local museum shows traces of lathe workshops that made parts for ships, machinery and rice mills. After seeing old homes and shops in the lanes, visit the museum to learn more about the community and how people once made a living here.

experiences.title: Alleys with murals and an orange Fiat
paragraphs: Murals on the alley walls depict lion dances, festivals and community life. An orange Fiat parked beside an old brick wall is another well-known Talat Noi sight. Look at the mural scenes and take photos in an alley where an old wall and car appear together.

When taking photos, leave the path clear for residents. Rather than seeing only the mural and car, look around at old houses and shrines too. This helps you appreciate Talat Noi as a real neighbourhood, not only a photo backdrop.

experiences.title: See shrines and repurposed buildings
paragraphs: Chao Sue Kong Shrine, established in 1804, is a Hokkien-style shrine. By the river, Rong Kueak Shrine is connected with the Chinese merchant community. After visiting the shrines, walk around the nearby pier and its small garden and trees to see the riverside setting.

Cafes in old courtyard houses and the local museum are examples of historic buildings given new uses. Residents still live here, so follow lanes and spaces open to visitors rather than entering private rooms or restricted areas.

accessSections.title: Walk from Hua Lamphong station
paragraphs: The Tourism Authority lists **about a 15-minute walk from Hua Lamphong station on the MRT Blue Line**. Search for Talat Noi, Samphanthawong as your destination. Charoen Krung 22 and Wanit 2 are highlighted areas; the map marker indicates the neighbourhood.

charoen-krung.name: Charoen Krung
charoen-krung.thai: ถนนเจริญกรุง
charoen-krung.type: Area with an old commercial street and creative spaces
charoen-krung.title: Charoen Krung Bangkok: Historic Architecture, TCDC and Warehouse 30 | ThaiLiveNow
charoen-krung.description: Charoen Krung is a road and surrounding neighbourhood in Bangkok’s old riverside commercial district, now home to galleries, design spaces and cafes. Explore historic architecture and art around the Grand Postal Building and Warehouse 30 near Soi Charoen Krung 30. Choose specific places to visit rather than walking the entire long road.
intro: Charoen Krung is a Bangkok street where historic buildings in the old riverside commercial district sit alongside new creative spaces. Highlights cluster around the Grand Postal Building, home to the Thailand Creative & Design Center (TCDC), and Warehouse 30, which repurposes seven old warehouses on Charoen Krung 30.

Architecture and design enthusiasts can look at the scale of the Grand Postal Building and the structure of the warehouses, then explore bookstores, record shops, cafes and exhibition spaces inside. Rather than planning to walk the entire long road at once, choose places that are actually open to visitors.

experiences.title: The Grand Postal Building and TCDC
paragraphs: The large Grand Postal Building houses the Thailand Creative & Design Center, or TCDC. If you are interested in architecture and contemporary design, look at the building’s exterior and then explore the design centre inside. You can see how a building in an old riverside commercial area is being used today.

After seeing the Grand Postal Building’s exterior, explore nearby commercial buildings too. If you want to use an exhibit or facility inside, first check what is open on your visit date. Exhibits and available spaces may change over time.

experiences.title: Seven old warehouses repurposed as Warehouse 30
paragraphs: Warehouse 30 repurposes seven warehouses from the Second World War era as an arts community space. Inside the structures, which retain their roofs and warehouse character, you can find clothing and electronics, homeware, bicycles, books, flowers and record shops. Explore a variety of design goods in historic buildings.

Walk through the different buildings to find spaces such as a bookstore-style coffee spot, restaurants, cafes and shops arranged by area. It is a place to browse at a relaxed pace with someone who wants to combine shopping and architecture.

experiences.title: Cafes and art events in the warehouses
paragraphs: Some warehouses have restaurants, cafes and bars; others serve as multipurpose venues for events such as films and workshops. See how the old warehouses have found new uses for contemporary life and creativity.

On days when a film screening or workshop is taking place, you can watch a work or participate in the activity at a multipurpose venue. Plan around the date if there is a particular event you want to attend, then explore the shops and cafes in the warehouse afterwards or beforehand.

accessSections.title: Set the specific building you plan to visit as your destination
paragraphs: Charoen Krung is a long road, so choose the building you actually want to visit, such as the **Grand Postal Building** or **Warehouse 30**. Warehouse 30 is at 52–60 Soi Charoen Krung 30, Bang Rak. This is the address of one creative complex, not an entrance to all of Charoen Krung.

nimmanhaemin.title: Nimmanhaemin Chiang Mai: Cafes, Boutiques and Gallery Lanes | ThaiLiveNow
nimmanhaemin.description: Nimmanhaemin is a Chiang Mai neighbourhood for exploring cafes, boutiques and galleries along its side streets. Several sois branch off the roughly 1 km main road, with shops tucked between homes. It suits visitors looking for coffee and small shops in an atmosphere different from temple sightseeing.
intro: Nimmanhaemin is a Chiang Mai neighbourhood where cafes, galleries, boutiques and lifestyle shops line a main road and its network of sois. Shops are tucked between homes, so the atmosphere changes when you turn off the main road into an alley. You can also find locally made goods such as scented candles, natural-fibre paper and embroidered bags.

It suits friends who enjoy coffee and small shops, and travellers who want to relax at a neighbourhood cafe and look for gifts. One Nimman is a separate commercial complex within Nimmanhaemin, while boutiques and galleries are dotted across the sois, giving you more places to explore on foot.
facts: Main road about 1 km · surrounding sois included

experiences.title: A walk from the main road into the side streets
paragraphs: Nimmanhaemin’s main road is about 1 km long, with several sois branching off it. Rather than walking only along the main road, choose an alley with a cafe or shop that interests you to see how homes and businesses fit together in the neighbourhood.

In Soi 1, look for lifestyle goods, candles, natural-fibre paper and bags embroidered by hill-tribe communities. If these items interest you, turn into Soi 1 from the main road and browse the shops. You can also pause for a coffee while looking for a gift.

experiences.title: Small-shop finds and cafes
paragraphs: Browse homeware or fragrance products in a small boutique, stop at a cafe for a break and then walk to another soi. Look around the shops tucked between homes.

Visit a gallery, choose a gift at a design shop and then walk to a cafe in another soi. Rather than rushing through many shops on one street, spend time at places that interest you and explore the neighbourhood’s mix of cafes and stores at a relaxed pace.

experiences.title: A gallery cafe in Soi 17 and One Nimman
paragraphs: In Soi 17, SS1254372 is a gallery cafe by artist Torlarp Larpcharoensook. It serves seasonal fruit and vegetables, local coffee and tea, and breakfast, brunch and lunch. It is worth a visit if you want to see art and have a meal in a gallery cafe.

One Nimman is a separate commercial complex within Nimmanhaemin. It has shops selling regional products from around Thailand, spaces for young creators, restaurants and cafes, as well as pop-ups and art events. If you want to see an event, check the date separately; if you want to visit shops on the sois nearby, check each business’s opening hours.

accessSections.title: Getting to Nimmanhaemin in Chiang Mai
paragraphs: The area is in **Suthep, Mueang Chiang Mai**. The Tourism Authority lists a trip of about 15 minutes by car or songthaew from central Chiang Mai. If travelling by car, use Nimmanhaemin as the area and enter the specific cafe or shop you plan to visit as your destination.

phuket-old-town.name: Phuket Old Town
phuket-old-town.thai: ย่านเมืองเก่าภูเก็ต
phuket-old-town.type: Phuket historic district with shophouses and street art
phuket-old-town.title: Phuket Old Town: Sino-Portuguese Shophouses, Street Art and Local Food | ThaiLiveNow
phuket-old-town.description: Explore historic shophouses, street art and cafes in Phuket Old Town. Buildings along both sides of the streets preserve traces of a commercial city shaped by Chinese, European and other cultural influences. It suits visitors who want to combine architecture and local food between beach days.
intro: Phuket Old Town is a historic district where you can explore the shophouses, street art and food culture of Phuket Town, which prospered through the tin industry. The legacy of a Peranakan community shaped by Chinese, Malay and Thai cultures remains in Sino-Portuguese buildings, murals and old mansions; some buildings have found new uses as museums and cafes.

It suits visitors who want to learn about architecture and urban history between beach and resort scenery, or explore local Phuket food with friends. Try Hokkien noodles, dim sum, apong pancakes and khanom chin to combine a walk with a meal.

experiences.title: Tin trade and Sino-Portuguese shophouses
paragraphs: Phuket grew as a commercial city during the tin boom, and shophouses and mansions from that period remain along the streets of the Old Town. Peranakan history, shaped by Chinese migration and Malay and Thai cultures, is reflected in the building facades and street decorations, often described as Sino-Portuguese architecture.

Walk along the streets to see historic shophouses that combine shops and homes in one building. An architectural stroll suits visitors who want to explore Phuket’s urban history beyond its beach resorts.

experiences.title: Museums and street art
paragraphs: At the Thai Hua Museum on Krabi Road, you can learn about local history in a historic building. As you walk around the Old Town, you will also find buildings preserved as museums and others put to new uses as restaurants, cafes and accommodation.

After visiting the Thai Hua Museum, walk along streets lined with old shophouses and murals. Look for murals in the alleys and stop for photos, then take a break at a cafe that catches your eye to enjoy both architecture and street art.

experiences.title: Hokkien noodles and Phuket snacks
paragraphs: Look for Phuket dishes such as Hokkien stir-fried noodles, oh tao, lo ba and oh eaw. Have dim sum or dumplings in the morning, then choose Hokkien noodles or khanom chin curry noodles for a meal. Try apong pancakes as well to enjoy both Chinese-influenced and southern Thai food.

Rather than deciding in advance exactly which dish to eat first, explore the restaurants and snack shops you come across on your walk. Knowing a few local dish names makes it fun to experience Phuket Town’s food culture, which differs from the beach resorts.

bophut-fishermans-village.title: Bophut Fisherman’s Village: Historic Shops, Crafts and Seaside Dining | ThaiLiveNow
bophut-fishermans-village.description: Bophut Fisherman’s Village is a street in northern Koh Samui where you can see old fishing-village homes, shops and restaurants. It is suited to an evening of architecture and souvenir browsing, distinct from swimming at the beach.
intro: Bophut Fisherman’s Village is a street of old fishing-village homes along the north coast of Koh Samui, now used as shops, accommodation and restaurants. Walk past Chinese-style wooden shophouses and traces of coastal life, then have dinner at a restaurant overlooking the sea.
Browse handmade soaps, wooden decorations, pottery and bags with friends or family who enjoy crafts. After walking through the village shops, enjoy a seafood dinner overlooking the water.

experiences.title: Old fishing-village homes and Chinese-style shophouses
paragraphs: The old fishing village in northern Bophut has homes of Chinese residents and wooden shophouses. Homes along the road have become shops, accommodation, restaurants and travel agencies, bringing the village’s past and present-day visitor businesses together on one street.

Walk past old wooden buildings and through lanes lined with shops. If you plan to shop and have dinner in the village, set the commercial street as your destination rather than only the sandy beach. You can combine it with a beach walk, but distinguish the area for swimming from the street of shops on a map.

experiences.title: Hand-carved soaps and small souvenirs
paragraphs: Shops display hand-carved soaps, wooden ornaments, pottery, bags, jewellery and clothing. If you enjoy crafts, look closely at the carved shapes and materials to choose a small gift.

experiences.title: An evening by the sea
paragraphs: Restaurants in Bophut serve seafood and dishes from several countries. It suits an itinerary where you take a walk on the beach and then have dinner, or browse the village shops and finish with a meal.

accessSections.title: Distinguish Bophut Beach from Fisherman’s Village
paragraphs: Search for **Fisherman’s Village Bophut, Koh Samui** on a map and check the marked location. Choose where to go based on whether you want to spend time at the beach or visit the village shops and restaurants.
